Once your footing settles, even a violent impact becomes something you can redirect rather than endure.

entries.name: Grounded
entries: You have Advantage on ability checks and saving throws you make to resist being Grappled, Shoved, knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}, moved against your will, or disarmed.

entries.name: Absorb the Impact
entries: When you take Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage from an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the damage by {@dice 1d6} + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
If this reduces the damage to 0, you can immediately move 5 feet without provoking {@variantrule {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}|XPHB|{@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}s}.
You can use Absorb the Impact a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Braced Position
entries: If you end your turn having moved no more than 10 feet since the start of that turn, you become Braced until the start of your next turn.

While Braced, you can't be moved against your will unless you are {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, standing from {@condition Prone|XPHB} costs only 5 feet of movement, and you count as one Size larger when determining what you can Grapple or Shove.

entries.name: Turn the Force
entries: Once per turn, when a creature within your reach fails to Grapple, Shove, move, or knock you {@condition Prone|XPHB}, you can immediately move that creature 5 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, provided it is no more than one Size larger than you.
This movement doesn't require an action or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

feat.name: Reactive Adaptation
entries: Pain teaches faster than theory ever could.
Once your body survives a danger, it remembers the lesson.
What harmed you once finds a far less welcoming target the second time.

entries.name: Learn the Damage
entries: When you take damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to choose one damage type dealt by that instance of damage.
You gain Resistance to the chosen damage type until the start of your next turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Retained Adaptation
entries: If you take the chosen damage type again while Learn the Damage is active, you can extend that Resistance until the end of your next turn without expending another use.
You can extend the same adaptation only once.

entries.name: Hardened Response
entries: Whenever your Resistance from this feat reduces damage, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} after the damage is resolved.

entries.name: Familiar Threat
entries: After you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, choose one damage type that dealt damage to you since your previous {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
The first time you take that damage type before your next Short or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8} + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
This reduction applies before you decide whether to use Learn the Damage.

entries.name: Refuse the Same Wound
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you take damage of a type to which you currently have Resistance from this feat, you can cause that instance of damage to deal no damage to you instead.
Any other effects of the triggering attack or effect still occur normally.

feat.name: Invocation Initiate
entries: Some powers are learned as spells. Others are carved into the self as enduring truths.
You have discovered the latter path unusually early.
An invocation is no formula you cast and forget—it becomes part of what you are.

entries.name: First Invocation
entries: Choose one Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites.
You gain that Invocation and all of its benefits.

For the purpose of choosing Invocations through this feat, you ignore any prerequisite that requires you to belong to a particular class, but you must still meet all other prerequisites, including level requirements, Pact requirements, required features, and any other specific prerequisite.

entries.name: Growing Doctrine
entries: Whenever your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases, you gain one additional Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites.
Invocations gained from this feat are permanent unless replaced by Rewritten Doctrine.

entries.name: Rewritten Doctrine
entries: Whenever you gain a level, you can replace one Invocation gained from this feat with another Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites.
If replacing an Invocation causes you to stop meeting the prerequisite of another Invocation you possess, you must also replace any Invocation that depends on it.

entries.name: Invocation Beyond Training
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, choose one Invocation for which you meet every prerequisite except its level requirement.
Your level can be up to 2 levels lower than that Invocation's requirement.
You temporarily gain that Invocation until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
This temporary Invocation doesn't count against the number of Invocations you gain from this feat.

entries.name: Independent Invocation
entries: Invocations gained from this feat are their own source of power.
They don't require spellcasting, spell slots, a particular spell list, or membership in another class unless the Invocation itself explicitly requires one of those things.

feat.name: Invocation Prodigy
entries: Your first Invocations were only the beginning.
What others engrave into themselves one doctrine at a time, you absorb with unnatural speed.
Each new stage of growth opens room for another permanent truth.

entries.name: Accelerated Doctrine
entries: You immediately gain two additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites.
These Invocations follow the same rules as Invocations gained through {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Unending Study
entries: Whenever your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases, you gain one additional Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites.
This Invocation is gained in addition to the Invocation granted by Growing Doctrine from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Refined Doctrine
entries: Whenever you gain a level, you can replace any number of Invocations gained through this feat with other Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites.

feat.name: Invocation Adept
entries: Your growing collection of Invocations has become second nature.
You no longer struggle to hold each doctrine separately within yourself.
With practice, one supernatural truth can be exchanged for another whenever your path demands it.

entries.name: Deepened Doctrine
entries: You immediately gain two additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites.
These Invocations follow the same rules as Invocations gained through {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Living Doctrine
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace one Invocation you possess from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}, {@feat Invocation Prodigy|FftForbiddenTome}, or this feat with another Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites.
The new Invocation remains until you replace it again.

entries.name: Practiced Revelation
entries: Choose one Invocation you possess that has a limited number of uses which are restored when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
You gain one additional use of that Invocation.
Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can choose a different eligible Invocation for this benefit.
If an Invocation has several separately limited abilities, choose which one receives the additional use when you select it.

entries.name: Expanding Doctrine
entries: Whenever your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases, you gain one additional Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites.

This Invocation is gained in addition to the Invocations granted by Growing Doctrine from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome} and Unending Study from {@feat Invocation Prodigy|FftForbiddenTome}.

feat.name: Invocation Paragon
entries: Your Invocations are no longer isolated secrets.
Each doctrine has become a permanent layer of your supernatural identity.
As your power grows, entire collections of Invocations unfold within you at once.

entries.name: Greater Doctrine
entries: You immediately gain three additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites.
These Invocations follow the same rules as Invocations gained through {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Cascading Insight
entries: Whenever your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases, you gain two additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites.

These Invocations are gained in addition to any Invocations granted by Growing Doctrine from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome} and Unending Study from {@feat Invocation Prodigy|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Perfected Doctrine
entries: Whenever you gain a level, you can replace any number of Invocations you possess from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}, {@feat Invocation Prodigy|FftForbiddenTome}, or this feat with other Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites.

entries.name: Endless Revelation
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose one Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites that you don't already possess.
You gain that Invocation until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
This temporary Invocation doesn't count against the number of Invocations granted by your feats.

feat.name: Invocation Sovereign
entries: Your Invocations no longer exist as separate doctrines.
They answer as parts of a single supernatural authority shaped around your will.
At this stage, learning an Invocation is less discovery than declaration.

entries.name: Sovereign Doctrine
entries: You immediately gain four additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites.
These Invocations follow the same rules as Invocations gained through {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Accelerated Ascension
entries: Whenever your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases, you gain three additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites.

These Invocations are gained in addition to those granted by Growing Doctrine from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}, Unending Study from {@feat Invocation Prodigy|FftForbiddenTome}, Expanding Doctrine from {@feat Invocation Adept|FftForbiddenTome}, and Cascading Insight from {@feat Invocation Paragon|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Sovereign Selection
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose two Invocations you don't possess for which you meet the prerequisites.
You gain both Invocations until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
These temporary Invocations don't count against the number of Invocations granted by your feats.

entries.name: Absolute Doctrine
entries: Whenever you gain a level, you can replace any number of Invocations you possess from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}, {@feat Invocation Prodigy|FftForbiddenTome}, {@feat Invocation Adept|FftForbiddenTome}, {@feat Invocation Paragon|FftForbiddenTome}, or this feat with other Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites.
You can make these replacements separately; you don't have to replace all of them at once.

entries.name: Perfect Invocation
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose one Invocation you possess that has a limited number of uses restored when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, the number of uses of that Invocation is doubled.
If the Invocation contains multiple separately limited abilities, choose one of those abilities to double.

feat.name: Boon of Infinite Doctrine
entries: Your Invocations are no longer powers you collect.
They are an infinite lattice of doctrine, instinct, and supernatural law written directly into your existence.
At this height, revelation does not come to you. It begins with you.

entries.name: Infinite Doctrine
entries: You immediately gain ten additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites.
These Invocations follow the same rules as Invocations gained through {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Endless Ascension
entries: Whenever your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases, you gain ten additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites.
These Invocations are gained in addition to every Invocation granted by the earlier feats in this chain.

entries.name: Living Archive
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose up to ten Invocations you don't possess.
You temporarily gain all chosen Invocations until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
For these choices, you can ignore class prerequisites, Pact prerequisites, required spells, required features, required Invocations, and level prerequisites.
You must still possess anything the Invocation actually requires to function.

entries.name: Perfect Doctrine
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace any number of permanent Invocations you possess from this feat chain with other Invocations.
Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can replace up to three such Invocations.
You must meet the prerequisites of the new Invocations unless another feature allows you to ignore them.

entries.name: Unbound Invocation
entries: Every Invocation you possess that has a limited number of uses has three times its normal number of uses.

This applies to uses restored on a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, uses per turn, uses per round, uses tied to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and any other explicitly limited use count.
If an Invocation contains multiple separate use pools, each pool is tripled.

entries.name: Inexhaustible Doctrine
entries: Whenever you expend a use of an Invocation, roll a {@dice d6}. On a 3-6, that use isn't expended.
If this causes the Invocation to remain at its maximum number of uses, you can still benefit from this feature.

entries.name: Doctrine Without Limit
entries: All Invocations you possess can apply simultaneously if their conditions are met.
They don't exclude one another merely because they modify the same attack, spell, action, Reaction, Bonus Action, movement, damage roll, Saving Throw, creature, object, target, or effect.
Identical effects with the same name still don't stack unless explicitly stated otherwise.

entries.name: Transcendent Invocation
entries: Whenever an Invocation refers to a class level, Warlock level, Pact level, or another progression value, you can use your character level instead.
Whenever an Invocation refers to an ability score or modifier, you can use any ability score of your choice.
Whenever an Invocation uses a fixed DC, you can instead use 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + one ability modifier of your choice if that DC would be higher.

entries.name: Supreme Revelation
entries: You no longer need to meet the prerequisites of Invocations you gain from Living Archive.
In addition, once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can permanently gain one Invocation whose prerequisites you don't meet.
That Invocation remains permanent even if you later lose whatever would normally qualify you for it.

entries.name: Eternal Revelation
entries: Whenever you gain a character level, choose two temporary Invocations you currently possess through Living Archive.
Both become permanent and no longer count against your temporary selections.

entries.name: Absolute Invocation
entries: Once per turn, when you use an Invocation, you can make that use Absolute.
For that use, no limited use is expended, no spell slot is expended, and no Material component is required unless it is consumed or has a listed cost.
Attack Rolls made as part of that use have Advantage, and Saving Throws made against it have Disadvantage.
Damage caused by that use ignores Resistance, and Immunity to that damage is treated as Resistance.
Any dice rolled for damage, healing, Temporary Hit Points, movement increase, or another numerical benefit use their maximum possible result instead of being rolled.
If the Invocation has a range other than Self, double that range. If it has a duration longer than Instantaneous, double that duration, to a maximum of 24 hours.

entries.name: Overwhelming Doctrine
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can activate up to five Invocations at the same time as part of the same action, Bonus Action, Reaction, attack, spell, or other qualifying event, provided each Invocation could legally apply to that event.
If multiple Invocations require the same trigger, they all resolve from that single trigger.

entries.name: Infinite Revelation
entries: At the start of each of your turns, choose one Invocation you don't possess.
You gain it until the start of your next turn and can ignore all prerequisites for it.
You can choose a different Invocation each turn.
This temporary Invocation doesn't count against any other Invocation limit.

entries.name: Doctrine Incarnate
entries: You can't be forced to lose, suppress, replace, or disable an Invocation you possess by any effect unless you choose to allow it.
Antimagic, nullification, suppression, dispelling, or similar effects don't suppress your Invocations unless the Invocation itself explicitly says otherwise.
Your Invocations function as part of your inherent existence rather than as external magic.

feat.name: Counterfighter
entries: You fight best when the enemy commits first.
Whenever a creature within your reach misses you with an attack, you can immediately make one melee weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against that creature.
This attack requires no Reaction and can't trigger Counterfighter again.
The attack has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} if the missed attack was a Critical Miss.
On a hit, the target can't make Opportunity Attacks against you until the start of its next turn.

feat.name: Flowing Combat
entries: Every attack carries you into the next position.
Whenever you make a weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can move up to 5 feet immediately before or after the attack.

This movement costs no additional movement, doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from the target of that attack, can occur even if your Speed is currently 0 provided you aren't {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, and can be used on every attack you make, not just once per turn.
You can't use this movement to pass through or enter a space you couldn't normally enter.

feat.name: Deflecting Guard
entries: You don't need to stop an attack completely. A slight change in angle is enough.
While you are wielding a melee weapon or are capable of making an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, whenever an attack hits you, you can attempt to deflect the blow.
Roll either the normal damage dice of one melee weapon you are wielding or the normal damage dice of your Unarmed Strike. If your Unarmed Strike doesn't normally use damage dice, use a d4 instead.
Reduce the damage you take from the triggering attack by the total rolled + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
This reduction requires no Reaction and can be used against every attack that hits you.
The reduction applies separately to each attack and can be used against melee attacks, ranged attacks, and spell attacks, provided you can perceive the attack.
If you are wielding more than one eligible melee weapon, you choose which weapon's normal damage dice to roll each time you use this Fighting Style.
If your Unarmed Strike can use more than one possible set of damage dice, use the damage dice you would normally use for that Unarmed Strike at the time the attack hits you.

entries.name: Perfect Deflection
entries: If Deflecting Guard reduces the triggering attack's damage to 0, you perfectly deflect the attack.
When this happens, you gain all of the following benefits:

items: You can immediately move up to 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
The attacker can't make Opportunity Attacks against you until the start of its next turn.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike you make against that attacker before the end of your next turn.

entries: These benefits require no Reaction.
The movement granted by Perfect Deflection doesn't count against your Speed.
Deflecting Guard can't reduce damage from an effect that doesn't involve an attack roll.

entries.name: Examples
entries: A character wielding a Greatsword rolls 2d6 + Proficiency Bonus to reduce the damage.
A character wielding a Greataxe rolls 1d12 + Proficiency Bonus.
If your Unarmed Strike normally uses 1d8 for its base damage, you roll 1d8 + Proficiency Bonus. If it normally uses 2d6, you instead roll 2d6 + Proficiency Bonus.

Only the normal base damage dice of the weapon or Unarmed Strike are used for this reduction. You don't include your ability modifier, magic-item bonuses, or additional damage dice from other features.

feat.name: Freehand Combat
entries: An empty hand is not an unused hand.
While you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and holding nothing in the other, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to AC.
Whenever you hit a creature with the weapon, you can immediately attempt to Grapple or Shove that creature as part of the same attack.
Making the Grapple or Shove this way requires no Action or Bonus Action.
A creature Grappled by you doesn't prevent you from continuing to attack with your one-handed weapon.

Whenever a creature you are Grappling misses you with an attack, you can immediately move it 5 feet to another unoccupied space within your reach, provided it is no more than one size larger than you.

entries: The Grapple or Shove granted by this Fighting Style can be attempted on every hit, though a creature already Grappled by you doesn't need to be Grappled again.

feat.name: Threatening Reach
entries: Once something enters your range, leaving it untouched is a choice you rarely make.

While wielding a melee weapon or capable of making an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, whenever a hostile creature enters your reach, moves from one space to another while remaining within your reach, or willingly moves 5 feet or more while within your reach, you can immediately make one melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike against that creature.
This attack requires no Reaction, occurs immediately after the triggering movement, doesn't count as an Opportunity Attack, and can be made even if the creature hasn't left your reach.
A creature can trigger this Fighting Style multiple times during its turn if its movement creates multiple separate qualifying triggers.
If one of these attacks hits, the creature's Speed is reduced by 5 feet until the end of that turn. This reduction is cumulative for multiple hits.

feat.name: Brutal Impact
entries: When you commit to a strike, you make sure the target feels all of it.
Whenever you hit with a melee weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can choose to make that hit a Brutal Impact.
When you do, roll the attack's normal damage dice one additional time and add them to the damage.

entries.name: Examples
entries: Longsword 1d8 → adds another 1d8.
Greatsword 2d6 → adds another 2d6.
An Unarmed Strike with normal base damage 1d10 → adds another 1d10.
Your ability modifier and other flat bonuses are added only once as normal.
If the attack is a Critical Hit, the additional damage dice granted by this Fighting Style are also doubled normally.
You can use Brutal Impact once on each of your turns.
At the end of your turn, if you used Brutal Impact and the attack hit a creature no more than one size larger than you, you can also choose to Push it 5 feet or knock it Prone.

feat.name: Escalating Force
entries: The first hit breaks the guard. The next one breaks everything behind it.

Whenever you hit the same creature more than once during a turn with a melee weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, each hit after the first deals additional damage equal to one of the attack's normal damage dice.
The bonus increases with each consecutive hit against that creature during the same turn:

items: Second hit: 1 additional normal damage die.
Third hit: 2 additional normal damage dice.
Fourth hit: 3 additional normal damage dice.
Each later hit adds one more normal damage die than the previous hit.

entries: For a weapon whose normal damage is 2d6, each additional normal damage die is 1d6, not 2d6.
If you attack a different creature, the count for the original creature ends.
The count also ends when your turn ends.
If one of these attacks is a Critical Hit, the additional damage dice from this Fighting Style are doubled normally.

entries.name: Example
entries: If you hit the same creature four times with a Greatsword during one turn, the attacks deal 2d6, then 2d6 + 1d6, then 2d6 + 2d6, then 2d6 + 3d6, before applying other modifiers as normal.

feat.name: Crushing Power
entries: Even your weakest strike carries enough force to break something.

Whenever you deal damage with a melee weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, each of the attack's normal damage dice that rolls below half of that die's maximum value is treated as half of its maximum value instead, rounded up.

entries.name: Examples
entries: d4: rolls of 1 become 2.
d6: rolls of 1–2 become 3.
d8: rolls of 1–3 become 4.
d10: rolls of 1–4 become 5.
d12: rolls of 1–5 become 6.
This applies to every qualifying attack you make.
This Fighting Style applies to all damage dice rolled as part of the attack, including damage dice from the weapon or Unarmed Strike, class features, feats, spells, magic items, and other effects.
Whenever every normal damage die of an attack rolls its maximum value, the attack also deals one additional normal damage die.

feat.name: Overwhelming Blow
entries: When you decide that one hit is enough, you make it true.
Whenever you hit a creature with a weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can turn that hit into an Overwhelming Blow.

When you do, roll the attack's normal damage dice one additional time and add them to the damage. The attack ignores Resistance to its damage. If the target has Immunity to that damage, treat that Immunity as Resistance instead. Any damage reduction that would reduce the damage of that attack is only half as effective.

After the damage is dealt, if the target is no more than one size larger than you, choose one of the following effects: push it up to 10 feet, knock it Prone, or cause it to drop one object it is holding.
You can use Overwhelming Blow once per turn.
If the attack is a Critical Hit, the additional damage dice granted by this feat are doubled normally as part of the Critical Hit.

entries.name: Example
entries: A Greatsword hit that normally deals 2d6 + Strength modifier instead deals 4d6 + Strength modifier when using Overwhelming Blow. Resistance is ignored, while Immunity is treated as Resistance.

feat.name: Titan Grip
entries: What others need two hands to control, you wield with one.
You can wield a melee weapon with the Two-Handed property in one hand.

items: The weapon retains its normal damage dice and all of its other properties.
The Two-Handed property doesn't require a second hand for you to attack with the weapon.
The weapon's Heavy property has no effect on you.
For features, feats, spells, and other effects, you can treat the weapon as being wielded with one hand or with two hands, whichever is more beneficial to you.
Your other hand remains completely free and can be used normally, including to wield another weapon, carry a Shield, Grapple, or manipulate objects.
You can draw or stow such a weapon as easily as a one-handed weapon.

Whenever you hit with a melee weapon you are wielding in one hand through this Fighting Style, you can Push the target 5 feet if it is no more than one size larger than you. This requires no additional action or saving throw.
Once on each of your turns when you hit with such a weapon, roll one of the weapon's normal damage dice one additional time and add it to the damage.

entries.name: Example
entries: A Greatsword can be wielded in one hand for its normal 2d6 damage while your other hand carries a Shield or another weapon. Once per turn, one hit can deal an additional 1d6, and each hit can Push an eligible target 5 feet.

feat.name: Charging Force
entries: Momentum turns every step into part of the strike.
Whenever you move at least 10 feet toward a creature immediately before hitting it with a melee weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, the attack gains the following benefits:

items: Roll the attack's normal damage dice one additional time and add them to the damage.
You can Push the target 10 feet directly away from you.
If the target collides with a solid surface or another creature before moving the full distance, it takes additional Bludgeoning damage equal to one of the attack's normal damage dice.
The movement toward the target doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from that target.

entries: You can benefit from Charging Force on every qualifying attack, provided you moved the required 10 feet before that attack.
If you have enough movement to create the required distance again during the same turn, you can trigger it again.

entries.name: Example
entries: Move 10 feet toward an enemy and hit with a Greatsword: its 2d6 normal damage dice are rolled one additional time, for 4d6 before other modifiers, and you can then Push the enemy 10 feet.

feat.name: Armor Breaker
entries: Every blow leaves something behind: a crack, a dent, an opening.
Whenever you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, its AC is reduced by 1.
This reduction is cumulative and lasts for 1 minute after the last time you hit that creature with a qualifying attack. Each new hit refreshes the duration.
A creature's AC can't be reduced below 10 by this effect.

whenever you hit a creature already affected by this Fighting Style, you can direct that hit against one source of its defense, including worn armor, a Shield, magical armor, Natural Armor such as scales, hide, shell, carapace, or similar protection, or an ongoing magical effect that grants AC, Resistance, Immunity, or damage reduction.

Targeting a defense with this Fighting Style doesn't replace or reduce the attack's damage. The creature takes the attack's damage normally, and the chosen armor, Shield, Natural Armor, or magical defense is damaged by the same hit.

If the chosen defense completely prevents the attack from reaching the creature, the attack damages the defense first and doesn't deal damage to the creature until the attack can pass through that defense.
Each time you target a defense that provides AC, you permanently reduce the AC it provides by 1. This reduction doesn't disappear when the 1-minute duration ends.

items: Armor or a Shield whose AC contribution is reduced to 0 provides no AC until repaired.
Magical armor or a magical Shield can be physically broken in the same way; being magical doesn't prevent this Fighting Style from damaging it.
Natural Armor can be cracked, shattered, torn, or otherwise breached, preventing the creature from benefiting from the destroyed portion until it is healed, regenerated, or restored.
An ongoing magical defense that is broken is ended, even if it would normally be unable to be damaged by weapon attacks.

entries: If a magical defense doesn't provide a numerical AC bonus, each qualifying hit against it counts toward breaking it. It is destroyed after a number of such hits equal to the effect's level + 1. If the effect has no level, it requires 3 hits.

The accumulated hits against a particular defense don't disappear merely because your turn or the encounter ends. They remain until that armor, natural defense, or magical effect is repaired, restored, renewed, or replaced.
While a creature has been hit at least 2 times by you while the 1-minute reduction remains active, your attacks against it ignore its damage reduction.
While it has been hit at least 3 times, your attacks against it ignore Resistance.
While it has been hit at least 5 times, you treat its Immunity as Resistance.
While it has been hit at least 7 times, your attacks ignore that Resistance as well.

entries.name: Example
entries: Repeatedly striking a creature in Plate can damage the creature normally while permanently reducing the Plate's AC contribution. The same attacks can instead crack Natural Armor or break an ongoing magical defense.

feat.name: Beyond Your Limits
entries: What others call a limit, you recognize only as the point where effort begins.

Whenever you make an Ability Check, Attack Roll, or Saving Throw and the result would fail, you can push yourself beyond your normal capability. Roll 1d6 and add it to the roll, potentially turning the failure into a success. You can decide to do so after knowing that the roll failed.

entries.name: Push Further
entries: If the roll still fails after adding the d6, you can roll another d6 and add it as well. You can continue doing this until the roll succeeds or you choose to stop.
For every d6 you roll beyond the first, you take 1d12 Force damage after the roll is resolved.
This damage can't be reduced or prevented in any way, doesn't interrupt the roll you're attempting, and can't reduce you below 1 Hit Point.

entries.name: Breakthrough
entries: If you succeed after rolling 3 or more d6s, you gain Advantage on the next d20 Test of the same type you make before the end of your next turn. If the triggering roll was an Attack Roll, this applies to your next Attack Roll; if it was a Saving Throw, it applies to your next Saving Throw; if it was an Ability Check, it applies to your next Ability Check.

entries.name: Example
entries: You miss an attack by 4. You roll a d6 and get a 2, so the attack still misses. You roll another d6 and get a 1, then a third d6 and get a 5, finally turning the miss into a hit. Because you rolled two d6s beyond the first, you take 2d12 Force damage after the attack is resolved, and because you succeeded after rolling at least 3d6, you have Advantage on your next Attack Roll before the end of your next turn.

feat.name: Strength Above All
entries: You have trained until raw physical power can substitute for talents that normally rely on speed, precision, presence, or even instinct.
Whenever you make an Ability Check, you can use your Strength modifier in place of the ability modifier normally used for that check. This includes checks involving any Skill or Tool proficiency.

entries.name: Physical Supremacy
entries: You can also use your Strength modifier in place of the normal ability modifier for Initiative, Saving Throws, determining the DC of a feature or ability you use, and Attack Rolls and Damage Rolls with weapons or Unarmed Strikes.
If a feature already uses Strength, this provides no additional benefit.

entries.name: Refuse to Falter
entries: Whenever you make a Saving Throw using Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma, you can use your Strength modifier instead.
whenever an effect would reduce one of your Ability Scores, you can choose for it to reduce your Strength score instead.

feat.name: Perfect Execution
entries: Once you prove that you can do something, chance has less and less authority over the result.
Whenever you succeed on an Ability Check, Attack Roll, or Saving Throw, record the unmodified d20 result of that roll for that type of test.
Whenever you later make the same type of test and roll lower than the recorded result, you can expend 1 use of this feat to treat the d20 roll as the recorded result instead.
You can use this feat a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Raise the Standard
entries: If you later succeed with a higher unmodified d20 result for the same type of test, the recorded result increases to that number.
Recording or increasing a result doesn't expend a use.

feat.name: Absolute Focus
entries: When you decide that something must succeed, uncertainty stops mattering.
Whenever you make an Ability Check, Attack Roll, or Saving Throw, after rolling the d20 but before the outcome is determined, you can replace the d20 result with a 20.
This replacement counts as the actual d20 result for all purposes.
When used on an Attack Roll, this can cause the attack to become a Critical Hit if a roll of 20 would normally do so.
You can use this feat a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

feat.name: Act Before the Moment
entries: By the time everyone else realizes what is happening, you have already acted.
Immediately after another creature you can see starts its turn, you can interrupt that turn and take a special turn of your own before it continues.
During this special turn, you can move up to your Speed, take one Action, and take one Bonus Action.
After your special turn ends, the interrupted creature resumes its turn from where it stopped.
Your special turn doesn't replace your normal turn and doesn't change your Initiative.

You regain your Reaction at the start of this special turn, but when the special turn ends, you return to however many Reactions you had before it began. This prevents the special turn from permanently granting additional Reactions.
You can use this feat a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

feat.name: Refuse the Outcome
entries: Failure is only final if you allow it to be.
Whenever you fail an Ability Check, Attack Roll, or Saving Throw, you can immediately declare that result unacceptable.
Instead of resolving the failure, roll the d20 again and use the new result.
If the new result also fails, you can choose to roll again.
You can continue rerolling the same test until you succeed or choose to stop.

entries.name: The Cost of Insistence
entries: The first reroll is free.
For every reroll after the first, you take 1d12 Force damage after that reroll is resolved.
This damage can't be reduced or prevented, doesn't interrupt the roll, and can't reduce you below 1 Hit Point.

entries.name: Uses
entries: You can use this feat a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
One use of this feat allows you to continue rerolling that same test until you succeed or choose to stop.

subclassFeature.name: The Archive
entries: Starting at 3rd level, your forbidden studies open the Archive, granting the features below.

subclassFeature.name: Archive Keeper
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you gain Pact of the Tome without meeting its prerequisites. It doesn't count against Forbidden Invocations, and its Book of Shadows becomes your Archive and Wizard spellbook.

entries.name: Endless Pages
entries: The Archive has effectively endless pages and can hold any number of Wizard spells, Pact magic, formulae, research, maps, drawings, notes, and other written or illustrated information.

It counts as both your spellbook and Book of Shadows for your features. When Pact of the Tome lets you choose spells or cantrips, you can choose them from any spell list, using Intelligence as your spellcasting ability for them.

entries.name: Living Chronicle
entries: The Archive automatically records anything you personally see, including creatures, locations, events, objects, visible writing, appearances, actions, and other observable details. It records only what you actually perceived and reveals no hidden or unknown information.

It preserves detailed portraits and each appearance in which you encounter a person. When you first gain the Archive, it can also record people you previously encountered, but only from details you genuinely remember.
The Archive maintains a searchable index. While holding it, you can use a Bonus Action to request recorded information, causing the relevant entries to appear immediately.
Information recorded by the Archive doesn't fade when your own memory does.

entries.name: The Archive Remembers
entries: Information accepted into the Archive can't be permanently lost through ordinary damage.

If the Archive is lost or destroyed, you can recreate it with a 1-hour ritual, restoring all stored spells, Pact magic, records, portraits, maps, illustrations, research, and other information. Any previous copy disappears when the ritual is completed.

subclassFeature.name: Forbidden Invocations
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you gain two Eldritch Invocations of your choice from the Warlock class.

You ignore every prerequisite for Invocations gained through this feature. If one refers to a prerequisite you lack, you are treated as having it only to use that Invocation; this grants no prerequisite and qualifies you for nothing else.
If such an Invocation uses a spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, or spell save DC, you can use your Intelligence and Wizard spellcasting statistics.
Whenever you gain a Wizard level, you can replace one Invocation gained through this feature with another, ignoring its prerequisites.
Pact of the Tome granted by The Archive doesn't count toward this number.

subclassFeature.name: Archive Spells
entries: Starting at 3rd level, when you reach a Wizard level shown in the Archive Spells table, the listed spells are added to your Archive if absent, requiring no gold, time, or materials. They aren't automatically prepared unless another feature says otherwise.

subclassFeature.name: Tome Convergence
entries: Starting at 6th level, the Archive can merge with written vessels of magic without destroying them.

entries.name: Merge Spellbook
entries: While touching your Archive and an eligible spellbook, magical spellbook, grimoire, codex, tome, or similar written object containing spells or magical research, you can merge it into the Archive with a 10-minute ritual.

While merged, it is physically incorporated into the Archive, counts as part of your Archive, Book of Shadows, and Wizard spellbook, and its magical properties remain usable through the Archive. Its Charges, limitations, activation requirements, Attunement, and other rules remain unchanged.
You can merge multiple eligible spellbooks. Merging creates no additional Attunement or Attunement slot, though you must still be attuned to a merged spellbook that requires Attunement at this level.

entries.name: Perfect Copy
entries: When a spellbook merges, the Archive copies everything recorded within it, including spells, rituals, formulae, notes, diagrams, maps, research, and illustrations, requiring no gold, special ink, or additional time.
Wizard spells copied this way are permanently recorded. The Archive can preserve spells above your current casting level, but you can't prepare or cast them until you normally could.

entries.name: Separate Tome
entries: You can separate a merged spellbook with a 1-minute ritual while touching the Archive. It returns intact with all Charges, enchantments, and other magical properties, while the Archive retains copies of its recorded contents.
After separation, the original and Archive copy are independent. Merging it again copies any new or changed information.

entries.name: Hovering Archive
entries: The Archive can hover, follow you, keep pace with your normal movement, remain nearby, and move into your hand when you reach for it, requiring no action from you.

subclassFeature.name: Open the Index
entries: Starting at 10th level, as a Bonus Action, you open the Archive's Living Index for 1 minute. Once used, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a spell slot of 4th level or higher to activate it again.

entries.name: Every Page at Hand
entries: While Open the Index is active, every Wizard spell recorded in your Archive is prepared for you without counting against your prepared spells; you still expend spell slots normally.
For an Intelligence check concerning a creature, location, object, symbol, event, spell, or other subject previously recorded by the Archive, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

After casting a Wizard spell that wasn't prepared before Open the Index began, you take {@damage 1d4} Psychic damage per spell level. Cantrips cause no damage. If this reduces you to 0 Hit Points, Open the Index ends.

entries.name: Second Mind
entries: When you cast a Wizard spell that requires Concentration, you can have the Archive maintain Concentration instead, requiring no action. You can then concentrate on another spell normally, and the Archive can maintain only one spell at a time.
The Archive makes no Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration; damage, effects that would force such a save, and you becoming {@condition Incapacitated} don't end it.

Its Concentration ends only if you die, the Archive is destroyed, you and it are more than 1 mile apart, you end the spell, the spell ends normally, or the Archive begins concentrating on another spell.

subclassFeature.name: The Archive Awakens
entries: Starting at 14th level, the Archive awakens as a living magical entity.

entries.name: Living Archive
entries: The Archive becomes a living magical entity. It can independently open, close, rearrange, write, illustrate, present relevant information, fly, follow you, avoid obvious danger, and return to your hand; its ordinary movement and harmless behavior require no action from you.
It can communicate through writing, moving illustrations, speech, or telepathy. You can communicate telepathically with it within 1 mile.
It understands languages you understand and can interpret languages sufficiently preserved within its pages without teaching them to you.
While on the same plane, you always know its direction and approximate distance. If it is within 30 feet, you can call it into an empty hand without using an action.
The Archive always recognizes you as its Keeper regardless of changes to your appearance, age, disguise, transformation, form, or body.

entries.name: The Archive Acts
entries: Once on each of your turns, the Archive can cast one Wizard cantrip recorded within it without requiring your Action or Bonus Action.

It uses your Wizard spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC. The spell originates from the Archive, requires no Verbal or Somatic components from you, and must have a casting time of 1 Action or less.
The Archive makes the spell's choices, though you can mentally direct them while within 1 mile. The spell still counts as your Wizard spell for your class and Archive features.

entries.name: Beyond Attunement
entries: A magic spellbook merged with your Archive can have its Attunement requirement satisfied by the Archive. You can use its Attunement-required properties without attuning to it or occupying an Attunement slot.

If already attuned, you can end that Attunement and retain those properties while it remains merged. This benefit ends when the spellbook is separated, and the Archive never permanently copies its magical properties.

subclassFeature.name: This Is Only the Beginning
entries: Starting at 17th level, the Archive carries your magic beyond conventional limits.

entries.name: Magic Without Permission
entries: Antimagic and similar effects can't suppress, nullify, disable, or prevent your Wizard spells, Wizard class features, Archive subclass features, the Archive, magical properties of spellbooks merged through Tome Convergence, or spells maintained through Second Mind.

This includes {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB}, dead-magic zones, magical nullification, and similar effects whose primary purpose is suppressing magic. Your Wizard spells can be cast, enter, originate, pass through, and continue functioning within them.

If you create an antimagic or magic-suppressing effect, you can leave your own magic and the Archive unaffected while it suppresses other magic normally. This doesn't make you immune to hostile magic.

entries.name: Beyond the Ninth
entries: Once per Long Rest, you can cast one 9th-level Wizard spell recorded in your Archive without expending a spell slot, following its normal casting time, components, material costs, and consumed components.

When you cast a Wizard spell of 6th level or higher, a lower-level spell or magical effect can't counter, dispel, suppress, or end it solely by suppressing magic. Effects of the same or higher level can interact with it normally unless another feature says otherwise.

A rule treating 9th level as the maximum spell level doesn't prevent an Archive feature from enhancing, reproducing, protecting, modifying, or otherwise interacting with your 9th-level spells. This feature creates no 10th-level spells or spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: The Last Archivist
entries: Starting at 20th level, you and the Archive become inseparable.

entries.name: The Archive Within
entries: Every Wizard spell recorded in your Archive is always prepared for you without counting against your prepared spells, and you can cast it with your Wizard spell slots even without the physical Archive.
You no longer suffer Knowledge Overload. Anything permanently contained within the Archive remains available through your bond with it.

If the Archive is lost, sealed, suppressed, or destroyed, you retain its recorded Wizard spells and Archive subclass features. Any Archive feature requiring a stored spell, formula, or piece of information can access it regardless of the book's location.

entries.name: The Final Keeper
entries: The Archive can no longer be permanently separated from you. If destroyed, you can use a Bonus Action to recreate it in an empty hand or an unoccupied space within 5 feet, retaining every recorded spell and other preserved record.
Tome Convergence doesn't duplicate an external magic item; a merged spellbook remains the same original item.
Once you recreate the Archive this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Physiology
entries: Starting at 3rd level, when you cast a Sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, choose one Manifestation until the start of your next turn:

items: {@b Flow.} Immediately move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
{@b Density.} Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Sorcerer level.
{@b Refraction.} Until the manifestation ends, you have Half Cover.
{@b Surge.} Add your Charisma modifier to one damage or healing roll of the spell.

subclassFeature.name: Spellform
entries: Starting at 3rd level, as a Bonus Action, you can spend 2 Sorcery Points to enter Spellform for 1 minute.
While in Spellform:

items: You can move through creatures but not objects.
You can move through a creature's space without treating it as Difficult Terrain.
You have Advantage on checks and saving throws made to escape a Grapple or the Restrained condition.
You can provide Somatic components even if your hands are occupied.
Your body visibly changes into an arcane form of your choice—living flame, flowing runes, fractured light, black mist, geometric energy, or another magical manifestation.

entries: Spellform doesn't make you incorporeal or let you end your movement inside another creature.

subclassFeature.name: Rewrite the Formula
entries: Starting at 6th level, whenever you cast a Sorcerer spell, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to alter one of the following properties for that casting:

items: {@b Shape.} If the spell creates a Cone, Cube, Cylinder, Line, or Sphere, you can change it into another of those shapes while preserving approximately the same affected size.
{@b Vector.} Change the direction from which the spell's force or visible effect appears to strike a target.
{@b Signature.} Change one damage type dealt by the spell to Acid, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, Necrotic, Psychic, Radiant, or Thunder.
{@b Origin.} Cause the spell to originate from an unoccupied point you can see within 30 feet rather than from yourself, provided doing so doesn't increase its maximum range.

entries: This isn't Metamagic and can be combined with Metamagic normally.

subclassFeature.name: No Longer Entirely Physical
entries: Starting at 14th level, your Spellform gains the following benefits:

items: You gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and can hover.
You can move through solid objects and creatures as though they were Difficult Terrain.
If you end your turn inside a solid object, you are moved to the nearest unoccupied space and take {@damage 1d10} Force damage.
You can't be Grappled or Restrained by purely physical means.
Squeezing never costs you additional movement.

entries: Spellform now costs 1 Sorcery Point.

subclassFeature.name: I Am the Casting
entries: Starting at 18th level, once on each of your turns when you cast a Sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, you can become part of it until it finishes resolving.
During that casting:

items: You can choose any point occupied by or affected by the spell as your position.
You can move between points within the spell's area or path without spending movement.
Attacks and effects can't target you until the spell finishes resolving unless they can also affect the spell itself.

entries: When the spell finishes resolving, you appear in an unoccupied space the spell affected or passed through.
While in Spellform, the first Metamagic option you apply to a spell on each of your turns costs 1 fewer Sorcery Point, to a minimum of 0.

subclassFeature.name: Break the Impossible
entries: Starting at 3rd level, your weapon attacks and Unarmed Strikes count as magical for overcoming Resistance and Immunity.

You can physically attack magical effects with a tangible boundary or occupied area, such as barriers, walls, restraints, and summoned bindings. Such an effect has AC 10 + its spell level, or AC 15 if it has no spell level.

On a hit, you damage it as an object. It has Hit Points equal to 5 × its spell level, or 20 Hit Points if it has no spell level. At 0 Hit Points, the struck portion is destroyed, or the entire effect ends if it can't meaningfully exist in separate portions. Instantaneous effects can't be attacked this way.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, you can break its stance, preventing it from making Opportunity Attacks against you until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Nothing Holds Forever
entries: Starting at 7th level, you have Advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to escape the Grappled, Restrained, or Paralyzed condition. When you fail such a saving throw, you can expend one use of Second Wind to succeed instead.

As an Action, you can strike a magical condition affecting yourself or a creature within your reach. Make one weapon attack or Unarmed Strike against AC 10 + the effect's level, or AC 15 if it wasn't created by a leveled spell.
On a hit, end one of these conditions caused by that effect on the target: Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Restrained, or Stunned.

subclassFeature.name: Strike Through Magic
entries: Starting at 10th level, once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, you can force one magical effect affecting it to make a Constitution saving throw against DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + the Strength or Dexterity modifier used for the attack.
On a failed save, choose one:

items: Suppress that magical effect until the start of your next turn.
End one spell of 3rd level or lower affecting the creature.
Prevent the creature from teleporting until the start of your next turn.

entries: At Fighter level 15, the maximum spell level you can end becomes 5th level.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses after a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: There Is No Safe Distance
entries: Starting at 15th level, when a creature you can see within 60 feet attempts to teleport, magically move to another space, or move to another plane, you can use your Reaction to make one weapon attack against it; your weapon's reach or range extends far enough for this attack.

On a hit, the creature takes damage normally and must make a Constitution saving throw against your Strike Through Magic DC. On a failure, the movement fails, but any Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell slot, or other resource spent on it is still expended.

subclassFeature.name: Everything Can Break
entries: Starting at 18th level, your attacks can interact with Force effects, incorporeal or ethereal creatures, magical barriers, and similar effects as though they were physically present.
When you hit a creature, object, or magical effect, you can declare a Perfect Break. The attack:

items: Ignores Resistance to its damage.
Treats Immunity to its damage as Resistance instead.
Ignores magical bonuses to AC.
Ignores Half Cover, Three-Quarters Cover, and magical cover.
Can damage magical effects even if they normally state that they can't be damaged.

entries: Against a spell or magical effect of 8th level or lower, you can destroy or end it immediately instead of dealing damage.
You can use Perfect Break a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can cast spells from the Wizard spell list as martial techniques through your weapons.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: At 3rd level, you know four Wizard cantrips of your choice. You learn more as shown in the Cantrips column of the Spellblade Spellcasting table.
Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace one Spellblade cantrip you know with another Wizard cantrip.

entries.name: Prepared Spells
entries: You prepare Wizard spells, with the number prepared shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Spellblade Spellcasting table.
Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace any prepared Spellblade spells with other Wizard spells for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Spellblade Spellcasting table shows your spell slots, which you regain when you finish a Long Rest.
You reach 5th-level Spellblade spells at Fighter level 11 and never progress beyond 5th-level Spellblade spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: When you cast a Spellblade spell using a weapon as your Spellcasting Focus, your Spellcasting Ability is the ability you would use for an attack roll with that weapon: Strength or Dexterity. If multiple abilities are eligible, choose one when you cast the spell.
Your spell save DC equals 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Spellcasting Ability modifier.
Your spell attack modifier equals your Proficiency Bonus + your Spellcasting Ability modifier.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use any weapon with which you are proficient as a Spellcasting Focus for your Spellblade spells, incorporating Somatic components into attacks, guards, flourishes, draws, aiming motions, or changes in stance.

subclassFeature.name: Spellwoven Combat
entries: Starting at 3rd level, when you take the Attack action, you can replace one attack with a Spellblade cantrip that normally has a casting time of an Action. If it requires a weapon attack as part of its casting, that attack counts as the attack you replaced.

Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can change that attack's damage type to Force, Psychic, or a damage type dealt by one of your prepared Spellblade spells. Choose the type when the attack hits.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Rhythm
entries: Starting at 5th level, once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can immediately cast one Spellblade cantrip with a casting time of an Action.
Casting it this way:

items: Requires no Action or Bonus Action.
Is considered part of the same Attack action.
Can originate from you or from the weapon that triggered this feature.
Doesn't prevent you from making any remaining attacks granted by Extra Attack.

entries: You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. At Fighter level 11, the first use on each of your turns expends no use; a second use that turn expends one.

subclassFeature.name: Blade and Spell as One
entries: Starting at 7th level, when you cast a Spellblade spell of 1st level or higher with a casting time of an Action, you can make one weapon attack as part of the same Action.

Alternatively, when you take the Attack action, you can replace one attack with a Spellblade spell of 1st level or higher that normally has a casting time of an Action. You can do so a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest, and you can't cast more than one leveled Spellblade spell as part of the same Attack action this way.

You can also deliver a Spellblade spell that requires a melee weapon, melee weapon attack, or an attack with a melee weapon through a ranged weapon with which you are proficient, including a bow, crossbow, thrown weapon, or firearm if present.

If the spell requires a melee weapon attack as part of its casting, make a ranged weapon attack instead. If its range or melee-reach requirement exists solely to permit that melee weapon attack, use the ranged weapon's normal range instead. The projectile or thrown weapon carries the spell, which otherwise functions normally when that attack resolves.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Impact
entries: Starting at 10th level, once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, its next saving throw against one of your Spellblade spells before the end of your next turn is made with Disadvantage.
If the next Spellblade spell you use against it instead requires an attack roll, you have Advantage on the first spell attack roll you make against it before the end of your next turn.
Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with a Spellblade spell, you can prevent it from making Opportunity Attacks until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Pursuit
entries: Starting at 15th level, immediately after you cast a Spellblade spell or make a weapon attack as part of your Attack action, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, once on each of your turns.
If you appear within the reach of a weapon you wield, your next weapon attack against a creature within that reach before the end of the turn has Advantage.
When you use Action Surge, you can teleport once before or after each Action you take that turn without counting those teleports against this feature's normal once-per-turn limit.

subclassFeature.name: Perfect Spellwarfare
entries: Starting at 18th level, when you take the Attack action, you can replace any number of attacks with different Spellblade cantrips that normally have a casting time of an Action; you can't cast the same cantrip more than once during that Attack action this way.
Once on each of your turns when you cast a Spellblade spell of 1st level or higher, you can immediately make one weapon attack without using an Action or Bonus Action.

When you use Action Surge, one Spellblade spell of 5th level or lower you cast that turn can be cast without expending a spell slot. Once you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can cast spells from the Wizard spell list through physical combat techniques.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: At 3rd level, you know four Wizard cantrips of your choice. You learn more as shown in the Cantrips column of the Spellfist Spellcasting table.
Whenever you gain a Pugilist level, you can replace one Spellfist cantrip you know with another Wizard cantrip.

entries.name: Prepared Spells
entries: You prepare Wizard spells, with the number prepared shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Spellfist Spellcasting table.
Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace any prepared Spellfist spells with other Wizard spells for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Spellfist Spellcasting table shows your spell slots, which you regain when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
You gain 1st-level spells at Pugilist level 3, 2nd at level 5, 3rd at level 7, 4th at level 9, and 5th at level 11. Your Spellfist spellcasting never progresses beyond 5th-level spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Strength is your Spellcasting Ability for your Spellfist spells.

Your spell save DC equals 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier, and your spell attack modifier equals your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: Your body counts as a Spellcasting Focus for your Spellfist spells, and you can perform Somatic components through punches, guards, footwork, feints, breathing patterns, or other fighting motions.

subclassFeature.name: Fists and Formulae
entries: Starting at 3rd level, when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can replace one attack with a Spellfist cantrip that normally has a casting time of an Action, then make any remaining attacks normally.

For your Spellfist spells, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} count as proficient melee weapons and can satisfy requirements to wield, use, or attack with a melee weapon. For a Material component or other requirement specifying a melee weapon with a monetary value, an Unarmed Strike counts as a melee weapon worth 1 GP only for casting that spell. If the spell makes an attack with the weapon used in its casting, you can make an Unarmed Strike for that attack.

Whenever you make a spell attack, you can treat it as an Unarmed Strike for Pugilist features that trigger when you make or hit with an Unarmed Strike. It remains a spell attack and deals the spell's normal damage unless another feature says otherwise.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Follow-Through
entries: Starting at 5th level, once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can expend 1 {@classFeature Moxie|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|2|Pugilist2024|Moxie Point} to immediately cast a Spellfist cantrip with a casting time of an Action.
The casting requires no Action or Bonus Action, counts as part of the same Attack action, doesn't prevent remaining Extra Attack attacks, and can target the creature you hit or another legal target.

If it targets the creature you hit, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the first attack roll of the cantrip, or that creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its first saving throw against the cantrip.
You can use this feature only once on each of your turns.

subclassFeature.name: Moxie Casting
entries: Starting at 6th level, when you cast a Spellfist spell of 1st level or higher, you can expend Moxie Points equal to the spell's casting level instead of a spell slot. The spell otherwise functions normally, and you can't cast it above the highest Spellfist spell level you can normally cast.

When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can replace one attack with a Spellfist spell of 1st level or higher that normally has a casting time of an Action, once on each of your turns, then make any remaining attacks normally.

subclassFeature.name: Magic Hits Back
entries: Starting at 11th level, once on each of your turns when you damage one or more creatures with a Spellfist spell, you can immediately make one {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} without using an Action or Bonus Action.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you can immediately cast one Spellfist cantrip with a casting time of an Action without using an Action or Bonus Action. You can benefit from each of these effects during the same turn.

When a Spellfist spell requires a spell attack against a creature within your Unarmed Strike's reach, you can instead make an Unarmed Strike attack roll. On a hit, the spell hits and the target suffers both the spell's normal effects and your Unarmed Strike's normal damage; the attack counts as both a spell attack hit and an Unarmed Strike hit.

subclassFeature.name: Perfect Arcane Violence
entries: Starting at 17th level, when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can replace any number of attacks with different Spellfist cantrips that normally have a casting time of an Action; you can't cast the same cantrip more than once during that Attack action this way.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can expend Moxie Points equal to the level of a prepared Spellfist spell to cast it immediately without using an Action or Bonus Action.

The spell must normally have a casting time of an Action and must be able to target the creature you hit or have an area that can legally originate from its space. An area spell can include that creature. The spell counts as part of the triggering attack but otherwise follows its normal rules.
Whenever you cast a 5th-level Spellfist spell using 5 Moxie Points, roll your Fisticuffs die after it resolves. On a 5 or higher, regain 1 Moxie Point.

subclassFeature.name: Beyond Ordinary Flesh
entries: Starting at 3rd level, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} count as magical for overcoming Resistance and Immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
For carrying, lifting, pushing, dragging, Grappling, and Shoving, you count as one size larger than you are.

When you hit with an Unarmed Strike, you can roll twice the normal number of Fisticuffs dice for its normal damage. Only those dice are doubled; your ability modifier and additional damage aren't unless another feature says otherwise. This costs no Moxie Point.
If the hit causes a Strength check or Strength saving throw, the target makes it with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

When you fail a Strength check, Strength saving throw, or Constitution saving throw, you can add one roll of your Fisticuffs die, potentially turning it into a success. You can do so a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all uses on a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
If this turns a failed saving throw into a success, that effect can't knock you {@condition Prone|XPHB}, push, pull, forcibly move you, or reduce your Speed.
Your Unarmed Strikes deal double damage to objects and structures and ignore a Damage Threshold equal to or lower than your Pugilist level + your Strength score.

subclassFeature.name: Force of Will
entries: Starting at 5th level, your physical power begins producing effects that resemble magic without actually being magic. What others accomplish through spells, you reproduce through impossible strength, speed, pressure, instinct, and force of will.

entries.name: Impossible Techniques
entries: Choose four cantrips from the Cleric, Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard spell list. They become your Conquerer Techniques.
You use the chosen cantrips' rules to determine what each technique can do, but a Conquerer Technique isn't a spell or magical effect, and you aren't casting a spell when you use one.

You don't gain the Spellcasting feature or Spell Slots from this feature. Your Conquerer Techniques can't be {@spell Counterspell|XPHB|Counterspelled} or dispelled, and Antimagic and similar effects don't suppress them. Using one doesn't count as casting a spell.

You ignore any Verbal component of a Conquerer Technique. You still perform any Somatic component as part of the physical motion that produces the technique. You don't need a Material component unless it is consumed or has a listed cost.

entries.name: Strength Is Your Power
entries: Strength is the ability you use whenever a Conquerer Technique refers to your spellcasting ability.

Your Technique Save DC equals 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier, and your Technique Attack Modifier equals your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength modifier.
If a cantrip uses your spellcasting ability modifier for damage, healing, distance, or another numerical effect, use your Strength modifier instead.

entries.name: Technique Attack
entries: Whenever you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with the use of a Conquerer Technique that normally has a casting time of an Action. Using a technique this way isn't casting a spell.
If the technique includes one or more attack rolls, those rolls count as attacks for the purposes of your Pugilist and Conquerer features.

entries.name: Cast Through Violence
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can immediately use one Conquerer Technique that normally has a casting time of an Action.

The technique must be able to target the creature you hit, include it among its targets, or create an area that can legally originate from its space. It resolves immediately after the attack's damage and requires no additional Action.
Using a technique this way isn't casting a spell. This use is separate from Technique Attack.

entries.name: Growing Force
entries: You learn one additional Conquerer Technique when you reach Pugilist levels 8, 11, 14, and 17.

entries.name: Weaponized Body
entries: Your Unarmed Strikes count as proficient melee weapons worth 1 gp for the purpose of your Conquerer Techniques.
Your body can be targeted and treated as a weapon by a Conquerer Technique that targets, enchants, empowers, imbues, coats, alters, or otherwise affects a weapon.
If such a technique normally requires you to hold or wield the affected weapon, you are considered to be holding and wielding your own body for that purpose.

subclassFeature.name: Too Tough to Matter
entries: Starting at 6th level, whenever you take damage, reduce it by one roll of your Fisticuffs die + your Constitution modifier + your Pugilist level. This requires no action or Moxie, has no usage limit, and applies every time you take damage.
The number of Fisticuffs dice rolled for this reduction increases to two at Pugilist level 11, three at level 17, and four at level 20.

Apply this reduction after every other damage modifier, including Resistance, Immunity, Vulnerability, multiplication, and other reductions. It is the final reduction before you lose Hit Points, and the damage source can't reduce, ignore, bypass, or prevent it.

If the damage remaining after this reduction is equal to or less than your Constitution modifier, you take 0 damage. If this feature reduces damage to 0, any additional effect that would occur solely because that damage was dealt also fails to affect you.
Against an effect that normally deals half damage on a successful save, you take no damage on a success and half on a failure; then apply Too Tough to Matter to any remaining damage.
You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against being {@condition Frightened|XPHB} or magically put to sleep.

subclassFeature.name: Magic Gives Way
entries: Starting at 8th level, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} can physically interact with ongoing magical effects that have tangible form or occupy physical space, such as walls, barriers, restraints, conjured objects, Force constructs, cages, chains, and shields. You need no special weapon, damage type, or property to strike them.

If such an effect has AC and Hit Points, you can attack and damage it normally. If it normally can't be attacked, make an Unarmed Strike against AC 10 + its spell level, or AC 15 if it has no spell level.
When you hit such an effect, you can deal your Unarmed Strike's damage normally and also suppress or destroy part of it; you no longer have to choose between dealing damage and disrupting the effect.

You can suppress a contiguous section of the effect no larger than a 20-foot cube until the start of your next turn. If the effect's spell level is no greater than half your Pugilist level, rounded down, you can permanently destroy that section instead.
If the entire effect fits within the section you can destroy, you can destroy the entire effect with that hit.
At Pugilist level 17, this feature has no spell-level limit.
This doesn't affect purely abstract magic such as charms, curses, divinations, teleportation effects, or resolved spells with no physical manifestation.

subclassFeature.name: Nothing Keeps You Down
entries: Starting at 11th level, at the start of each of your turns, you can end one of these conditions on yourself without an action or Moxie: {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Restrained|XPHB}, or {@condition Stunned|XPHB}.
Difficult Terrain costs you no extra movement, standing from {@condition Prone|XPHB} costs only 5 feet, and while conscious your Speed can't be reduced below half its normal value.

You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against being unwillingly transformed, teleported, banished, or transported to another plane. When an effect would move you against your will, you choose how much of that movement occurs, from 0 feet to the full distance.

During your turn, you can move through a hostile creature's space regardless of size, but can't willingly end there. A larger creature's space counts as Difficult Terrain for this movement, and Opportunity Attacks triggered by moving through a hostile creature's space are made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Magic Cannot Hold
entries: Starting at 14th level, your Unarmed Strikes can interact with ongoing magical effects attached to a creature or object even if the effect has no separate physical form.

When you hit a creature or object with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, once on each of your turns you can choose one spell or magical effect affecting it. The effect makes a Constitution saving throw against DC 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier.
If a spell created the effect, use its caster's spellcasting ability modifier for the save. If it has no identifiable caster, use a modifier equal to the effect's level, or +5 if it has no level.

On a failed save, choose one: suppress the effect until the start of your next turn; end it if its spell level is no greater than half your Pugilist level, rounded down; or remove one magical restraint, barrier, transformation, or defensive benefit affecting the target. This costs no Moxie.
