These effects can't deal damage, restore Hit Points, remove conditions, or replace a spell that would normally be required for a larger magical effect.

entries.name: Beacon of Hope
entries: A willing creature within 10 feet of the affected weapon can always tell which direction the weapon is in while it remains within 300 feet.
The wielder can suppress or restore this effect at any time.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: At character level 5, the extra Radiant damage becomes {@damage 2d8}.

At character level 11, the extra Radiant damage becomes {@damage 3d8}. Once on each of your turns when at least one Radiant damage die from this spell triggers Overflowing Light, the wielder can immediately expend 1 Radiance without reducing its stored Radiance.

At character level 17, the extra Radiant damage becomes {@damage 4d8}. Against a creature below half its Hit Point maximum, the affected weapon scores a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20, and every point of Radiance spent on Burn, Mend, or Ward produces two dice instead of one. In addition, whenever Judgment of Dawn triggers, the wielder can immediately make one additional attack with the affected weapon against a creature within its reach or range. This attack requires no Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction and can't trigger another additional attack from this feature during the same turn.

entries.name: Everlasting Dawn
entries: At character level 17, whenever the affected weapon reduces a hostile creature to 0 Hit Points, this spell's duration resets to 1 minute.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Gate
entries: You possess a key to doors that were never built.
You create a supernatural object called your Gate Key. It can take any form you choose—a key, coin, card, ring, shard, or similar Tiny object.
If the Gate Key is lost or destroyed, you can recreate it during a Short or Long Rest, causing the previous Gate Key to disappear.

entries.name: Open the Way
entries: As a Bonus Action while holding your Gate Key, choose an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet.
You create two linked gateways: one in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you and one at the chosen destination. Each gateway is a vertical opening up to 5 feet wide and 10 feet tall.
The gateways last until the start of your next turn. A creature or object entering one gateway immediately exits the other, preserving its direction and momentum.
Passing through a gateway isn't considered teleportation.

entries.name: Reach Through
entries: You can see and hear through either gateway.
You can make attacks, cast spells, interact with objects, and move through the gateways using normal movement.
Distance measured through the gateways is measured from one opening to the other as though the two openings were adjacent.

entries.name: Moving Gate
entries: Once on each of your turns while the gateways exist, you can move either gateway up to 10 feet to another unoccupied space you can see. This requires no action.

items: {@b Level 5.} The maximum distance of Open the Way increases to 60 feet.
{@b Level 11.} The maximum distance increases to 120 feet, and the gateways can also be horizontal.

{@b Level 17.} The maximum distance increases to 300 feet. You create three gateways instead of two, and any gateway can connect to either of the others. A creature entering a gateway chooses which other gateway it exits from.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Mirror
entries: Your reflection has learned that it need not remain on the other side of the glass.
You create a supernatural Pact Mirror, a Tiny reflective object whose appearance you choose, such as a hand mirror, polished coin, crystal shard, metal plate, or glass eye.
If it is lost or destroyed, you can recreate it during a Short or Long Rest, causing the previous Pact Mirror to disappear.

entries.name: Living Reflection
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can cause your reflection to step out of the Pact Mirror and appear in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet.

The reflection looks and sounds exactly like you, occupies its space, has your Size, is intangible, can't attack, manipulate objects, or directly affect creatures, and has a Speed equal to your Speed.
It can move through creatures and objects as Difficult Terrain and disappears if it ends its turn inside an object.
You can have only one Living Reflection at a time. It lasts until dismissed, you create another, you become Incapacitated, or it is more than 300 feet away from you.

entries.name: Borrowed Position
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can instantly exchange positions with your Living Reflection.
This movement isn't teleportation. Your body and the reflection simply exchange which position each occupies.
You can use Borrowed Position a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Mirror Casting
entries: When you cast a spell or use an ability that originates from you, you can choose for it to originate from your space or your Living Reflection's space.
You still make all attacks, choose all targets, and provide all components normally. Range is measured from the chosen origin.
The reflection itself isn't considered the caster or user of the effect.

entries.name: False Target
entries: When a creature you can see targets you with an attack, you can use your Reaction to exchange places with your Living Reflection immediately before the attack is resolved.
The attack then targets whichever of you now occupies your former space.
Because the reflection is intangible, an attack directed at it automatically misses unless the effect can affect incorporeal magical manifestations.
Using False Target expends one use of Borrowed Position.

entries.name: Through the Looking Glass
entries: While your Living Reflection exists, you can see and hear from its space in addition to your own.
You can perceive through it even if you don't have line of sight to it, provided it remains within 300 feet of you.

items: {@b Level 5.} Your Living Reflection can exist up to 1 mile from you.
{@b Level 11.} You can maintain two Living Reflections simultaneously. When using Borrowed Position or Mirror Casting, choose either reflection.
{@b Level 17.} You can maintain three Living Reflections, and once on each of your turns you can exchange positions with one of them without expending a use of Borrowed Position.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Arsenal
entries: You carry no arsenal upon your back. Steel, ammunition, and instruments of battle wait beyond ordinary space for the instant you call.
Every weapon entrusted to the Arsenal remembers your hand.
Disarm you, and another blade appears. Empty your quiver, and another arrow is already nocked.
So long as the Arsenal answers, you are never truly unarmed.
You possess a supernatural extradimensional armory called your Arsenal.

entries.name: Bound Arsenal
entries: During a Short or Long Rest, you can place any number of weapons, shields, ammunition, spellcasting focuses, and tools you are touching into the Arsenal.
You can also place an eligible object into the Arsenal as a Bonus Action while holding it.

An object stored there has no weight or bulk for you, is inaccessible to other creatures through ordinary means, doesn't age, rust, decay, or deteriorate while stored, retains its magical properties, charges, and other characteristics, and remains attuned to its current wielder if storing it wouldn't normally end that Attunement.
You always know every object currently stored in your Arsenal. There is no inherent limit to the number of eligible objects it can contain.

entries.name: Call to Hand
entries: Once on each of your turns, you can summon one stored object directly into an empty hand without using an action.
You can simultaneously return one eligible object you are holding to the Arsenal.
If you have no free hand, you can instead cause the summoned object to appear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

entries.name: Instant Exchange
entries: Whenever you make an attack with a weapon from your Arsenal, you can return it and summon another stored weapon into the same hand before or after that attack, no action required.
You can therefore wield different weapons for different attacks made during the same turn.

entries.name: Unbroken Armament
entries: A weapon from your Arsenal recognizes you as its intended wielder. While you wield it, you are proficient with it and you can't be unwillingly disarmed of it unless you are Incapacitated.
If it leaves your grasp unwillingly, you can immediately return it to the Arsenal, no action required.
A weapon you throw can return to the Arsenal immediately after the attack resolves.
This doesn't override an Artifact or another item's property that specifically determines who can wield or possess it.

entries.name: Arsenal Ammunition
entries: Ammunition stored in the Arsenal can appear directly inside a weapon as part of loading or firing that weapon.
You don't need a free hand to retrieve ammunition from the Arsenal.
After ammunition from the Arsenal hits or misses, you can cause it to return to the Arsenal at the end of the turn if it still exists.

entries.name: Familiar Grip
entries: While wielding a weapon from your Arsenal, you can use Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls, regardless of which ability that weapon normally uses.
This doesn't change any other property of the weapon.

entries.name: Level 2 — Arsenal Enhancement
entries: Every weapon in your Arsenal gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls while you wield it.
This bonus becomes +2 at 7th level and +3 at 13th level.
If a weapon already grants a bonus to its attack or damage rolls from being a Magic Item, use the higher bonus rather than adding the bonuses together.

entries.name: Level 5 — Awakened Arsenal
entries: Every weapon in your Arsenal is considered magical while you wield it.
Whenever you summon a weapon using Call to Hand, you can immediately alter its handling until it leaves your grasp. Choose one of the following options:

items: {@b Swift.} If the weapon lacks the Finesse property, it gains Finesse.
{@b Far-Reaching.} If it is a melee weapon, its reach increases by 5 feet.
{@b Returning.} If it has the Thrown property, its normal and long ranges are doubled, and it returns to your hand immediately after the attack.
{@b Unburdened.} The weapon loses the Heavy property for you.

entries: You choose again whenever that weapon is summoned.

entries.name: Extra Attack
entries: Starting at 5th level, you can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

entries.name: Level 11 — Arsenal Without Pause
entries: You can summon or return any number of objects from your Arsenal during your turn, provided each exchange occurs immediately before or after you make an attack, cast a spell, or interact with an object.

You can summon or dismiss a Shield as part of these exchanges. Changing weapons never interferes with making multiple attacks. A weapon you summon is immediately ready to use, including loaded ammunition if appropriate.
You can summon a spellcasting focus from the Arsenal as part of casting a spell and return it immediately afterward.

entries.name: Arsenal Reach
entries: When you make a weapon attack, you can cause the weapon to emerge from the Arsenal at a point you can see within 30 feet of you.
Make the attack as though you occupied that point for determining the attack's reach and line of attack.
After the attack resolves, the weapon immediately returns to your Arsenal or your hand.
You can use Arsenal Reach once per turn.

entries.name: Level 17 — Endless Armory
entries: Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with a weapon from your Arsenal, you can make one additional weapon attack with a different stored weapon as part of the same Action.
This additional attack requires no Action or Bonus Action.

entries.name: Rain of Steel
entries: Once per Long Rest, you can use an Action to open the Arsenal around yourself.
Choose any number of creatures you can see within 60 feet, up to your Proficiency Bonus.
For each chosen creature, select a weapon currently stored in your Arsenal and make one weapon attack against that creature with the selected weapon.
A weapon can be used for only one of these attacks.
After all attacks resolve, every weapon used immediately returns to the Arsenal.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Vessel
entries: Magic need not be spent when it is cast. Some power can be caught, sealed, and taught to wait.

You create a supernatural container called your Pact Vessel. Its form is your choice: a bottle, lantern, gemstone, scroll case, orb, reliquary, card, ring, or another Tiny object capable of symbolically containing something.
If the Vessel is lost or destroyed, you can recreate it during a Short or Long Rest. Creating a new Vessel causes the previous one to disappear, but any magic stored within it is preserved.

entries.name: Seal a Spell
entries: When you cast a spell with a casting time of an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, you can choose to seal the spell inside your Pact Vessel instead of producing its normal effect.

The spell is cast normally: a spell slot is expended normally, Material components are provided and consumed normally, and any other resources required by the spell are expended normally. The spell produces no effect when sealed.
The Vessel can hold one sealed spell at a time. You can't seal a spell whose level is higher than the maximum shown by Deepening Vessel.

entries.name: Release the Spell
entries: While holding your Pact Vessel, you can release a sealed spell using the same type of action required by the spell's normal casting time.

When released, no spell slot is expended and no Material components are required again. You make all targeting and other choices at the moment of release, and range and area are measured from the releaser's current position.
The spell uses the same spellcasting ability, spell save DC, and spell attack bonus it had when sealed, and it counts as being cast by the creature that originally sealed it.
Once released, the spell disappears from the Vessel.

entries.name: Held Casting
entries: A sealed spell remains in the Vessel until it is released, replaced, or willingly erased. There is no time limit on how long it can remain sealed, and finishing a rest doesn't remove it.

entries.name: Pass the Vessel
entries: Another creature can hold your Pact Vessel and release a spell stored within it.
When it does so, the spell still uses the original caster's spellcasting statistics and treats the creature releasing it as the point of origin.
The creature doesn't need to know the spell or possess spellcasting.
If the spell requires Concentration, the creature that released the spell maintains that Concentration.

entries.name: Replace the Contents
entries: If you seal another spell while the Vessel already contains one, you can choose to erase the existing spell and replace it. The erased spell and resources originally spent to cast it aren't refunded.

entries.name: Level 5 — Greater Vessel
entries: You can seal spells of 2nd level or lower.
Your Vessel can now hold two spells simultaneously. When you seal a spell, choose which space within the Vessel contains it.

entries.name: Level 11 — Vault of Spells
entries: You can seal spells of 4th level or lower, and your Vessel can hold three spells simultaneously.
when a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell of a level you can store, you can use your Reaction to attempt to capture it.
Make an ability check using your spellcasting ability against a DC equal to 10 + the spell's level. On a success, the spell is sealed inside an empty space in your Vessel instead of taking effect.
The original caster still expends the spell slot and any components normally.
Once you successfully capture a spell this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 17 — Endless Vessel
entries: You can seal spells of 6th level or lower, and your Vessel can hold five spells simultaneously.

items: {@b Swift Release.} Once on each of your turns, when you release a spell with a casting time of an Action, you can release it as a Bonus Action instead.
{@b Perfect Capture.} When you use your Reaction to capture a spell of 6th level or lower, you no longer make an ability check. The spell is automatically sealed if your Vessel has an empty space.
{@b Overflow.} If your Vessel is full when you successfully capture a spell, you can immediately erase one stored spell to make room for the captured one.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Brand
entries: Some marks are written on flesh. Yours is written on certainty.
Once you have claimed a creature with your Brand, distance becomes less useful, concealment less reliable, and escape increasingly difficult.
You gain the ability to place a supernatural mark called your Pact Brand upon another creature.

entries.name: Place the Brand
entries: As a Bonus Action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet.
The creature becomes Branded by you until you dismiss the Brand, you Brand another creature, or the creature dies.
You can have only one Branded creature at a time.
The Brand can appear visibly on the creature in a form you choose, or remain completely invisible.
Placing the Brand doesn't require a saving throw and doesn't by itself Charm, damage, or otherwise control the creature.

entries.name: Hunter's Certainty
entries: While the Branded creature is on the same plane of existence as you, you always know its direction from you, its approximate distance from you, whether it is conscious or unconscious, and whether it is currently moving.
The creature gains no indication that you are sensing this information.

entries.name: Marked Beyond Sight
entries: You can perceive the Branded creature even when it is Invisible, Heavily Obscured, Hidden from you, or behind ordinary walls or other physical cover.
This doesn't allow you to see the surrounding area through those obstructions. You simply perceive the creature's exact position as a supernatural outline.
The Brand doesn't grant line of effect through barriers.

entries.name: Claim the Opening
entries: Once on each of your turns when you deal damage to the Branded creature, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Force or Psychic damage, your choice.
You choose the damage type each time.

entries.name: Refuse Escape
entries: When the Branded creature willingly teleports or otherwise instantly moves to another space within 120 feet of you, you can use your Reaction to immediately move to an unoccupied space within 10 feet of it.
This movement isn't teleportation, and you don't provoke Opportunity Attacks from this movement.

entries.name: Level 5 — Relentless Mark
entries: Claim the Opening increases to {@damage 1d8}.
The Branded creature gains no benefit against you from being Invisible.
You can target it with attacks and effects that require you to see the target as long as your Brand allows you to perceive its exact position.

entries.name: Level 11 — Unbroken Pursuit
entries: You can maintain Brands on two creatures simultaneously.
When you use Place the Brand while already at this limit, choose which existing Brand ends.
Refuse Escape can trigger when a Branded creature teleports or instantly moves from anywhere within 300 feet of you.
When you follow it, you can appear within 5 feet of the creature instead of 10 feet.

entries.name: Level 17 — No Refuge
entries: You can maintain Brands on up to three creatures simultaneously.
Your Brand functions across planar boundaries. You always know which plane each Branded creature occupies.

entries.name: Follow Anywhere
entries: When a Branded creature teleports, travels to another plane, or is magically transported elsewhere, you can use your Reaction to follow it.
You appear in the nearest safe unoccupied space within 10 feet of the creature, even if doing so crosses planar boundaries.

entries.name: Final Claim
entries: Claim the Opening increases to {@damage 2d8}.
Once on each of your turns when you damage a Branded creature, you can also choose one of the following effects:

items: {@b Hamper.} Its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
{@b Expose.} It can't benefit from Half Cover or Three-Quarters Cover against you until the start of your next turn.

{@b Anchor.} Until the start of your next turn, if it attempts to teleport or travel to another plane, you immediately know and can use Follow Anywhere even if you would normally be unable to perceive the attempt.

optionalfeature.name: Living Margins
entries: The words in your tome have grown restless.
Ink crawls between paragraphs. Pages turn without wind. When commanded, fragments of the book tear themselves free—not as paper, but as living extensions of the knowledge written within.
Your Pact Tome can manifest supernatural Living Pages that act as extensions of yourself.

entries.name: Awaken the Pages
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can cause a number of spectral pages equal to your Proficiency Bonus to emerge from your Pact Tome.
The Living Pages remain until you dismiss them, your Pact Tome ceases to exist, or you are Incapacitated.
They can appear as parchment, floating runes, strips of glowing text, black sheets covered in shifting script, or another form appropriate to your Tome.
The pages aren't creatures and can't be targeted or damaged individually.

entries.name: Wandering Script
entries: As part of your movement on your turn, you can move the Living Pages up to 60 feet to a point you can see.

items: They can fly and hover.
They can pass through spaces as narrow as 1 inch.
They can turn pages, open unlocked doors, pull levers, and perform simple object interactions.
They can carry unattended objects weighing no more than 10 pounds per Living Page.
They can write, erase, copy, or arrange ordinary text.
They can retrieve or return objects to you.

entries: You perceive the exact location of every Living Page.

entries.name: Eyes Between the Lines
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can perceive through any one of your Living Pages until the start of your next turn.
While doing so, you can see and hear from its position as though you occupied its space.
You retain awareness of your own surroundings.
A Living Page has Darkvision out to 60 feet for this purpose.

entries.name: Spell Through the Page
entries: When you cast a spell with a range other than Self, you can choose one Living Page within 60 feet as the spell's point of origin.
You still cast the spell and provide all components normally.
Range, areas of effect, and lines of effect are measured from the chosen Living Page.
If the spell requires you to see a target, you must be able to see it either normally or through that Living Page.
After originating a spell in this way, that Living Page disappears.

entries.name: Hand of the Tome
entries: When you cast a spell with a range of Touch, one Living Page can deliver it to a creature or object within 5 feet of that page.
The page disappears after delivering the spell.

entries.name: Written Relay
entries: You can write a message of up to 25 words into your Pact Tome and send one Living Page to a creature you know.
The page travels toward that creature by the most direct route it can navigate at a flying speed of 120 feet.
When it reaches the creature, your message appears upon the page in whatever language you wrote it.
The recipient can write a response of up to 25 words, after which the page returns to you.
There is no fixed maximum distance, but the page can't cross planar boundaries.

optionalfeature.name: Scripted Recursion
entries: Some spells are written to be cast once.
Yours are written to remember the shape of their own casting.
Your Pact Tome can preserve a magical pattern after you cast it, allowing the book to reproduce that spell again.

entries.name: Record the Casting
entries: When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher using a spell slot, you can cause your Pact Tome to record that exact casting as a Recursion Script.

The script records the spell, the level at which it was cast, any choices made as part of the spell that are determined when casting it, and the spellcasting ability, spell save DC, and spell attack bonus used.
The script doesn't record targets, locations, or directions unless the spell itself permanently requires those choices when cast.
You can have only one Recursion Script recorded at a time. Recording a new one erases the old script.

entries.name: Recast the Script
entries: While holding your Pact Tome, you can cast the recorded spell from the Recursion Script without expending a spell slot or providing any components.
You choose targets, points of origin, directions, and other choices that are normally made at the moment of casting.
The spell is cast at the same level stored in the script.
Once you use the Recursion Script, it disappears.

entries.name: Persistent Formula
entries: A Recursion Script remains in your Pact Tome until you use it, replace it, or willingly erase it.
Finishing a Short or Long Rest doesn't remove it.
The script also survives the destruction or recreation of your Pact Tome and reappears within the recreated Tome.

entries.name: Level 11 — Double Script
entries: You can maintain two Recursion Scripts at once.
Each script can hold a different spell or a different casting of the same spell.
when you cast a spell recorded in one of your scripts using a spell slot normally, you can choose to refresh that script with the new casting instead of erasing it.

entries.name: Level 15 — Perfect Repetition
entries: When you use a Recursion Script, roll a d6.
On a 5 or 6, the script isn't erased.
You can immediately use it again later.
A script preserved this way can continue to preserve itself repeatedly.

entries.name: Level 17 — Recursive Chain
entries: You can maintain three Recursion Scripts at once.
Once on each of your turns, when you cast a spell from a Recursion Script with a casting time of an Action, you can immediately begin a Recursive Chain.
If you cast a different spell before the end of your next turn, you can choose to record that spell into the script you just consumed instead of losing the script completely.
The newly recorded spell can be of any level you are normally capable of casting.

entries.name: Level 19 — The Tome Casts Again
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you cast a spell from a Recursion Script, you can command the Tome to reproduce the script without consuming it.
The spell is cast normally from the script, but the Recursion Script remains intact automatically.
If Scripted Recursion would already preserve the script from another effect, that doesn't grant an additional casting.

optionalfeature.name: Unwritten Chapter
entries: There are pages in your tome that were never written.
They wait for knowledge you don't possess.
When need becomes great enough, the empty page supplies its own answer.
Your Pact Tome contains a supernatural section called the Unwritten Chapter.

entries.name: Write the Unknown
entries: When you finish a Long Rest, choose one spell from any spell list.
The spell appears within your Pact Tome as though written there by an unseen hand.
The spell remains in the Unwritten Chapter until you replace it after another Long Rest.
You don't need to have previously seen, learned, prepared, or encountered the spell.

entries.name: Borrowed Formula
entries: While the spell remains written in your Unwritten Chapter, you can cast it using any spell slots you possess of the appropriate level.
The spell counts as prepared for you.
It doesn't need to belong to any spell list normally available to you.
You use your normal spellcasting ability for it.
You can cast it at higher levels normally if you have higher-level spell slots.
You provide the spell's components normally.

entries.name: The Tome Understands
entries: The Unwritten Chapter contains enough supernatural instruction for you to cast its spell correctly even if you don't understand its original magical tradition.
For example, the Tome could contain a divine prayer, primal invocation, occult formula, or arcane theorem without requiring you to adopt the tradition it came from.
The spell remains the spell it normally is; the Tome simply gives you a usable formula for it.

entries.name: Level 13 — Two Answers
entries: Your Unwritten Chapter can contain two spells at the same time.
When you finish a Long Rest, you can replace either or both.

entries.name: Level 17 — Forbidden Chapter
entries: Your Unwritten Chapter can contain three spells at the same time.
When you finish a Long Rest, you can replace any or all of them.

entries.name: Level 19 — The Missing Spell
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you encounter a problem and realize that a particular spell would solve it, you can use a Bonus Action to immediately replace one spell in your Unwritten Chapter with another spell of your choice.
You don't need to finish a Long Rest.
The newly written spell is immediately available to cast.
You can do this even during combat.

optionalfeature.name: Pages of Appraisal
entries: The tome doesn't merely record what something appears to be.
It watches. Compares. Corrects.
Every action becomes another line of evidence, until disguise gives way to understanding.
Your Pact Tome can create supernatural dossiers on creatures you encounter.

entries.name: Open a Dossier
entries: As a Bonus Action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet.
A page in your Pact Tome becomes dedicated to that creature as its Dossier.
You can maintain a number of Dossiers equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If you exceed this limit, choose one existing Dossier to erase.
A Dossier remains until you erase it, even if the creature dies or leaves your plane of existence.

entries.name: Initial Appraisal
entries: When you create a Dossier, the Tome immediately records the creature's creature type, Size, current and maximum Hit Points, Armor Class, Speeds, senses, languages it can speak, damage Vulnerabilities, Resistances, and Immunities, and condition Immunities.
The creature isn't aware that this information has been recorded.

entries.name: Observed Truth
entries: Whenever a creature with a Dossier uses a trait, action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell, supernatural ability, Legendary Action, or similar feature that you can perceive, the Tome permanently records that feature.

The entry includes enough information for you to understand what the feature does, its range and area, its damage or healing, its saving throw or attack roll if any, its recharge or usage limitation, whether it requires Concentration, and any trigger or condition required to use it.
You don't need to spend an action reading a feature already recorded by the Tome; you can recall its contents perfectly.

entries.name: Updating Record
entries: While a creature with a Dossier is within 120 feet of you, its page updates automatically.
You always know its current Hit Points, current conditions, whether it is concentrating, and whether it has expended or regained a feature already recorded in the Dossier.
The Tome doesn't reveal a feature it has never observed merely because that feature exists.

entries.name: Level 9 — Read the Pattern
entries: After observing a creature with a Dossier for at least 1 round, the Tome also records its Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, its saving throw bonuses, its skill proficiencies and bonuses, its Proficiency Bonus, and its spellcasting ability, spell save DC, and spell attack bonus, if any.
whenever the creature casts a spell you can perceive, the Tome records the spell's name and level before its effects resolve.

entries.name: Level 13 — Predictive Annotation
entries: Your Tome begins predicting behavior from everything it has recorded.
Once on each of your turns when you make an attack roll against a creature with a Dossier, you can gain Advantage on that roll.
Alternatively, when that creature makes a saving throw against one of your spells or abilities, you can impose Disadvantage on that saving throw.
You can use only one of these benefits per turn.

entries.name: Level 17 — Complete Dossier
entries: After you have observed a creature with a Dossier for at least 1 minute, the Tome completes its analysis.

It reveals every currently existing trait, action, spell, reaction, resistance, immunity, vulnerability, transformation, resource, and other game feature possessed by that creature, including those you haven't personally witnessed.

It also reveals which features are currently available or expended, any alternate forms it possesses, the conditions required to activate those forms or features, any regeneration, resurrection, or death-prevention abilities it possesses, and any specific method described in its statistics for bypassing, suppressing, or defeating one of its features.

entries.name: Exploit the Margin
entries: Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature whose Dossier is complete, you can choose one damage type dealt by that attack, spell, or effect.
For that instance of damage, the creature's Resistance to that damage type is ignored.
If it is Immune instead, treat that Immunity as Resistance for that instance.
This doesn't permanently alter the creature's defenses.

optionalfeature.name: Stolen Footnote
entries: Not every secret is a spell.
Some are written in muscle, blood, instinct, training, divinity, monstrous anatomy, or stranger things.
Your tome has never cared about the distinction.
Your Pact Tome can record a feature possessed or used by another creature and preserve it as a Stolen Footnote.

entries.name: Cite the Ability
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet uses or visibly demonstrates a feature, you can use your Reaction to record that feature in your Pact Tome after its use resolves. A passive or continuous feature can be recorded when you directly observe its effect or otherwise learn that the creature possesses it.

You can record a trait, Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell, Spellcasting feature, class feature, species feature, monster feature, Legendary Action, Lair Action, Mythic Action, Multiattack, transformation, movement mode, sense, aura, regeneration, resistance, immunity, vulnerability, or another game feature or statistic with a defined mechanical effect.
The Tome records the chosen feature as it exists for that creature. You don't need to understand how the creature performs it.
You can maintain one Stolen Footnote at a time. Recording another replaces the previous one.

entries.name: Use the Footnote
entries: While holding your Pact Tome, you can use the recorded feature as though it appeared among your own features.

If the feature normally uses an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, you use the same type of action. If it uses a special action economy you don't possess, such as a Legendary Action, Lair Action, or Mythic Action, you use it as a Bonus Action instead unless the feature itself already requires an Action or Reaction.

If the feature is passive or continuous, you can invoke it as a Bonus Action and gain its benefits for 1 minute, or until you are Incapacitated. If the feature represents a movement mode, sense, resistance, immunity, vulnerability, aura, regeneration, Armor Class calculation, or similar continuous statistic, it functions for that duration exactly as recorded, using the adaptations described below when necessary.

If the feature is a spell or Spellcasting feature, you can use it without needing the original creature's class, spell list, spellbook, focus, or other unique spellcasting structure. Any spell slot or unique resource supplied by the recorded feature is provided by the Footnote for that use. Components required by a spell are still required unless the recorded feature itself ignores them.
After you use or invoke the Stolen Footnote, it disappears from the Tome unless another part of this invocation preserves it.

entries.name: Translate the Feature
entries: Your Tome translates the recorded feature into a form you can perform. You don't need the anatomy, species, creature type, class, size, equipment, lair, legendary status, transformation, or physical structure normally required to use it.

The Tome creates a magical analogue whenever necessary. Spectral wings can perform a wing attack, spectral jaws can reproduce a bite, runes can reproduce a gaze, the Tome can supply a monstrous roar, and an effect tied to a lair can manifest from the Tome or the space around you.
If the feature requires an attack roll, use your spell attack modifier unless the recorded feature specifies another fixed bonus.
If it requires a saving throw, use your spell save DC unless the recorded feature specifies another fixed DC.

If it uses the original creature's ability modifier, Proficiency Bonus, level, Hit Dice, or similar personal statistic to calculate a number, use your corresponding statistic when possible. If no corresponding statistic exists, use your spellcasting ability modifier, your Proficiency Bonus, or your character level, whichever most closely matches the original calculation.

If the feature creates or depends on an object, body part, weapon, organ, limb, terrain element, or other prerequisite you don't possess, the Tome can manifest a temporary magical analogue that exists only for the feature's duration.
Copying a feature doesn't permanently change your creature type, body, statistics, class, species, or identity unless the feature itself explicitly changes one of those things.

entries.name: Everything Can Be Cited
entries: Stolen Footnote isn't limited by the origin of a feature. If it has a defined game effect and belongs to or is used by a creature you can observe, the Tome can record it.

This includes passive defenses, supernatural anatomy, special senses, alternate forms, innate spellcasting, entire activated traits, Legendary and Mythic features, and abilities that would normally be impossible for your body to reproduce.

If a recorded entry contains several linked effects as one feature, such as Multiattack or a transformation that grants a package of abilities, the Footnote records the complete feature rather than only one sentence from it.

entries.name: Level 13 — Two Footnotes
entries: Your Pact Tome can hold two Stolen Footnotes simultaneously. They can come from the same creature or different creatures.

If a recorded feature normally has limited uses, a Recharge roll, Legendary Action cost, Mythic requirement, or a resource unique to its original creature, your single use of the Stolen Footnote supplies that requirement automatically. You don't need the original creature's resource.

entries.name: Level 17 — Perfect Citation
entries: Your Tome can hold three Stolen Footnotes simultaneously.
When you use or invoke a Stolen Footnote, roll a d6. On a 5 or 6, the Footnote remains in your Tome instead of disappearing.

entries.name: Rewrite the Scale
entries: When you use a recorded feature, you can calculate any damage, healing, range, area, number of targets, or similar value that normally scales from the original creature's CR, level, Hit Dice, Proficiency Bonus, or similar progression using your character level or Proficiency Bonus instead, using the nearest equivalent progression represented by the feature.
If the feature doesn't scale, it remains unchanged.

entries.name: Level 19 — Plagiarism Perfected
entries: Once per Long Rest, when a creature you can see within 120 feet uses or reveals an eligible feature, you can record it without using your Reaction.
You can then immediately use or invoke that Stolen Footnote as part of the same trigger, provided the recorded feature can meaningfully function at that moment.
Doing so doesn't erase another Footnote if you have an empty Footnote slot.

optionalfeature.name: Wellspring of the Tome
entries: Every spell leaves something behind.
Power gathers between the lines, beneath the ink, and within the spaces no reader notices.
As the tome deepens, those remnants cease to be traces.
They become an entire second reservoir of magic.
Your Pact Tome develops its own reserve of magical power, granting you additional spell slots called Tome Slots.

entries.name: Tome Slots
entries: Tome Slots are additional spell slots separate from those granted by your classes, species, feats, magic items, or other features.
You can expend a Tome Slot whenever you would normally expend a spell slot.
A Tome Slot can also be used to upcast a spell normally.
You regain all expended Tome Slots when you finish a Long Rest.
Destroying, dismissing, or recreating your Pact Tome doesn't restore expended Tome Slots.

entries.name: Level 5 — First Reservoir
entries: You gain one 1st-level Tome Slot, one 2nd-level Tome Slot, and one 3rd-level Tome Slot.

entries.name: Level 9 — Deep Reservoir
entries: You additionally gain one 4th-level Tome Slot and one 5th-level Tome Slot.
You now have one additional spell slot of every level from 1st through 5th.

entries.name: Level 13 — Greater Reservoir
entries: You additionally gain one 6th-level Tome Slot and one 7th-level Tome Slot.
You now have one additional spell slot of every level from 1st through 7th.

entries.name: Level 17 — Endless Reservoir
entries: You additionally gain one 8th-level Tome Slot and one 9th-level Tome Slot.
You now have one additional spell slot of every level from 1st through 9th.

entries.name: Reflow the Ink
entries: When you finish a Short Rest, you can restore expended Tome Slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed your Proficiency Bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier.
For example, with a Proficiency Bonus of +6 and a spellcasting ability modifier of +5, you could restore up to 11 total levels of Tome Slots.
Once you use Reflow the Ink, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 19 — Overflowing Archive
entries: You gain a second Tome Slot of each of the following levels: 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th.

entries.name: Bottomless Page
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you expend a Tome Slot of 6th level or higher, you can cause the Tome to restore that slot immediately after the spell resolves.
You choose to use Bottomless Page after the spell resolves.

optionalfeature.name: Ascending Formula
entries: Most spell formulas end exactly where the power invested in them ends.
Your tome has learned to keep writing.
One more line. One more circle. One more impossible step beyond what the spell slot should have been able to sustain.
While holding your Pact Tome, you can use its accumulated knowledge to cast spells at a higher level than the spell slot you expend.

entries.name: Overcast
entries: When you cast a spell using a spell slot, you can cause your Pact Tome to increase the spell's effective spell level by 1.

For example, a spell cast using a 2nd-level slot functions as though cast with a 3rd-level slot, a spell cast using a 4th-level slot functions as though cast with a 5th-level slot, and a spell cast using an 8th-level slot functions as though cast with a 9th-level slot.
You still expend only the original spell slot.

The spell uses its increased level for all purposes, including At Higher Levels effects, damage and healing scaling, number of targets, duration or area increases, interactions with effects that check spell level, and any other feature that checks the spell's level.
Overcast can't increase a spell beyond 9th level unless Formula Beyond Measure specifically allows otherwise.
You can use Overcast a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 11 — Deep Formula
entries: When you use Overcast, you can increase the spell's effective level by up to 2 levels instead of 1.
Using either a +1 or +2 increase expends only one use of Overcast.
For example, a spell cast using a 3rd-level slot can function as though cast using a 5th-level slot.

entries.name: Level 15 — Efficient Ascension
entries: Once on each of your turns when you use Overcast to increase a spell by only 1 level, roll a d6 after the spell resolves.
On a 4–6, the use of Overcast isn't expended.
This doesn't restore the spell slot.

entries.name: Excess Formula
entries: If a spell has no benefit from being cast at one of the intermediate levels you pass through, that doesn't prevent you from Overcasting it.
For example, a spell that gains a new effect only at 6th level can be cast using a 4th-level slot and increased by 2 levels to gain that 6th-level benefit.

entries.name: Level 17 — Grand Overcast
entries: You can increase a spell by up to 3 levels with a single use of Overcast.
For example, a 3rd-level slot can produce a 6th-level casting, a 5th-level slot can produce an 8th-level casting, and a 6th-level slot can produce a 9th-level casting.
once per Long Rest, you can use Overcast without expending one of its uses.

entries.name: Level 19 — Formula Beyond Measure
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you cast a spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can invoke Formula Beyond Measure.
The spell is treated as though it were cast using a 9th-level spell slot, regardless of the slot actually expended.
This doesn't expend a use of Overcast.

entries.name: Overflow Beyond Ninth
entries: If you expend an actual 9th-level spell slot, you can instead use Formula Beyond Measure to treat the casting as 10th level solely for determining numerical or scalable effects that explicitly increase when cast using a higher-level spell slot.
This doesn't create a 10th-level spell, doesn't allow you to learn or cast spells above 9th level, and doesn't bypass restrictions that specifically require something other than spell level.
For example, a spell that deals one additional damage die for each slot level above its base level gains one additional step of scaling beyond its normal 9th-level casting.

optionalfeature.name: Condensed Formula
entries: Most spell formulas waste power.
Tradition calls the excess necessary. Your tome calls it poor notation.
Line by line, the formula contracts until the same miracle fits inside a smaller measure of magic.
Your Pact Tome can compress spells into more efficient forms, allowing you to cast them using lower-level spell slots without weakening the resulting spell.

entries.name: Spell Compression
entries: When you cast a spell of 2nd level or higher that is written in your Pact Tome, you can cast it using a spell slot 1 level lower than the spell's normal level.
The spell still functions as a spell of its original level.
For example, a 2nd-level spell can use a 1st-level slot, a 4th-level spell can use a 3rd-level slot, and a 7th-level spell can use a 6th-level slot.

For every purpose other than the slot actually expended, the spell retains its normal level. This includes damage and healing, saving throws and attack rolls, Counterspell and Dispel Magic interactions, effects that check the spell's level, Concentration, duration, area, and number of targets.
You can use Spell Compression a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
A spell can never be compressed below a 1st-level spell slot.

entries.name: Level 13 — Deep Compression
entries: You can reduce the required spell slot by up to 2 levels instead of 1.
For example, a 3rd-level spell can use a 1st-level slot, a 5th-level spell can use a 3rd-level slot, and a 9th-level spell can use a 7th-level slot.
Using either one or two levels of compression expends only one use.

entries.name: Compressed Upcasting
entries: You can also apply Spell Compression to an upcast spell.
Determine the level at which you want the spell to function, then reduce the slot actually expended.
For example, you could cast a 3rd-level spell as a 6th-level casting while expending only a 4th-level spell slot.
The spell functions as a 6th-level spell for all purposes.

entries.name: Level 17 — Perfect Compression
entries: You can reduce the required slot by up to 3 levels.
For example, a 4th-level spell can use a 1st-level slot, a 6th-level spell can use a 3rd-level slot, an 8th-level spell can use a 5th-level slot, and a 9th-level spell can use a 6th-level slot.
the first time after each Long Rest that you use Spell Compression, it doesn't expend one of your uses.

entries.name: Efficient Notation
entries: When you use Spell Compression and expend a spell slot of 3rd level or lower, roll a d6 after the spell resolves.
On a 5 or 6, the use of Spell Compression isn't expended.
The spell slot is still expended normally.

entries.name: Level 19 — Formula Without Waste
entries: Your mastery of compressed spellcraft becomes extreme.
Once per Long Rest, when you cast a spell written in your Pact Tome, you can use Perfect Formula.

entries.name: Perfect Formula
entries: Choose the level at which the spell will function, up to 9th level.
You expend a spell slot only half that level, rounded up.
The spell functions at its full chosen level for every purpose.
Perfect Formula doesn't expend a use of Spell Compression.

optionalfeature.name: Sovereign Armament
entries: Your pact weapon no longer behaves like an ordinary weapon enchanted by magic. It recognizes only one authority: yours. Its shape, balance, and method of killing rearrange themselves around your intent. In your hands, a single weapon can answer problems that would normally demand an entire arsenal.
Whenever you summon or bond with your Pact Weapon, you can cause it to take the form of any Simple or Martial melee or ranged weapon. You are proficient with every form it takes.

Changing its form requires no action, and you can do so immediately before or after any attack you make with it. A magical weapon bonded through Pact of the Blade retains its magical properties regardless of the form, unless a property logically requires its original form.

Whenever the weapon changes form, choose up to two of the following properties for it: Finesse, Light, Reach, Thrown (30/90), Two-Handed, or Versatile (1d10). If it already has a property you choose, choose another instead. You can also remove the Heavy property whenever you change its form.

While you wield it, the Pact Weapon ignores ordinary limitations of shape. You can use it even when its form would normally be impractical for your Size, and changing its form never causes you to drop it.
If the weapon requires ammunition, it creates the mundane ammunition needed for each attack as part of that attack. The ammunition disappears after the attack resolves.

entries.name: Level 5
entries: Your Pact Weapon gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls unless it already has an equal or greater bonus.
Whenever you hit with it, you can choose for the attack to deal Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, or Force damage regardless of the weapon's form.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: You can have three of the listed weapon properties on your Pact Weapon at the same time.
Immediately before each attack, you can independently change its form, damage type, and chosen weapon properties for that attack. Its inherent magical properties remain through these transformations.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: Your Pact Weapon gains a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls unless it already has an equal or greater bonus.
It can have any number of the listed weapon properties at the same time.
Its Reach increases by 5 feet.
Its normal and long ranges are doubled whenever it is in a ranged or Thrown form.
Its attacks ignore Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, and Force damage.
It can't be forcibly removed from your grasp while you are conscious.
If it leaves your hand, it can return to you immediately after the attack or effect resolves, requiring no action.

optionalfeature.name: Severing Edge
entries: Your pact weapon has learned to cut things that were never meant to possess an edge. A ward can be split. A curse can be opened. A spell can be wounded until its structure collapses. Where ordinary steel meets magic and stops, your weapon continues.
Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with your Pact Weapon, you can choose one spell or magical effect currently affecting that creature that you are aware of.

Make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a success, that spell or magical effect ends on the creature as though successfully dispelled. If the effect has no spell level, the GM determines an equivalent level for this purpose.

When your Pact Weapon damages a creature that is concentrating, the creature has Disadvantage on the Constitution saving throw it makes to maintain Concentration from that damage. If the attack is a Critical Hit, the creature instead automatically fails that Concentration saving throw.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: Your Pact Weapon can strike magical effects directly.
As an Action, you can make one attack with your Pact Weapon against a magical barrier, ward, conjured structure, magical restraint, magical portal, or similar magical manifestation you can perceive.

On a hit, choose one: deal the weapon's normal damage to the manifestation if it can take damage; make a spellcasting ability check against DC 10 + the effect's spell level to end it as though successfully dispelled; or suppress one of its magical properties until the start of your next turn.

If the effect has no spell level, the GM determines an equivalent level for the ability check. A manifestation with no AC has an AC equal to 10 + its spell level, or a value determined by the GM if it has no spell level.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you hit a creature or magical manifestation with your Pact Weapon, choose one magical effect affecting the target that you are aware of.
That effect ends immediately without an ability check if it was created by a spell of level 8 or lower.
For a 9th-level spell, Artifact, deity-created effect, or magic of comparable power, make a spellcasting ability check against DC 19 instead. On a success, the effect ends on that target.

optionalfeature.name: Spell-Eater
entries: Magic that fails to take hold of you doesn't simply disperse. You tear the dying spell from the Weave, swallow its structure whole, and keep it inside yourself until you decide what to do with it.

When a creature casts a spell of level 1 or higher that targets you or includes you in its area, you can use your Reaction to devour that spell after it fails to affect you because its spell attack misses you, you succeed on its saving throw and suffer no effect from it, or another feature causes the spell to have no effect on you.
You can keep one spell devoured this way at a time. Devouring another spell replaces the one you were already keeping. A spell you keep this way remains available until you finish a Long Rest.

While you are keeping a spell this way, you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You use your own spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC, use the level at which the spell was originally cast, and make any choices normally made by the caster.
You must still provide any Material component that has a listed cost or is consumed by the spell. After you cast the spell, you are no longer keeping it.

entries.name: Level 5
entries: You can devour a spell of up to 3rd level.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: You can devour a spell of up to 6th level.
You can keep up to two spells devoured this way at the same time.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: You can devour spells of any level.
You can keep up to three spells devoured this way at the same time.
When you successfully devour a spell that targets only you, you can cause it to be completely consumed. If it would normally produce a lingering effect after resolving, that effect isn't created.

optionalfeature.name: Unseen Dominion
entries: Your influence reaches farther than your hands ever could.

entries.name: Invisible Grasp
entries: You can manipulate unattended objects within 60 feet of you as though you were touching them. You can open doors, pull levers, draw or stow objects, use tools, pour liquids, and perform similar interactions remotely.
You use your normal Strength and Dexterity for anything that would require them.

Invisible Grasp doesn't require Concentration. Manipulating an object through it uses the same action economy as manipulating that object normally; an interaction that would require no Action at your reach requires no Action at range.

entries.name: Level 11 — Seize the Held
entries: As an Action, choose one object you can see within 60 feet that is being held or carried by a creature. The creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or the object is pulled from its grasp and flies to your hand or to an unoccupied space you choose within 5 feet of you.
A creature has Advantage on the save if the object is secured to its body.

entries.name: Level 17 — Dominion Without Distance
entries: The range of Invisible Grasp and Seize the Held becomes 300 feet.
you can use Invisible Grasp on objects you can see even if a transparent barrier separates you from them, provided there is a physical path the object could travel to reach you.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Crown
entries: Power is not always about force; sometimes it is about being obeyed.
Your words carry a weight that makes hesitation feel unnatural and defiance feel difficult.
Whether before a throne, across a battlefield, or in a dark alley, you speak as though obedience were already decided.

entries.name: Commanding Presence
entries: Instantaneous for each check.
Whenever you make a Charisma Check, you can treat a d20 roll of 7 or lower as an 8.
This applies to checks involving Deception, Intimidation, Performance, Persuasion, and any other Charisma Check.
This benefit is automatic and requires no Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction.

entries.name: Assume Command
entries: Until the end of the target's next turn.
When you speak to a creature that can understand you, you can issue a short, direct instruction as part of the same speech.
Issuing the command requires no Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction.
If the creature is not hostile, you have Advantage on the next Charisma Check you make to convince it to follow that instruction.
If the creature is hostile and within 60 feet, you can force it to make a Wisdom Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC.
On a failed save, the creature is compelled to follow the instruction you gave it until the end of its next turn.
It must use its movement, Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, and other available abilities as necessary to carry out the instruction to the best of its ability.

Your instruction can be anything reasonably expressible as a direct command, such as "Drop your weapon," "Run away," "Come here," "Stay still," "Protect me," "Attack him," "Tell me the truth," "Open the gate," "Get on your knees," or "Stop casting spells."
If the instruction becomes impossible to perform, the creature follows it as closely as reasonably possible.
A creature can be forced to make this Saving Throw through this Pact once per turn.

entries.name: The Voice That Carries
entries: For as long as you continue speaking.
Whenever you speak, you can choose for your voice to be heard clearly by any creatures you choose within 300 feet, even through loud noise.
You choose exactly which creatures hear you this way.
Speaking through this feature doesn't reveal your exact location unless the listener can already determine it.

entries.name: Level 5: Authority Takes Root
entries: Up to 1 minute for an extended command.
Your authority begins to linger after the initial command.
When a creature fails its Saving Throw against Assume Command, you can choose for the command to last for 1 minute instead of until the end of its next turn.
The creature repeats the Wisdom Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the command on a success.
For commands that can be completed immediately, the effect ends once the command has been fulfilled.
whenever you make a Charisma Check against a nonhostile creature that can hear you, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10 instead of 7 or lower as an 8.

entries.name: Level 9: Command the Many
entries: Your authority is no longer limited to a single listener.
When you use Assume Command, you can target a number of hostile creatures up to your Proficiency Bonus, provided each creature is within 60 feet of you, can hear you, and can understand you.
Each target makes its own Wisdom Saving Throw.
You can issue the same command to every target or give different commands to individual creatures.

Outside combat, when addressing a group or crowd that can hear you, you can make one Charisma Check for the group as a whole when resolving the same attempt against all of them, rather than making a separate check against each individual where appropriate.

entries.name: Level 13: Royal Decree
entries: Until the end of the target's next turn for a resisted decree.
Even successful resistance is no longer enough to escape your authority completely.
When a creature succeeds on its Saving Throw against Assume Command, you can choose one reasonable portion of the command you issued.
The creature must still obey that portion until the end of its next turn.
The chosen portion can't require the creature to spend its entire turn carrying out the command.

For example, "Drop your weapon and leave" can still force it to drop the weapon; "Stop casting and kneel" can still force it to stop casting spells; "Tell me everything and surrender" can still force it to answer one direct question truthfully to the best of its knowledge; and "Release him and attack your ally" can still force it to release the creature.
creatures that are Charmed or Frightened by you have Disadvantage on Saving Throws against Assume Command.

entries.name: Level 17: The Crown Is Absolute
entries: Up to 1 minute.
Your commands can become declarations that lesser wills struggle to escape.
Once per turn when you use Assume Command, you can declare the instruction to be an Absolute Command.

A creature that fails its Saving Throw against an Absolute Command doesn't repeat the Saving Throw at the end of its turns, remains compelled for the full 1 minute, and must continue carrying out the command until the command is completed, becomes impossible, or the duration ends.
An Absolute Command can contain more complex instructions than the short commands normally used with Assume Command.

For example, you could command: "Protect this person from everyone until the command ends," "Lead us through the fortress and don't betray us," "Fight beside me against your former allies," "Tell everyone here exactly what happened," "Prevent anyone from entering this room," or "Find the prisoner, release them, and bring them to me."
The creature uses its movement, Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, speech, objects, and other available abilities as necessary to fulfill the command to the best of its ability.
You can have only one Absolute Command active at a time.
If you create another Absolute Command while one is already active, the previous Absolute Command immediately ends.

optionalfeature.name: Edict of the Iron Throne
entries: The Crown no longer merely demands attention. Its commands begin to carry the weight of law.
You gain the following additional Decrees for your Pact of the Crown.

entries.name: Halt
entries: The creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or its Speed becomes 0 until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Drop
entries: The creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or immediately drop one object of your choice that it is holding. The object lands in its space.

entries.name: Level 11 — Obey
entries: You gain another Decree:

{@b Obey.} Choose one simple physical action the creature could immediately perform, such as move 10 feet, open that door, release that creature, stand up, or drop Prone. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or immediately perform that action if physically possible. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.
The Decree can't force a creature to directly damage itself.

entries.name: Level 17 — Imperial Edict
entries: Once per turn when a creature fails a saving throw against one of your Decrees, you can immediately issue a second different Decree to that creature without using an Action or Bonus Action.

optionalfeature.name: Threshold Without Warning
entries: Your gateways no longer merely connect two places. They begin to decide where motion itself is allowed to finish.
You gain the following improvements to your Pact of the Gate.

entries.name: Intercepting Gate
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of one of your gateways willingly moves at least 10 feet, you can use your Reaction to move one gateway into an unoccupied space along that creature's path immediately before it enters that space.
If the creature continues moving through the gateway, it exits from the linked gateway normally.

entries.name: Level 11 — Redirect the Blow
entries: When an attack or spell effect travels through one of your gateways and targets a creature, you can move the linked gateway up to 10 feet immediately before the attack or effect resolves.
This movement can change the point from which the attack or effect emerges, potentially changing line of sight, cover, or whether the original target is still valid.

entries.name: Level 17 — Sovereign Threshold
entries: Once on each of your turns, when a creature or object passes through one of your gateways, you can choose to:

items: Preserve its momentum normally.
Reduce its momentum to 0.
Redirect its movement in any direction as it exits.

entries: If a falling creature passes through one of your gateways, you can therefore cause it to exit without retaining its falling speed.

optionalfeature.name: Hold the Door
entries: Your gateways no longer flicker shut the moment their immediate purpose is fulfilled.
Once you open a path, you can hold it against the natural shape of space.
Those who travel through it do so because you have chosen to leave the door open.

entries.name: Held Threshold
entries: When you use Open the Way, you can choose to hold your gateways open. If you do, they last for 1 minute instead of until the start of your next turn.
The gateways end early if you dismiss them (no action required), you create a new set of gateways with Open the Way, or you become Incapacitated.
While the gateways remain open, you retain all benefits of Reach Through and Moving Gate.

entries.name: Keeper of Passage
entries: Whenever a creature you can see attempts to pass through one of your gateways, you can choose whether that gateway carries it to another gateway.
If you refuse passage, the creature doesn't pass through the gateway and its movement into the gateway's space is halted immediately before the opening. This requires no action from you.
You can make this choice separately for each creature each time it attempts to enter a gateway.

entries.name: Open for the Chosen
entries: When you create your gateways, you can designate any number of creatures you can see.
A designated creature can pass through your gateways even while Incapacitated, Grappled, or being carried, provided some part of it or the creature or object carrying it enters the gateway.
In addition, a willing designated creature can move through one of your gateways once on each of its turns without provoking Opportunity Attacks from that movement.

entries.name: The Door Makes Room
entries: Your held gateways can momentarily expand to accommodate those you permit to pass.

When you or a willing creature, or an unattended object, would enter one of your held gateways but is too large to fit through its normal opening, you can cause every gateway involved in that passage to expand just enough for it to pass.
This can accommodate a creature or object of up to Huge size.
The gateways return to their normal dimensions immediately after the passage is complete.
A creature or object can't emerge into a space that is too small to physically contain it; if there is no suitable space at the exit, it can't pass through that gateway.

entries.name: Level 11 — Door That Refuses to Close
entries: Your held gateways can last for 10 minutes.
Becoming Incapacitated no longer immediately ends them. Instead, they remain until the end of your next turn, giving you a chance to recover before they collapse.

entries.name: Level 17 — Permanent Invitation
entries: Your held gateways no longer have a maximum duration. They remain until you dismiss them, create another set of gateways, die, or are on a different plane from every gateway.
In addition, creatures you designated with Open for the Chosen can always identify which gateway they will emerge from before entering one.

optionalfeature.name: There Is Always Another Door
entries: A wall is only a door that has not been opened yet.
Distance matters less when you already know where the other side must be.
Where others see a sealed path, you see another threshold waiting to exist.
When you use Open the Way, you can place one of your gateways against a solid surface, such as a wall, door, floor, ceiling, or similar barrier.

The linked gateway can appear in an unoccupied space on the opposite side of that surface even if you can't see that space, provided the destination is within the normal range of Open the Way and you know or can reasonably determine where that space is.
If no suitable unoccupied space exists at the destination, the gateway doesn't form, and you don't expend the Bonus Action used to create it.

entries.name: Level 5 — Find the Other Side
entries: When you place a gateway against a solid surface with There Is Always Another Door, you can sense whether a suitable unoccupied space exists on the opposite side within the range of Open the Way.
You learn the direction and approximate distance to the nearest space large enough for the gateway to form, but you learn nothing else about that space or anything within it.
You can choose that space as the destination even if you can't see it.

optionalfeature.name: Step Between Heartbeats
entries: There is a moment between intent and impact when a path still exists.
You have learned to find that path before the blow can finish falling.
To everyone else, you simply vanish from the place where you were about to be struck.

entries.name: Instant Passage
entries: When a creature you can see targets you with an attack, you can use your Reaction to create your gateways immediately before the attack roll is made.
One gateway must appear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you, and the other in an unoccupied space you can see within the normal range of Open the Way.
You can immediately move through the adjacent gateway and emerge from the linked gateway without expending movement and without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
If this movement places you outside the attack's reach or range, or causes the attacker to lose line of sight or line of effect to you, the attack automatically misses.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 11 — Take Them With You
entries: When you use Step Between Heartbeats, you can bring one willing creature within 5 feet of you through the gateway with you.
The creature appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of your exit and doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from this movement.

entries.name: Level 17 — Before the World Can React
entries: When you use Step Between Heartbeats, you can create the gateways and move through them even if you are Grappled or Restrained.
In addition, after you emerge, you can immediately make one weapon attack, cast one cantrip with a casting time of an Action, or use one feature that normally requires an Action.

optionalfeature.name: The World Is Full of Entrances
entries: Distance has ceased to be an obstacle.
Every place you have stood has become another possible doorway.
The world is vast only to those who must travel across it.

entries.name: Familiar Destination
entries: When you use Open the Way, one of your gateways can appear at any location on the same plane that you have personally visited, regardless of distance and without requiring you to see the destination.
You must be able to identify the destination from memory, such as a particular room, street, rooftop, chamber, clearing, or other distinct place.
The gateway forms in the nearest suitable unoccupied space to the location you remember.
If no suitable space exists, the gateway fails to form, and you don't expend the Bonus Action used to create it.
You immediately know whether the gateway successfully formed.

entries.name: Distant Threshold
entries: A gateway created with Familiar Destination functions exactly like any other gateway created by Open the Way.
You can see and hear through it, move through it, make attacks through it, cast spells through it, and allow other creatures or objects to pass through it normally.
Distance between the gateways doesn't alter these functions.

entries.name: Level 17 — Every Plane Has a Door
entries: When you use Open the Way, one of your gateways can appear at a location on another plane of existence.
If you have personally visited the destination, the gateway can open there regardless of planar distance.
If you haven't personally visited it, you must be able to clearly identify the destination through a reliable description, map, magical observation, or similar source.
The gateway forms in the nearest suitable unoccupied space to the intended destination. If no suitable space exists, it fails to form, and you don't expend the Bonus Action used to create it.
A gateway created this way functions normally for passage, sight, attacks, spells, creatures, and objects.
Planar boundaries, planar distance, and effects that merely prevent teleportation or planar travel don't stop a gateway created by this feature.

optionalfeature.name: Fractured Counterpart
entries: Your reflections have stopped behaving like copies. Each now seems to remember a slightly different version of what you were about to do.

entries.name: Reflected Motion
entries: Whenever you take the Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help action, each of your Living Reflections can immediately move up to half your Speed, no action required from you.
This movement can occur before or after the action resolves.

entries.name: Level 11 — Mirror Feint
entries: Once on each of your turns, when you make an attack or cast a spell originating from your Living Reflection's space through Mirror Casting, you can cause another Living Reflection—or yourself—to perform the same visible motions.
Choose one creature that can see at least two of those positions. Until the attack or spell resolves:

items: The creature can't determine which position is the true origin by sight alone.
The first attack roll you make against that creature has Advantage.
If the creature makes a saving throw against the effect, it has Disadvantage on the first saving throw it makes against it.

entries: Choose the benefit when you use Mirror Feint.

entries.name: Level 17 — Impossible Reflection
entries: Once on each of your turns when you cast a spell or use an ability through Mirror Casting, you can choose two different origins among yourself and your Living Reflections.

The effect still occurs only once, but for determining range, line of sight, cover, and the direction or point of origin of an Area of Effect, you can use whichever of the two origins is more favorable for each target affected by that single use.
For example, a creature behind Total Cover from one reflection might still be affected if the second chosen origin has a clear path to it.

optionalfeature.name: War Without a Hand
entries: The Arsenal no longer waits for your hand. Its weapons have learned to answer violence on their own.

entries.name: Arsenal Strike
entries: Once on each of your turns when you take the Attack action, you can cause one weapon stored in your Arsenal to appear momentarily in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet and make one attack with it.
You make the attack as though you were wielding the weapon, using your normal attack modifier for it. The weapon vanishes back into the Arsenal immediately after the attack.
This attack is part of the same Attack action and doesn't require a free hand.

entries.name: Level 11 — Crossfire Arsenal
entries: Once per turn when Arsenal Strike hits, you can immediately summon a different stored weapon from another unoccupied space within 30 feet and make one additional attack with it against the same target.
You can make this additional attack only once per turn.

entries.name: Level 17 — Battlefield Arsenal
entries: The range of Arsenal Strike becomes 120 feet.

once on each of your turns when you use Arsenal Strike, you can cause the weapon to attack from up to three different possible spaces within range. Choose which space is the true origin only when the attack is resolved.
For determining range, line of sight, and cover, use whichever of those spaces is most favorable to the attack.
The weapon still makes only one attack.

optionalfeature.name: The Vessel Remembers
entries: Magic sealed long enough begins to leave an impression. Even after release, the Vessel remembers what it once contained.

entries.name: Refuse to Empty
entries: When you release a sealed spell and that spell fails to affect any creature because every spell attack misses, every affected creature succeeds on its initial saving throw, or every intended target becomes invalid before the spell resolves, the spell isn't removed from your Pact Vessel.
Any resources spent when the spell was originally sealed remain spent. You can attempt to release the spell again normally.

entries.name: Level 11 — Vessel Concentration
entries: When a Concentration spell is released from your Pact Vessel, the creature releasing it can cause the Vessel to maintain Concentration instead.
While doing so:

items: The releaser doesn't need to concentrate on the spell.
The Vessel can maintain only one spell at a time.
It makes no Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration.
Starting Concentration on another spell this way ends the previous one.

entries: The Concentration ends if the Vessel is destroyed or if it is more than 300 feet from the creature that released the spell.

entries.name: Level 17 — Perfect Memory
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you release a spell from your Pact Vessel, you can choose for the Vessel to retain a perfect copy of that sealed spell instead of removing it.
The released spell functions normally, while the identical spell remains stored in the same space of the Vessel and can be released again later.

optionalfeature.name: Claim Beyond Barriers
entries: The mark is no longer merely something you can sense. It becomes a point through which your power can reach.

entries.name: Brand Conduit
entries: Once on each of your turns when you make an attack or cast a spell that targets only one of your Branded creatures, you can treat the Brand itself as the point of origin for determining range and line of sight.
You still need to be within the normal range of the attack or spell measured to the Branded creature, but ordinary cover and intervening creatures don't block the effect.
This doesn't allow an Area of Effect to originate from the Brand.

entries.name: Level 11 — No Wall Between Us
