entries: Brand Conduit can function even if the Branded creature is behind Total Cover or enclosed within a mundane solid structure.
A spell or attack used this way can affect only the Branded creature and can't damage or pass through the intervening structure.

entries.name: Level 17 — The Brand Is the Opening
entries: Once on each of your turns when you cast a spell with an Area of Effect, you can cause that Area of Effect to originate from the space of one of your Branded creatures instead of from you or the spell's normal point of origin.
You make all choices for the spell normally, and the Branded creature can be affected by the spell normally.
distance on the same plane no longer prevents you from using Brand Conduit, though the spell or attack must otherwise be capable of targeting that creature.

optionalfeature.name: Momentum Thief
entries: Movement is only borrowed certainty. You have learned how to take some of it for yourself.

entries.name: Steal the Step
entries: Once per turn, when a creature you can see within 60 feet willingly moves at least 10 feet, you can reduce the remaining movement it can make during that turn by 10 feet.
Until the end of your next turn, your Speed increases by the same amount.
This requires no Action or Reaction.
A creature's Speed can't be reduced below 5 feet by this invocation.

entries.name: Level 11 — Take the Momentum
entries: When you use Steal the Step, you can instead steal up to 20 feet of movement.
until the end of your next turn, you can spend stolen movement in any combination to:

items: Increase your walking Speed.
Increase a Climb or Swim Speed you possess.
Stand from Prone without spending movement.
Move 5 feet immediately after a creature misses you with an attack, without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

entries: Each 5 feet moved this way consumes 5 feet of stolen movement.

entries.name: Level 17 — No Motion Is Wasted
entries: You can use Steal the Step once on each creature's turn, rather than once per round.
Stolen movement accumulates until the end of your next turn, to a maximum of 60 feet.
you can spend 20 feet of stolen movement to immediately move up to 20 feet when:

items: You succeed on a saving throw.
A creature misses you with an attack.
A creature you can see within 60 feet begins moving.

entries: This movement requires no Action or Reaction and doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

optionalfeature.name: Mastery Beyond Training
entries: You have stopped treating weapons as fixed techniques. Every grip, angle, and impact is another answer waiting to be used.

Choose two kinds of weapons with which you are proficient. You gain access to their Weapon Mastery properties. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace either choice with another weapon with which you are proficient.
When you make an attack with a weapon whose mastery you can use, you can choose to use its normal mastery property or one other mastery property for which that weapon qualifies.

At Level 11, you no longer need to choose specific weapons. You can use Weapon Mastery with every weapon with which you are proficient, and each time you attack you can choose any mastery property for which that weapon qualifies.
At Level 17, once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon, you can apply two different mastery properties to that attack instead of one.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Aegis
entries: Some bargains grant weapons. Yours taught the space around your body to refuse harm.

You can manifest a supernatural Aegis around yourself as a Bonus Action. Its appearance is entirely your choice: spectral armor, overlapping runes, floating plates, a second shadow, hardened light, invisible force, or another protective manifestation.
The Aegis lasts until you dismiss it, become Incapacitated, or manifest it again.
While the Aegis is active:

items: If you aren't wearing armor, your base AC becomes 13 + your Dexterity modifier.
You can use the Aegis as a Shield, gaining the normal +2 AC benefit while one of your hands is free.
Using it as a Shield doesn't place an object in that hand and doesn't interfere with Somatic components.
You are proficient with the Aegis.
It can't be disarmed, removed, or destroyed separately from you.

entries: Whenever you take damage, you can use your Reaction to reduce that damage by 1d10 + your Charisma modifier.
You can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
At Level 5, the reduction becomes 2d10 + your Charisma modifier. when you reduce damage to 0, you can immediately move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

At Level 11, while the Aegis is active, whenever you succeed on a saving throw that would cause you to take half damage, you instead take no damage. If you fail that saving throw, you take only half damage.

At Level 17, the damage reduction becomes 4d10 + your Charisma modifier, and using it no longer requires your Reaction once on each round. You can still spend your Reaction to use it an additional time during the same round.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Martial Discipline
entries: Your patron did not teach you a spell. It taught you how to fight.
When you gain this Pact, choose two Fighting Style feats of your choice. You gain those feats, and this Pact counts as the Fighting Style feature for the purpose of meeting their prerequisites.
You can choose a Fighting Style even if its prerequisite normally requires you to possess the Fighting Style feature from a particular class, but you must meet any other prerequisites it has.
Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can replace any Fighting Style gained from this Pact with another Fighting Style you qualify for.
You can't choose the same Fighting Style more than once through this Pact.

whenever a Fighting Style you gained from this Pact allows you to make an attack, move, Grapple, Shove, or otherwise perform an effect without using an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, doing so doesn't interfere with or prevent another Fighting Style gained from this Pact from triggering from the same attack, movement, or event.
At Level 5, you gain a third Fighting Style.
At Level 11, you gain a fourth Fighting Style.
At Level 17, you gain a fifth Fighting Style.
All Fighting Styles gained from this Pact can be active at the same time, provided the conditions of each Fighting Style are met.

optionalfeature.name: Discipline Without Boundaries
entries: Weapons are tools.
Stances are habits.
A discipline mastered deeply enough no longer depends on either.

entries.name: Universal Application
entries: When a Fighting Style gained from Pact of the Martial Discipline requires you to wield a particular type of weapon, use a particular weapon property, fight with a specific number of weapons, have a free hand, or wear a particular category of armor, you can ignore one such equipment requirement.
The Fighting Style must still be capable of producing a meaningful effect.

For example, a Fighting Style intended for ranged weapons could function with a thrown weapon, one intended for two-handed weapons could function with a one-handed weapon, or one requiring an empty hand could remain functional while that hand is occupied.
This feature doesn't change the weapon's own properties, damage die, range, or other statistics.

entries.name: Level 11 — Technique Over Tool
entries: You can ignore all equipment requirements of Fighting Styles gained from this Pact.

Whenever one of those Fighting Styles refers to a specific weapon category or property, you can apply its benefit to any weapon attack or Unarmed Strike for which the effect can meaningfully function.
A Fighting Style still can't create an impossible effect; for example, a benefit that modifies ammunition doesn't create ammunition for a weapon that doesn't use it.

entries.name: Level 17 — Discipline Defines the Weapon
entries: Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can treat that attack as possessing any weapon property or equipment qualification required by one of your Fighting Styles gained from this Pact, solely for determining whether that Fighting Style applies.
This doesn't actually grant the property to the weapon and doesn't alter the attack for any other rule.

optionalfeature.name: Unrestricted Discipline
entries: Rules exist to teach a technique safely.
Mastery begins when you understand which parts of those rules were never essential.
Your disciplines no longer demand perfect circumstances before they answer you.

entries.name: Loosen the Form
entries: Whenever a Fighting Style gained from Pact of the Martial Discipline has a restriction on how its benefit can be used, you can relax one of the following restrictions each time that Fighting Style applies:

items: A required minimum distance moved is reduced by 10 feet, to a minimum of 0 feet.
A required distance from a creature is reduced by 5 feet, to a minimum of 0 feet.
A range or reach limitation imposed specifically by the Fighting Style increases by 10 feet.
A requirement that you haven't moved, have moved, or remain in a particular position can be ignored.
A requirement concerning whether the target is adjacent to, within reach of, or farther away from another creature can be ignored.
A Fighting Style that requires a particular direction of movement, such as moving toward or away from a creature, can function with movement in any direction.

entries: You can relax only one restriction of a Fighting Style at a time.
This feature doesn't remove resource costs, action costs, requirements to hit or miss, or limitations on how often a Fighting Style can be used.

entries.name: Level 11 — Flexible Execution
entries: You can relax up to two restrictions simultaneously whenever a Fighting Style gained from this Pact applies.

In addition, if a Fighting Style requires a specific type of combat event to trigger, such as making an Opportunity Attack, entering a creature's reach, leaving a creature's reach, or taking a particular combat action, you can treat a closely equivalent combat event as satisfying that trigger.
For example, a feature that triggers when a creature enters your reach could also trigger when you move into that creature's reach.

entries.name: Level 17 — Technique Without Constraint
entries: Whenever a Fighting Style gained from Pact of the Martial Discipline applies, you can ignore any positional, movement, distance, facing, adjacency, or target-placement restriction imposed by that Fighting Style.
You must still satisfy its core trigger, expend any required resource, and obey any limit on how often it can be used.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of Hunger for Power
entries: Power is never enough. Every victory reveals another height you have yet to reach, and every height conquered only reveals another beyond it.

Your hunger isn't for flesh, wealth, or knowledge. You crave the strength possessed by those powerful enough to stand in your way. By overcoming worthy opponents, you can seize fragments of that strength and permanently reshape yourself with them.
You gain the following benefits.
Power first changes the vessel that contains it. The first thing your hunger devours is weakness itself, and your body begins discarding needs that once dictated whether you lived or died.
Power begins to flow through your body with greater efficiency. Movements that once required effort become instinctive, fluid, and unnaturally precise.
The power within you is no longer dormant. It begins to follow every attack you make, adding a fraction of your accumulated strength to every blow.
Your body has endured enough force to understand how to resist it. Moving you against your will becomes increasingly difficult, and every layer of power makes your body harder to break.
The limitations you were born with cease to be absolute. Strength, speed, endurance, intellect, instinct, and presence become qualities that can simply be pushed further.
Your power begins reinforcing more than flesh. Fear loses its grip, influence struggles to take root, and your mind becomes increasingly difficult to bend against your will.
Your body no longer adapts only to mundane hardship. Poison, flame, steel, supernatural energy, and even hostile magic become forces your growing existence learns to endure.
Gravity and physical restraint begin to lose their authority over you. Your own power becomes sufficient to support your body where the world no longer does.
You have grown tired of being told that something can't be harmed. Resistance is merely another obstacle, immunity merely a greater one, and obstacles exist to be surpassed.
Survival is no longer a struggle your body must consciously endure. It has become the natural state to which your existence constantly returns.

entries.name: Sense Power
entries: After you observe a creature take an action, make an attack, cast a spell, or use a feature, you can tell whether its Challenge Rating is high enough to grant you Power Points through Claim Power.
You don't learn its exact Challenge Rating.
If the creature has no Challenge Rating, use its character level instead.

entries.name: Claim Power
entries: When a hostile creature that you participated in defeating is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can claim a fragment of its power.
The creature must have a Challenge Rating equal to or greater than your Proficiency Bonus.
You gain Power Points equal to the creature's Challenge Rating.
If the creature has no Challenge Rating, you instead gain Power Points equal to its character level.
Once you gain Power Points this way, you can't gain Power Points again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
The same individual creature can grant you Power Points only once.
A creature created, summoned, controlled, or deliberately provided by you or one of your allies can't grant you Power Points.
Your Power Points have no maximum, don't disappear when you rest, and remain until you spend them.

entries.name: Endless Growth
entries: When you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can spend your accumulated Power Points on any improvement below that your current level has unlocked.
Unless an improvement says otherwise, you can purchase it more than once.
All improvements gained through this feat are permanent.

entries.name: Level 1 — Fortify
entries: You no longer need to eat, drink, or breathe. You can still eat, drink, and breathe normally if you choose to.
You have Advantage on saving throws against Exhaustion.

entries.name: Tireless Body
entries: You require only 4 hours of rest to complete a Long Rest.

During those 4 hours, you don't need to sleep. You can spend the time sitting, keeping watch, reading, maintaining equipment, eating or drinking by choice, meditating, or performing other light activity.
You can't perform strenuous activity during this time, such as fighting, casting spells, traveling at a normal pace, or performing heavy physical labor.
You can still benefit from only one Long Rest in a 24-hour period, as normal.

entries.name: Fortify
entries: 3 Power Points → Increase your Hit Point Maximum by 1.
Your Hit Point maximum permanently increases by 1.
You can purchase this improvement any number of times.

entries.name: Level 3 — Refine
entries: Your Speed increases by 5 feet.
Your jump distance is doubled.
Standing up from Prone costs you only 5 feet of movement.

entries.name: Unrestricted Movement
entries: You gain a Climb Speed and Swim Speed equal to your Walking Speed.

entries.name: Refine
entries: 4 Power Points → Refine one Skill.
Choose one skill.
If you aren't proficient in that skill, you gain proficiency in it.
If you're already proficient in that skill, you instead gain Expertise in it.
You can't purchase this improvement more than once for the same skill.

entries.name: Level 5 — Empower
entries: Your Speed increases by an additional 5 feet, for a total increase of 10 feet from this feat.
You gain a bonus to Initiative equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded up.

entries.name: Overwhelming Strength
entries: Your attacks deal double damage to objects and structures.

entries.name: Empower
entries: 6 Power Points → Increase your Power Damage by 1.
Your Power Damage bonus starts at 0 and permanently increases by 1 each time you purchase this improvement.
Whenever you deal damage with an attack, that attack deals additional damage equal to your Power Damage bonus.
The additional damage is one damage type already dealt by the attack.
This benefit applies to every attack you make.
Your Power Damage bonus can't exceed your Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Example
entries: If your Power Damage bonus is +3 and you hit with four attacks, each of those attacks deals 3 additional damage.

entries.name: Level 7 — Harden
entries: You count as one Size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.
You have Advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to resist being Grappled, Restrained, knocked Prone, pushed, or otherwise forcibly moved.

entries.name: Unbreakable Landing
entries: Whenever you take Falling damage, reduce that damage by an amount equal to 5 × your character level, to a minimum of 0.

entries.name: Harden
entries: 8 Power Points → Increase your Armor Class by 1.
Your AC permanently increases by 1.
You can purchase this improvement a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
If your Proficiency Bonus later increases, the maximum number of times you can purchase this improvement increases accordingly.
This bonus applies whether you are armored, unarmored, or wielding a Shield.

entries.name: Level 9 — Transcend
entries: When you make an ability check using a skill or tool in which you have proficiency, a d20 roll of 4 or lower is treated as a 5.
Aging no longer causes your physical capabilities to deteriorate.

entries.name: Purified Body
entries: You are Immune to Disease.
You also have Advantage on saving throws against the Poisoned condition.

entries.name: Transcend
entries: 10 Power Points → Increase one Ability Score by 1.
Choose Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma.
The chosen Ability Score permanently increases by 1.
You can purchase this improvement any number of times, and you can choose the same Ability Score repeatedly.
There is no maximum Ability Score imposed by this feat.
This improvement can increase an Ability Score beyond its normal maximum.

entries.name: Level 11 — Unyielding
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws against being Charmed or Frightened.

Whenever you fail a saving throw against either of those conditions, you can repeat that saving throw at the end of your next turn, even if the effect wouldn't normally allow another saving throw at that time.

entries.name: Unconquered Mind
entries: You can't be magically put to sleep.
You also have Advantage on saving throws against effects that would possess you or directly control your actions.

entries.name: Unyielding
entries: 10 Power Points → Gain proficiency in one Saving Throw.
Choose Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma.
You gain proficiency in saving throws using the chosen ability.
If you already have proficiency in that saving throw, you must choose another.
Each saving throw can benefit from this improvement only once.

entries.name: Level 13 — Adapt
entries: You have Advantage on Death Saving Throws.
You also have Advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects.

entries.name: Reject Magic
entries: When you fail a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, you can reroll the saving throw and must use the new roll.
Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Adapt
entries: 15 Power Points → Gain one Damage Resistance.
Choose any damage type.
You permanently gain Resistance to the chosen damage type.
This can include Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, Acid, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Psychic, Radiant, Thunder, or another damage type that exists in the game.
You can purchase this improvement multiple times, choosing a different damage type each time.
Choosing a damage type to which you already have Resistance provides no additional benefit.

entries.name: Level 15 — Unshackle
entries: You can Hover.
While conscious, you can remain suspended in the air up to 10 feet above a surface capable of supporting you.
While hovering this way, you can move horizontally using your normal Speed and can ascend or descend within this 10-foot limit.
You don't fall at the end of your turn while hovering.
at the start of each of your turns, you can choose one of the following conditions affecting you: Grappled, Prone, or Restrained.
If that condition was caused by a creature or effect whose Challenge Rating is lower than your character level, you immediately end the chosen condition on yourself.
If the source has no Challenge Rating, use its character level instead.

entries.name: Defy the Fall
entries: While you are conscious, you take no Falling damage.

entries.name: Unshackle
entries: 20 Power Points → Gain one Condition Immunity.
Choose one condition.
You permanently gain Immunity to the chosen condition.
You can purchase this improvement multiple times, choosing a different condition each time.

entries.name: Level 17 — Break Resistance
entries: Your Hover develops into true flight.
You gain a Flying Speed equal to your Walking Speed, and you can Hover.
You ignore Difficult Terrain.
Your Speed can't be reduced below half its normal value by a spell or magical effect unless that effect reduces your Speed to 0.
Your attacks and damaging effects count as magical whenever a rule or feature distinguishes between magical and nonmagical damage.

entries.name: Unstoppable Motion
entries: If your Speed is 0 at the start of your turn, you can end one spell or magical effect on yourself that is causing your Speed to become 0.
Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Break Resistance
entries: 20 Power Points → Overcome one Damage Resistance.
Choose one damage type.
The first time you purchase this improvement for that damage type, damage you deal of that type ignores Resistance.
You can purchase this improvement a second time for the same damage type. If you do, damage you deal of that type also ignores Immunity.

items: First Purchase. Ignore Resistance to the chosen damage type.
Second Purchase. Ignore both Resistance and Immunity to the chosen damage type.

entries: Further purchases for the same damage type provide no additional benefit.

entries.name: Level 19 — Absolute Adaptation
entries: Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you remove one level of Exhaustion.
You no longer suffer penalties caused solely by extreme heat, extreme cold, high altitude, atmospheric pressure, underwater pressure, or similar environmental conditions.
This doesn't prevent damage or other specific effects that such an environment directly causes.
You also have Resistance to damage dealt by spells.

entries.name: Existence Without Need
entries: You no longer need sleep.
You can't be magically aged.

You must still complete a Long Rest to regain features and resources, but you can remain conscious throughout the entire rest and spend it performing the same kinds of light activity permitted by Tireless Body.

entries.name: Absolute Adaptation
entries: 35 Power Points → Gain one Damage Immunity.
Choose one damage type to which you already have Resistance.
Your Resistance to that damage type permanently becomes Immunity.
You can purchase this improvement multiple times, choosing a different qualifying damage type each time.

entries.name: Example of Growth
entries: A Level 13 character with a Proficiency Bonus of +5 participates in defeating a CR 9 hostile creature and gains 9 Power Points. They can't gain Power Points through Claim Power again until they finish a Short or Long Rest.
After taking a Short Rest, they later participate in defeating a CR 12 creature and gain another 12 Power Points, giving them 21 Power Points total.

They could spend 15 Power Points to gain Fire Resistance through Adapt and retain 6 Power Points; or spend 10 Power Points to increase Strength by 1 through Transcend and 6 Power Points to increase Power Damage by 1 through Empower, retaining 5 Power Points.
They can instead spend nothing and save all 21 Power Points for a more expensive improvement.

There is no maximum to the amount of Power Points you can accumulate, and Hunger for Power has no fixed endpoint. As long as you can continue overcoming sufficiently powerful opponents, you can continue using their power to surpass your previous limits.

optionalfeature.name: The Strong Feed the Strong
entries: Power recognizes power.
The greater the thing you overcome, the more of it remains for you to claim.
You have learned not to let any of that strength go to waste.
Your hunger no longer quiets after feeding once.
Power only makes you capable of consuming more.

entries.name: Greater Prey
entries: When Claim Power grants you Power Points from a creature whose Challenge Rating or character level is greater than your character level, you gain additional Power Points equal to the difference.
For example, if you are level 10 and claim power from a CR 14 creature, you gain 18 Power Points instead of 14.

entries.name: Level 11 — Nothing Wasted
entries: When you would gain Power Points through Claim Power, you can choose to gain at least an amount equal to your character level, even if the defeated creature's Challenge Rating is lower.
The creature must still meet every normal requirement of Claim Power, including the minimum Challenge Rating requirement.

entries.name: Level 17 — Bottomless Hunger
entries: The restriction in Claim Power that prevents you from gaining Power Points again until you finish a Short or Long Rest no longer applies.
You can gain Power Points from every qualifying hostile creature you participate in defeating.

All other restrictions of Claim Power still apply, including that the same individual creature can grant you Power Points only once and that creatures created, summoned, controlled, or deliberately provided by you or your allies can't grant Power Points.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Stolen Gift
entries: What another creature possesses is only theirs until you decide otherwise.

entries.name: Claim Slots
entries: You have a number of Claim Slots equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended Claim Slots when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Claim a Gift
entries: Whenever a creature you can see within 60 feet uses a feature, trait, spell, special attack, movement mode, sense, Resistance, Immunity, or another distinct ability, you can record that ability as a Gift.
Recording a Gift requires no action and expends no Claim Slot.
You retain a Gift after recording it and can remember any number of Gifts. You don't need to keep the original creature nearby, and the creature doesn't lose the ability you copied.
You learn enough about the Gift to understand broadly what it does, but you don't automatically learn unrelated statistics or hidden information about the creature.

entries.name: Use a Gift
entries: As a Bonus Action, choose one Gift you have recorded and expend 1 Claim Slot. For the next 1 hour, you gain an imitation of that Gift.
Unless the Gift says otherwise, you use your own statistics rather than those of the creature you copied it from.
If the Gift requires an Attack Roll, you can use Charisma for that attack.
If the Gift requires a Saving Throw, its save DC is 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Charisma modifier.

A Gift can reproduce abilities such as Flying, Climbing, Swimming, Burrowing, Hovering, Darkvision, Blindsight, Tremorsense, Truesight, Damage Resistance or Immunity, natural weapons, unusual attacks, supernatural movement, regeneration, defensive traits, activated creature abilities, spells, or other distinct abilities you have witnessed.
If a Gift depends on a resource belonging specifically to the original creature, you don't gain that creature's resource pool unless the Gift itself explicitly provides one.

entries.name: Stolen Spell
entries: If the Gift is a spell, you can cast that spell once while the Gift is active without expending a Spell Slot.
You don't need Material Components unless the spell's Material Component has a listed cost.
There is no restriction based on the spell's level.
Once you cast the stolen spell, that Gift immediately ends.

The spell remains recorded in your collection. You can activate the same Spell Gift again later by expending another Claim Slot, allowing you to cast it once again. A Spell Gift has no separate cooldown or once-per-rest restriction beyond your available Claim Slots.

entries.name: Permanent Gifts
entries: If a Gift normally represents a passive ability rather than something used a limited number of times, you retain that ability for the full 1-hour duration.
For example, if you activate a recorded Truesight, Damage Resistance, or Flying Speed, you retain that copied trait until the Gift ends.
If the Gift itself has a shorter duration or naturally ends under certain conditions, those restrictions still apply.

entries.name: Things That Cannot Be Taken
entries: You can't record or reproduce Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic transformations, an entire Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature, an entire class, subclass, or collection of class levels, an entire stat block, an ability whose primary purpose is creating permanent duplicates of yourself, or an ability whose primary purpose is permanently creating additional creatures.
However, an individual spell or individual distinct ability used through one of those larger features can still be recorded as a Gift.
For example, you can't steal a Wizard's entire Spellcasting feature, but you can record a specific spell you witness that Wizard cast.

entries.name: Multiple Gifts
entries: Starting at Warlock level 11, you can have up to two Gifts active at the same time.
At Warlock level 17, you can have up to three Gifts active at the same time.
Each Gift still requires its own Claim Slot.
If activating a new Gift would cause you to exceed your maximum number of active Gifts, you choose one of your currently active Gifts to end immediately.

optionalfeature.name: I Saw That
entries: You do not need to understand a Gift before you take it.
Observation is enough.
One moment of exposure is all the invitation you require.

entries.name: Instant Claim
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet uses an ability that you can record as a Gift, you can immediately activate that Gift as part of the same moment, expending 1 Claim Slot but requiring no Bonus Action.
The Gift becomes active after the triggering ability finishes resolving.
You must still be able to record that ability normally through Claim a Gift.

entries.name: Level 11 — Steal the Timing
entries: When you activate a Gift with Instant Claim, you can use that Gift immediately if it normally requires an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction.
Doing so requires no additional action.
If the Gift is a spell, you can cast the stolen spell immediately as part of this use.

entries.name: Level 17 — Better the Original
entries: The first time you use a Gift activated through Instant Claim, choose one of the following benefits that can apply to that use:

items: Gain Advantage on one Attack Roll made with the Gift.
Impose Disadvantage on one Saving Throw caused by the Gift.
Maximize one damage or healing die of the Gift.
Increase the Gift's range by 60 feet.
Double one movement speed granted by the Gift until the end of the turn.

optionalfeature.name: Composite Theft
entries: A stolen Gift does not need to remain whole.
You have learned to separate function from form, keeping only the parts worth taking.
What others possess as one ability, you can rebuild into something better suited to you.

entries.name: Borrowed Pieces
entries: When you activate a Gift, you can choose one distinct component of another Gift you have recorded and graft that component onto the active Gift for its duration.
The borrowed component must be something that can function independently, such as:

items: a movement mode
a sense
a Damage Resistance
a natural weapon damage type
a range increase
a secondary movement rider
a passive defensive trait
a non-resource passive effect

entries: You don't gain the entire second Gift, only the chosen component.
Using Borrowed Pieces doesn't expend an additional Claim Slot.

entries.name: Level 11 — Two Things Worth Taking
entries: You can graft up to two components from recorded Gifts onto a single active Gift.
The two components can come from the same Gift or from different Gifts.

entries.name: Level 17 — Perfect Reconstruction
entries: When you activate a Gift, you can rebuild it from pieces of your recorded collection.
Instead of activating one recorded Gift exactly as copied, choose up to three compatible components from Gifts you have recorded and combine them into one reconstructed Gift for 1 hour.
The reconstructed Gift still counts as one active Gift and costs only one Claim Slot.
A reconstructed Gift can't reproduce an ability prohibited by Things That Cannot Be Taken, and the DM determines whether chosen components are mechanically compatible.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Unwritten Rule
entries: Once a limitation has stopped you, it never gets to stop you the same way again.

entries.name: Record a Restriction
entries: Whenever a rule, condition, environmental restriction, magical effect, or defensive property directly prevents, limits, or reduces something you attempted to do, you can record that restriction.
Recording a restriction requires no action.
You can remember any number of recorded restrictions.

entries.name: Break the Rule
entries: As a Bonus Action, choose one restriction you have recorded.
For 1 hour, you can ignore that restriction whenever it would apply to you.

Examples of restrictions you could record include Difficult Terrain slowing you, needing a free hand to perform something, being unable to speak because of Silence, being unable to see a target because of Darkness, needing to breathe underwater, being unable to move through a particular kind of barrier, a spell preventing teleportation, a condition preventing a particular action, a feature requiring you to remain on the ground, an effect preventing healing, an effect preventing you from taking Reactions, a magical effect limiting your Speed, an effect preventing you from casting spells, or a creature's Damage Resistance reducing damage you deal.
You ignore only the specific restriction you recorded, not the entire source that created it.
For example, recording "I can't cast spells while Silenced" would let you cast despite that restriction, but wouldn't automatically make you immune to every other effect of the spell or area.

entries.name: Break Resistance
entries: If a creature's Damage Resistance reduces damage dealt by one of your attacks or damaging effects, you can record that Resistance as a restriction.
While you are ignoring that recorded restriction, your attacks and damaging effects ignore that creature's Resistance to the recorded damage type.

entries.name: It Must Stop You First
entries: You can only record a restriction after it has actually affected you or something you attempted to do.
Knowing that something could stop, limit, or reduce you isn't enough.
You have to personally encounter the limitation at least once.

entries.name: No Longer Applicable
entries: Once you activate a recorded restriction, that restriction simply doesn't apply to you for the duration.
If it says "You can't take Reactions," you can take Reactions.
If it says "Your Speed becomes 0," that part doesn't affect you.
If it says "You can't regain Hit Points," you can regain Hit Points normally.
It doesn't automatically end or dispel the original effect; you just ignore the recorded limitation.

entries.name: More Than One Rule
entries: At Warlock level 11, you can have two recorded restrictions ignored simultaneously.
At Warlock level 17, you can have three.
Activating each restriction requires its own Bonus Action.

optionalfeature.name: Once Is Enough
entries: You no longer need to be the one who suffers first.
A rule only has to prove that it exists once.
After that, you already know where it breaks.

entries.name: Witnessed Restriction
entries: When a rule, condition, environmental restriction, magical effect, or defensive property directly prevents, limits, or reduces something attempted by a creature you can see within 60 feet, you can record that restriction as though it had affected you personally.
You must be able to perceive what actually prevented or limited the creature. Merely knowing that a restriction exists isn't enough.
This counts as satisfying It Must Stop You First for that restriction.

entries.name: Level 11 — Shared Exception
entries: When you use Break the Rule, you can choose one willing creature you can see within 30 feet.
For as long as you ignore the chosen restriction, that creature ignores the same restriction whenever it would apply to it.
You can change the chosen creature as a Bonus Action without ending Break the Rule.

entries.name: Level 17 — Precedent
entries: Once you have recorded a restriction, you can activate Break the Rule for that restriction at the moment it would affect you, requiring no action.
You can do this even if the restriction itself would prevent you from taking Actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions.

optionalfeature.name: The Rule Bends Both Ways
entries: A limitation defines more than what cannot be done.
It also reveals exactly where reality expects resistance.
Once you understand that pressure, you can push in the opposite direction.

entries.name: Invert the Restriction
entries: While you are ignoring a recorded restriction with Break the Rule, once on each of your turns when that restriction would normally hinder, reduce, or prevent something you do, you can instead gain a benefit based on the nature of that restriction.
The benefit must directly oppose the restriction and lasts only for that instance.

items: A restriction that would reduce your Speed can instead increase your Speed by the same amount.
Difficult Terrain that would cost additional movement can instead cost you no movement for the affected space.
An effect that would impose Disadvantage on one of your rolls can instead grant Advantage on that roll.
An effect that would reduce damage you deal can instead cause that damage to ignore the reduction and deal additional damage equal to your Charisma modifier.
An effect that would prevent you from taking a Reaction can instead allow you to take one additional Reaction before the start of your next turn.

An effect that would prevent you from regaining Hit Points can instead cause the next healing you receive before the start of your next turn to restore additional Hit Points equal to your Warlock level.

entries: The benefit must be a direct inversion of the specific restriction you recorded. It doesn't grant unrelated abilities.

entries.name: Level 11 — Turn the Pressure
entries: When Invert the Restriction grants you Advantage, additional movement, additional damage, additional healing, or an additional Reaction, you can grant that same benefit to one willing creature you can see within 30 feet instead of yourself.

entries.name: Level 17 — Reality Overcorrects
entries: The first time on each of your turns that you use Invert the Restriction, you can apply the inverted benefit at double its normal numerical value, if it has one.
For example, a 10-foot Speed reduction could become a 20-foot Speed increase, and additional damage equal to your Charisma modifier would become twice your Charisma modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Your Rule, Not Mine
entries: A restriction does not vanish simply because you refuse to obey it.
The rule still exists.
You have merely decided who it applies to instead.

entries.name: Return the Restriction
entries: While you are ignoring a recorded restriction with Break the Rule, when a creature you can see causes that same restriction to apply to you, you can use your Reaction to force that creature to suffer an equivalent restriction until the start of your next turn.
The reflected restriction must be one that can meaningfully apply to that creature.

items: If it prevents you from taking Reactions, that creature can't take Reactions.
If it reduces your Speed, its Speed is reduced by the same amount.
If it imposes Disadvantage on your attacks, its attacks have Disadvantage.
If it prevents you from regaining Hit Points, that creature can't regain Hit Points.
If its Resistance reduces damage you deal, it loses that Resistance against your damage for the duration.
If it prevents you from casting spells, it can't cast spells for the duration.

entries: You don't transfer the original effect itself. You impose only the specific recorded restriction you are currently ignoring.

entries.name: Level 13 — Same Rule for Everyone
entries: When you use Return the Restriction, you can affect up to a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier, provided each creature is contributing to or benefiting from the same recorded restriction and is within 30 feet of the original creature.
Each affected creature suffers the reflected restriction until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Level 17 — The Exception Becomes the Rule
entries: When you use Return the Restriction, the reflected restriction lasts for 1 minute instead.

An affected creature can repeat the saving throw, if any saving throw was originally associated with the restriction, at the end of each of its turns, ending the reflected restriction on itself on a success.
If the original restriction had no saving throw, the reflected restriction lasts for the full duration unless ended by an effect that could normally remove an equivalent condition or limitation.

optionalfeature.name: Relentless Casting
entries: Once the spell begins, interruption only makes you force it through harder.

Whenever you cast a spell and one of the following causes that spell to fail or have no effect against at least one target, you can immediately attempt to force the same spell through again against one affected target:

items: The target succeeds on its Saving Throw.
Your Spell Attack misses.
The spell is Counterspelled.
The target's Resistance or Immunity causes the spell to deal reduced or no damage.

entries: You don't expend another Spell Slot or Material Component.
Resolve the spell against that target again as though you had just cast it, including making another Spell Attack or forcing another Saving Throw as appropriate.
You can continue doing this until the spell successfully affects that target or you choose to stop.
Each additional attempt after the first causes you to take 1d12 Force damage after that attempt is resolved.
This damage can't be reduced or prevented and can't reduce you below 1 Hit Point.

optionalfeature.name: Spellbreaker's Instinct
entries: Magic always reveals itself in the instant before it takes form.
You have learned to recognize that fragile moment and strike directly into it.
To you, a spell is not an inevitability—it is simply another thing that can be broken.
Whenever a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell, you can immediately make one Spell Attack against that creature.

items: The attack requires no Reaction.
The attack happens before the spell resolves.
The attack uses your Charisma modifier for the attack roll.
On a hit, the attack deals 1d10 + your Charisma modifier Force damage.

entries: If the attack hits, the caster must make a Constitution Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC.
On a failed save, choose one:

items: The spell is Countered and has no effect.
If the spell requires Concentration, the caster begins it with Disadvantage on all Concentration saves until the end of its next turn.
The spell's damage ignores none of your Resistances or Immunities this casting.

entries.name: Break Through Resistance
entries: When this attack hits a creature that has Resistance to Force damage, you ignore that Resistance.
If the creature has Immunity to Force damage, treat that Immunity as Resistance instead.

optionalfeature.name: Echoes Left Behind
entries: Every hand leaves something behind, even when no fingerprint remains.
Places remember those who passed through them, and objects remember how they were used.
You have learned how to make those silent memories answer.
When you touch an object, structure, or section of terrain and concentrate on it for 1 minute, you can read fragments of impressions left upon it.
Choose one of the following questions:

items.name: Who Used This?
items.entry: Learn a general description of the most recent creature to meaningfully use or interact with it.

items.name: What Happened Here?
items.entry: Learn the most significant event involving it within the last 24 hours.

items.name: Where Did It Come From?
items.entry: Learn the general direction and approximate distance to the place where the object was created, last assembled, or last considered its home.

items.name: What Is Hidden?
items.entry: Learn whether it contains a hidden compartment, concealed mechanism, secret entrance, trap, or intentionally hidden feature.

items.name: How Does It Work?
items.entry: Learn the object's intended mundane or magical function and the basic method normally used to operate it.

items.name: Where Did They Go?
items.entry: If a creature interacted with the target within the last 24 hours, learn the direction that creature traveled immediately afterward.

entries: You receive the information as brief sensory impressions, emotions, images, sounds, or instinctive understanding, rather than a perfect recording.

entries.name: Dig Deeper
entries: After receiving an answer, you can immediately ask one additional question from the list about the same target.
Doing so causes you to take 1d6 Psychic damage, which can't be reduced or prevented.
You can continue asking additional questions in this way, taking an additional 1d6 Psychic damage for each question after the first.

entries.name: Old Memories Fade
entries: Normally, this Invocation can read impressions from only the last 24 hours.
At Warlock level 7, this increases to 30 days.
At Warlock level 13, it increases to 1 year.
At Warlock level 17, you can read impressions from any point in the target's history, provided some meaningful trace still remains.

optionalfeature.name: Sovereign's Mark
entries: Those who stand before your authority don't simply leave your presence unchanged.
Once the Crown has acknowledged someone, distance alone can't fully sever that connection.
Your subjects may wander beyond sight, but the Crown remembers where its gaze has fallen.

entries.name: Mark a Subject
entries: Until you finish a Long Rest, dismiss the mark, or replace it.
After you speak directly with a creature for at least 1 minute, you can mark that creature as one of your Subjects.
You can have a number of Subjects equal to your Proficiency Bonus at the same time.
If you mark another creature while already at this maximum, choose one existing Subject; its mark immediately ends.
You can dismiss a mark at any time.
A creature doesn't automatically know that it has been marked.

entries.name: The Crown Knows Its Subjects
entries: While the creature remains your Subject.

While a Subject is on the same plane of existence as you, you instinctively know the general direction toward it; whether it is within 300 feet, 1 mile, 10 miles, or farther away; and whether it is conscious or unconscious.
This feature doesn't reveal the Subject's exact location.
Barriers, darkness, invisibility, and ordinary concealment don't prevent this awareness.

entries.name: Speak Across Distance
entries: For as long as you continue the communication.
You can speak directly into the mind of any Subject on the same plane of existence.
Only that Subject hears your words unless you choose to speak normally as well.
The Subject can mentally reply to you while the connection remains open.
You don't need to share a language to communicate simple concepts, intentions, emotions, images, or commands.
Complex conversation still requires a language both of you understand.
Distance doesn't prevent this communication as long as you and the Subject remain on the same plane of existence.

entries.name: Through the Eyes of a Subject
entries: Establishing the connection requires an Action; switching senses afterward requires no Action.
Up to 10 minutes.
Choose one of your Subjects on the same plane of existence.
For the duration, you can perceive through that Subject's senses instead of your own.
You can use every sense the Subject normally possesses, including sight, hearing, smell, Darkvision, Blindsight, Tremorsense, Truesight, or another special sense naturally available to that Subject.
You perceive what the Subject perceives from its position and perspective.
While using the Subject's senses, you are Blinded and Deafened with regard to your own surroundings.
You can switch back to your own senses at any time.
While the duration remains, you can return to the Subject's senses at any time.
The Subject doesn't automatically know that you are perceiving through it.
You can still use Speak Across Distance with that Subject while perceiving through its senses.
This effect ends early if the Subject leaves your plane of existence, its mark ends, you become Incapacitated, or you choose to end the effect.

entries.name: Authority Finds You
entries: You can use Assume Command against one of your Subjects even if that creature is outside Assume Command's normal 60-foot range, can't physically hear you, or isn't currently visible to you.
The Subject must still be on the same plane of existence.
Your command is transmitted directly through Speak Across Distance, so the Subject counts as hearing and understanding the command for the purpose of Assume Command.
If the Subject is within 1 mile, Assume Command functions normally.
If the Subject is farther than 1 mile away, it has Advantage on its Saving Throw against Assume Command.
All other rules and durations of Assume Command remain unchanged.

entries.name: Summoned Before the Crown
entries: Activating this feature requires a Bonus Action.
Up to 1 minute.
Choose one of your Subjects on the same plane of existence.
For the duration, you know its exact direction, you know its approximate distance from you, and the Subject instinctively knows the shortest reasonable direction toward you.

If that Subject fails a Saving Throw against your Assume Command during this duration, you can include an instruction such as "Come to me" as part of the command without that portion counting toward the command's normal complexity.
The Subject still uses its own movement and abilities normally to reach you.
This feature doesn't teleport the Subject or allow it to pass through obstacles it couldn't normally cross.
You can end this effect at any time with no Action required.

optionalfeature.name: Imperishable Decree
entries: Some commands are meant to outlive battles, kingdoms, and even the voice that first pronounced them.
Your authority no longer rests upon the mind alone; it is carved into flesh, will, and soul as an immutable law.
Once the Crown has spoken its decree, neither time nor another master's hand can teach the subject to disobey.

entries.name: Inscribe a Decree
entries: Activating this feature takes 1 minute.
Permanent until fulfilled, dismissed, or otherwise ended by this Invocation.
Choose one creature you can see within 60 feet that can understand you.
Speak a command, prohibition, duty, standing instruction, or conditional order to that creature.

The decree can be significantly more complex than Assume Command and can describe something the creature must do, something it must never do, someone it must protect, somewhere it must remain, a secret it must never reveal, a person or group it must obey, a condition that causes it to perform a specific task, a long-term responsibility, or a rule governing its future behavior.

Examples include: "Never reveal what happened in this chamber," "Protect this bloodline for as long as you exist," "Whenever this city is attacked, defend its people," "You will never willingly harm me or my companions," "When you find the man bearing this symbol, bring him before me," "Guard this door and permit entry only to those carrying my seal," or "If I die, deliver this letter to my successor."

entries.name: Willing Subjects
entries: Permanent.
A willing creature automatically accepts the decree.
No Saving Throw is required.

entries.name: Unwilling Subjects
entries: Permanent on a failed save.
An unwilling creature makes a Wisdom Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC.
On a failed save, the decree takes hold permanently.
On a successful save, the decree fails to take hold.
A creature that successfully saves against a particular decree can't be targeted by that same decree again until you finish a Long Rest.
Once the decree takes hold, the creature receives no further Saving Throws merely because time passes.

entries.name: Bound in Body and Soul
entries: While the decree exists.
An Imperishable Decree binds the creature's body, mind, will, and soul simultaneously.
The creature can't willingly or unwillingly perform an action that directly violates the decree.

This remains true even if the creature is affected by another effect that would normally control or replace its actions, including being Charmed or Dominated, possession, magical or psionic mind control, direct control of its body, forced movement or forced actions, memory alteration, personality or alignment alteration, control or manipulation of its soul, another creature choosing its actions, transformation into another form, or unconscious or altered states in which another effect attempts to direct its behavior.
If another effect attempts to force the creature to violate your decree, the conflicting portion of that effect fails.

For example, if your decree states "Never harm me" and another creature completely controls the Subject and commands it to attack you, the Subject can't make that attack. The controller may command it to perform other actions that don't violate the decree.
An Imperishable Decree therefore takes precedence over other forms of control whenever their instructions conflict.

entries.name: The Body Obeys
entries: While the decree exists.
If fulfilling the decree requires the creature to act, its body must cooperate with the decree even if its conscious mind resists.
It must use its movement, Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, speech, possessions, spells, features, and other available capabilities as reasonably necessary to obey.

A creature can't deliberately paralyze itself, surrender control of its body, render itself unconscious, alter its own memories, transform itself, or place itself under another creature's control for the purpose of escaping or violating the decree.

entries.name: The Soul Remembers
entries: While the decree exists.
The decree is attached to the creature's identity and soul, not merely its current body.
Changing bodies, possessing another body, transforming, being reincarnated, being resurrected, or otherwise continuing existence in another physical form doesn't remove the decree.
If the creature temporarily ceases to possess a usable body, the decree remains dormant rather than ending and resumes functioning when the creature can act again.

entries.name: Bound to the Word
entries: While the decree remains active.
The creature is compelled to act according to the decree's wording.
If the decree prohibits something, the creature simply can't violate that prohibition.

If obedience is temporarily impossible, the creature isn't required to accomplish the impossible. The decree remains active and resumes compelling obedience as soon as compliance becomes possible again.

entries.name: Conditional Decrees
entries: Its activation is defined when the decree is created.
Permanent until triggered and completed, unless written to repeat.
A decree can remain dormant until a condition you specify occurs.
For example: "If anyone opens this vault without my permission, sound the alarm and attack them."
You can also create a recurring decree.
For example: "Whenever the bells ring three times, return to this fortress."
A recurring decree continues to function whenever its condition occurs unless its wording states otherwise.

entries.name: The Crown Interprets
entries: While the decree exists.
A decree follows the meaning and intent you held when you created it, rather than merely its most technically convenient interpretation.
The creature can't escape through deliberate grammatical loopholes, technicalities, indirect actions, intermediaries, or intentional misinterpretation.
If circumstances make the wording ambiguous, the decree follows the interpretation that most closely reflects your original intent.

entries.name: Command From Afar
entries: Instantaneous modification.
If the affected creature is also one of your Subjects from Sovereign's Mark, you can modify an existing decree on that creature while both of you are on the same plane of existence.
You communicate the alteration through Speak Across Distance.
The creature receives no new Saving Throw if the alteration remains within the original purpose of the decree.
A fundamentally unrelated command counts as a new decree.

entries.name: Revoke the Law
entries: Instantaneous.
You can permanently end any Imperishable Decree you created, provided you and the affected creature are on the same plane of existence.

optionalfeature.name: Edict of the Unthinking
entries: The Crown doesn't require thought, language, life, or even a soul before it can demand obedience.
Steel, stone, earth, machines, relics, and monuments all possess forms capable of serving a purpose.
Where no will exists to answer your command, your authority becomes the will that moves the world.
Possession is merely another claim made beneath the Crown.
The weapon can hear you even while another hand grips its hilt.
When owner and Crown give conflicting orders, the object itself is forced to choose.
An object doesn't forget what it can do simply because its proper wielder is absent.
Bloodline, training, ritual, and attunement are permissions created for lesser hands.
The Crown asks only whether the power exists—and if it does, commands it to answer.
Attunement, curses, creators, and ancient bonds may all claim an object.
Such claims remain meaningful only until they contradict the Crown.
When two masters command the same thing, lesser authority is made to yield.
At last, the difference between an arsenal, a fortress, and a city becomes irrelevant.
Every silent thing within your domain is another body awaiting a command.
One declaration from the Crown can set an entire landscape into motion.
Sometimes countless servants are less useful than a single hand large enough to move a kingdom.
Weapons, machines, ruins, earth, stone, and every silent material nearby are summoned toward a single point.
What arrives as countless separate things rises again as one colossal body bearing the Crown.

entries.name: Authority Without a Mind
entries: Permanent.
Your features from Pact of the Crown can affect eligible targets even if they possess no mind, can't hear, can't understand language, aren't creatures, or were never alive.
Your Crown authority is imposed directly upon the target's physical form and supernatural essence, if it possesses one.
A genuinely mindless target automatically fails any mental Saving Throw required by one of your Crown features.
A target that possesses genuine independent will still makes its Saving Throws normally, even if it has extremely low Intelligence or can't communicate.

entries.name: Matter Answers the Crown
entries: Permanent.
Eligible targets aren't limited to manufactured objects.
You can command nonliving natural matter and discrete masses of material as though they were objects.
This includes earth, soil, sand, stone, gravel, clay, mud, minerals, ore, raw metal, crystal, ice, snow, bone, dead wood, rubble, ash, glass, and other nonliving natural or artificial matter.
The material doesn't need to have previously been considered an object.
A sufficiently large mass uses the Crown-Bound Object stat block appropriate to the Size of the mass being commanded.

entries.name: Animate the Unthinking
entries: When you command an eligible object or mass of material that normally can't move or act independently, you can animate it as a Crown-Bound Object.

Use the Crown-Bound Object stat block corresponding to its actual Size: {@creature Tiny Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, {@creature Small Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, {@creature Medium Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, {@creature Large Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, {@creature Huge Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, or {@creature Gargantuan Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}.
There is no numerical maximum to the number of Crown-Bound Objects you can animate simultaneously.
There is no Size restriction.

Animating something doesn't transform it. A sword remains a sword, stone remains stone, a wagon remains a wagon, and a mass of earth remains earth. The Crown simply grants it movement, the ability to act, and the capacity to obey.

entries.name: The Object Remains Itself
entries: While animated.
Animation doesn't erase or replace the target's existing properties.

It retains any existing Armor Class, Hit Points, Ability Scores, Saving Throws, Skills, Speeds, Resistances, Immunities, Vulnerabilities, senses, attacks, damage dice, weapon properties, magical properties, traits, actions, special functions, and other existing statistics.
The Crown-Bound Object stat block provides statistics or capabilities that the target doesn't already possess.
If the original value is better or more appropriate, use the original value.

entries.name: Bound to the Crown
entries: While animated.
Crown-Bound Objects obey your commands absolutely.
They understand the meaning and intent of your instructions despite lacking normal intelligence.
This doesn't make them Sapient, give them personalities, or create independent desires.

Once given a command, an object continues carrying it out until the task is completed, you replace the command, compliance becomes permanently impossible, or the effect maintaining the animation ends.
No further Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction from you is required.

entries.name: Floating Servants
entries: While animated.
Every Crown-Bound Object gains the Fly Speed listed in its stat block and can Hover.

Its shape doesn't need to be capable of natural flight. Weapons can fly, armor can float, vehicles can hover, statues can rise into the air, and masses of earth or stone can suspend themselves above the ground.
This doesn't physically reshape the target.

entries.name: Initiative
entries: While animated.
Crown-Bound Objects take their turns immediately after yours.
If multiple Crown-Bound Objects act at that time, you determine their order.
They can use their movement, Action, Bonus Action if available, Reaction, native abilities, and Crown-Bound abilities without requiring you to spend any of your actions.

entries.name: Crown Strike
entries: The Crown-Bound Object uses its Action.
Instantaneous.
If a Crown-Bound Object doesn't use a native attack, it can make a Crown Strike.
Attack Roll: d20 + the object's appropriate Strength or Dexterity modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.
Damage: {@damage 1d4} + the same Strength or Dexterity modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.

The damage type is determined by the object's actual form, normally Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing, or another appropriate damage type provided by the object's actual magical or physical properties.
This formula applies to ordinary Crown-Bound Objects. Crownforged Titans use their own Titan Attack Formula instead.

entries.name: Native Attacks
entries: Use the native attack's action economy.
If an object already possesses an attack, it can use that attack instead of Crown Strike.
The native attack retains its normal damage dice, modifiers, Reach, Range, riders, magical properties, additional damage, special effects, and ammunition rules.
Animation never forces a superior native attack to become a Crown Strike.

entries.name: Purpose of Form
entries: While animated.
A Crown-Bound Form describes what the target's existing physical shape is already suited to do.
Choosing or possessing a Form doesn't transform the target.
Available Forms from the Crown-Bound Object stat blocks are Edged, Piercing, Crushing, Guardian, Grasping, and Projectile.
A target can qualify for multiple Forms simultaneously when its actual construction supports them.

entries.name: Independent Servants
entries: While animated.
Your Crown-Bound Objects can independently interpret and execute complex instructions.

They can attack, defend, guard, patrol, search, retrieve objects, carry creatures or cargo, operate mechanisms, use tools, open and close doors, operate machinery, repair, construct, dismantle, sort objects, reload weapons, perform delicate physical work, and perform repetitive labor.
They understand your intended result, so you don't need to describe every individual motion required to accomplish it.

entries.name: The Crown Has Hands
entries: While animated.
A Crown-Bound Object can manipulate itself and nearby objects with whatever precision is necessary to fulfill a command.
It doesn't require literal hands.
When it makes an Ability Check involving a Skill or Tool with which you are proficient, it can add your Proficiency Bonus.
If you have Expertise with that Skill or Tool, it can instead add twice your Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Eyes of the Crown
entries: Until you stop perceiving through the object.
You can perceive through any Crown-Bound Object you control.
You can freely switch between your own senses, one Crown-Bound Object, or another Crown-Bound Object. Switching requires no Action.
You can use the senses listed in its stat block and any additional senses or sensory functions belonging to the original target.
You remain aware of your own surroundings unless you deliberately choose to focus entirely through the object.

entries.name: One Crown, Many Bodies
entries: While animated.
Your Crown-Bound Objects can coordinate perfectly with one another.

They can synchronize attacks, surround targets, create formations, divide complicated work, pass materials between one another, operate machines together, synchronize movement, avoid accidentally obstructing each other, and cooperate without verbal communication.
They understand the intended actions of your other Crown-Bound Objects on the same plane of existence.

entries.name: Combined Strength
entries: While cooperating on the same task.
Any number of Crown-Bound Objects can combine their physical capacities when working toward the same goal.
Their capabilities can be combined when determining what they can collectively carry, lift, push, drag, support, restrain, hold in place, construct, or dismantle.

entries.name: Command the Function
entries: While animated.
A Crown-Bound Object can independently activate and use any function genuinely belonging to itself.

This can include Magic Item properties, built-in spells, charges, command-word effects, activated weapon properties, siege weapon functions, vehicles, mechanisms, traps, magical devices, technological systems, and other native activated functions.
The object can fulfill the role of its own wielder, wearer, rider, driver, or operator.
It can press its own controls, pull its own triggers, speak its own command words where necessary, aim itself, and operate itself.
Actual resources such as ammunition, charges, fuel, or consumable components are still spent normally.

entries.name: No Operator Required
entries: While animated.
A Crown-Bound Object doesn't need another creature to hold, wear, wield, ride, or operate it in order to use a function that belongs to itself.
This doesn't give the object functions it never possessed.

entries.name: Endless Labor
entries: While its command remains active.
Crown-Bound Objects don't suffer Exhaustion from ordinary physical labor.

They can continuously perform construction, excavation, repairs, transportation, manufacturing, harvesting, fortification, demolition, maintenance, loading and unloading, cleaning, sorting, and similar labor.
They still require materials, fuel, tools, or other resources when those things are genuinely necessary.

entries.name: Coordinated Command
entries: You can issue the same command to any number of Crown-Bound Objects simultaneously.
There is no numerical limit to the number of objects that can receive that shared command.

entries.name: Command the Mindless
entries: You can use Assume Command against a mindless creature even if it can't hear or understand language.
A creature with no genuine independent will automatically fails its Saving Throw.
You can command its movement, Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, attacks, spells, supernatural abilities, target selection, object interactions, and other capabilities.
A creature possessing genuine independent will makes its Saving Throw normally.

entries.name: Decree Upon Matter
entries: Prerequisite: Imperishable Decree.
Use Imperishable Decree's action economy.
Permanent.
You can place an Imperishable Decree upon objects, natural matter, structures, mechanisms, Crown-Bound Objects, mindless creatures, and other eligible nonthinking targets.
A genuinely mindless target makes no Wisdom Saving Throw.
The decree binds the target's physical form and supernatural essence.
If fulfilling the decree requires an otherwise motionless target to act, it can automatically animate as a Crown-Bound Object whenever necessary.
When no action is required, the target can become motionless again without ending its permanent decree.

entries.name: Level 5: Awakened Instruments
entries: Permanent.
When you gain this Invocation, all of its base abilities become available.

Your Crown can animate objects and natural matter, grant them independent movement and action, allow them to use their own functions, coordinate them, perceive through them, and command mindless beings.

entries.name: Command the Possessed
entries: Your Crown features can target objects that are worn, wielded, carried, held, mounted, installed, operated, or otherwise actively possessed.
This includes weapons, armor, shields, Magic Items, Spellcasting Focuses, equipment, tools, containers, ammunition, and vehicles.
If your command directly opposes a creature's physical control over the object, that creature makes a Strength or Dexterity Saving Throw of its choice against your Spell Save DC.
On a failed save, the object obeys you.

entries.name: Rebellion of Property
entries: While the command remains active.
A commanded object can actively work against its possessor.
Weapons can pull away from attacks, armor can restrict its wearer, shields can expose their bearer, and vehicles can reject their drivers.
If the object can physically separate from its possessor, it can animate as a Crown-Bound Object and leave.

entries.name: Level 9: The Crown Uses All Things
Sovereign Activation
entries: Use the object's ability's action economy.
While animated or acting under your Crown authority.

A Crown-Bound Object can activate its own abilities even when they would normally require Attunement, a particular class, a particular species, a particular Ability Score, a command word, a wielder, a wearer, or another creature operating it.
The object counts as satisfying those requirements for the purpose of using its own abilities.
This doesn't make you personally attuned to the object.

entries.name: The Crown Supplies the Wielder
entries: While Sovereign Activation applies.
If an object's ability requires a wielder's Attack Bonus or Save DC but doesn't provide one itself, use the following values:
Attack Bonus = the object's appropriate Ability modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.
Save DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + the object's appropriate Ability modifier.
If the object already has a superior fixed Attack Bonus or Save DC, it can use the superior value.

entries.name: Unerring Operation
entries: While under your Crown authority.
A Crown-Bound Object automatically understands how to operate its own functions.
You don't need to personally understand how the object works.
This doesn't automatically give that technical knowledge to you.

entries.name: Level 13: Ownership Is a Lesser Law
Override the Bond
entries: For the duration of the Crown command that established control.
Your authority can contest supernatural effects determining who controls an object, owns it, commands it, can activate it, can recall it, or is permitted to use it.

This includes Attunement bonds, magical ownership restrictions, creator-only controls, bonded weapons, summoned weapons, remote control, magical recall effects, curses governing an object's actions, controlled Constructs, and similar supernatural claims.

If another creature actively controls the object, make a contested check: you make a Charisma Check and add your Proficiency Bonus; the opposing controller uses the Ability modifier used by its controlling feature and adds its Proficiency Bonus, if any.
If no creature can reasonably make the opposing check, use 10 + the effect's spell level, or 10 + its creator's Proficiency Bonus if no spell level exists and that Proficiency Bonus is known.
On a success, your Crown takes precedence.

entries.name: The Object Chooses the Crown
entries: While Override the Bond remains active.

While you successfully override another bond, its former controller can't command it, recall effects can't remove it from your control, another creature can't activate it without your permission, and effects attempting to force it to violate your command fail.
The suppressed original bond isn't necessarily destroyed and can resume when your Crown control ends.

entries.name: Relics Must Kneel Too
entries: Permanent modification to Override the Bond.
Magic Items and Artifacts aren't automatically immune to this feature solely because of their rarity or power.
If an object possesses a genuine independent sentient will, that will can resist your Crown normally.

entries.name: Mass Edict
entries: Activating this feature requires an Action.
Up to 1 hour.
Choose a point you can perceive within 1 mile.
Choose any number of eligible objects, structures, or masses of nonliving matter within 1 mile of that point.
Every chosen target can immediately animate if necessary and receive a command from you.
There is no numerical limit and no Size limit. Tiny objects through Gargantuan structures or masses of material can all be affected.
You can freely exclude anything you don't wish to command.

entries.name: One Voice, Countless Bodies
entries: While Mass Edict lasts.
You can communicate commands to every affected target throughout the area regardless of ordinary hearing distance.
You can command all of them together, divide them into groups, assign different commands to different groups, command individual objects, or replace existing instructions.

entries.name: A Living Domain
entries: While Mass Edict lasts.
Affected objects can coordinate as one enormous workforce or army.
They can perform large-scale combat, construction, evacuation, repair, transportation, excavation, searching, fortification, manufacturing, infrastructure maintenance, and logistics.

entries.name: The Crown Does Not Tire
entries: While Mass Edict lasts.
Mass Edict requires no Concentration.
Becoming Incapacitated doesn't automatically end commands already issued, although you can't issue new commands while unable to act.

entries.name: Titan Convergence
entries: Activating this feature requires an Action.
Up to 1 hour.
Choose one point you can perceive within 1 mile.

Choose any number of eligible targets within 1 mile of that point, including Crown-Bound Objects, ordinary objects, weapons, armor, vehicles, machinery, siege equipment, magical objects, statues, corpses, mindless Constructs, structures, sections of structures, rubble, earth, soil, stone, sand, clay, minerals, ore, raw metal, crystal, ice, snow, bone, dead wood, and other eligible nonliving matter.
Command the selected material to converge on the chosen point.
Things incapable of moving automatically animate as necessary. Loose matter can rise, flow, fly, crawl, or otherwise travel toward the convergence point.
When sufficient material reaches the point, it forms one Crownforged Titan.
A single use of Titan Convergence creates one Titan.
The components don't need to share the same material, origin, purpose, Size, shape, or magical nature.

entries.name: Crownforged Titan
entries: For the remainder of Titan Convergence.

Choose whichever stat block is appropriate to the amount of material gathered: {@creature Huge Crownforged Titan|FftForbiddenTome} or {@creature Gargantuan Crownforged Titan|FftForbiddenTome}. Both are CR 24.
The Titan uses its dedicated Crownforged Titan stat block and obeys your Crown absolutely.

entries.name: The Whole Remembers Its Parts
entries: While the Crownforged Titan exists.
Components incorporated into the Titan retain usable functions when those functions can still reasonably operate.

Weapons remain weapons, siege equipment can still fire, Magic Items can retain appropriate abilities, engines and machinery can still function, chains can restrain, armor can reinforce the Titan, and natural matter contributes physical mass and structure.
Consumable resources such as charges, ammunition, or fuel remain consumable normally.

entries.name: Titan Attack Authority
entries: Instantaneous for each attack.
This formula applies only to Crownforged Titans, not ordinary Crown-Bound Objects.
The Titan's Attack Bonus equals the Titan's relevant Ability modifier + the Titan's Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus.
Its damage equals the attack's damage dice + the Titan's relevant Ability modifier + the Titan's Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus.
Its abilities use the Save DC specified by the Titan stat block: 20 + your Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: When Titan Convergence Ends
entries: Instantaneous when triggered.
When the 1-hour duration ends, or when you voluntarily command the Titan to separate, its surviving components detach.
Objects and materials return to being separate things.
Anything still maintained by another Crown feature can immediately resume functioning under that effect.
Damage actually suffered during the Titan's existence can leave individual components damaged, broken, scattered, or destroyed as appropriate.

optionalfeature.name: Relic Assimilation
entries: The Arsenal does not merely preserve enchanted weapons. It learns them.
Every relic placed within it becomes another principle of violence written into the whole armory.
A single legendary edge can teach a thousand lesser weapons how to bite.

entries.name: Arsenal Relics
entries: When you finish a Long Rest, choose a number of eligible Magic Items stored within your Arsenal up to your Proficiency Bonus. The chosen items become your Arsenal Relics until you choose again when you finish a Long Rest.
An eligible item must be a weapon, ammunition, or a Magic Item whose magical properties directly modify a weapon or weapon attack.

entries.name: Total Assimilation
