entries: While you wield or make an attack with any weapon from your Arsenal, that weapon can use every applicable magical property of all your Arsenal Relics simultaneously.
For those properties, the Arsenal weapon counts as each Arsenal Relic whenever a property refers to "this weapon," "the weapon," or otherwise requires the effect to originate from that relic.

entries.name: Relic Without Form
entries: A copied property isn't restricted by the Arsenal Relic's original weapon type, ammunition type, damage type, reach, or range unless the property would be impossible to resolve without that requirement.
If a property requires a melee attack, ranged attack, thrown attack, Critical Hit, specific target, or another condition created by the attack itself, you must still satisfy that condition.

entries.name: Convergent Enchantments
entries: Properties from different Arsenal Relics can function on the same attack and their benefits are cumulative, including bonuses to attack rolls, damage rolls, additional damage, Critical Hit effects, and other effects triggered by an attack.
A property with the same name from multiple Arsenal Relics doesn't stack with itself unless it explicitly says otherwise.

entries.name: Shared Activation
entries: If an Arsenal Relic has a property you can activate while holding, wielding, attacking with, or otherwise using that item, you can activate it through any weapon from your Arsenal as though you were using the Arsenal Relic.
If the property creates an effect from the relic, you can have that effect originate from the Arsenal weapon you're currently using.

entries.name: One Relic, One Resource
entries: The Arsenal shares power, not resources. Charges, limited uses, Recharge, once-per-turn limits, once-per-round limits, and other usage limits remain tied to the original Arsenal Relic.
Using that property through any Arsenal weapon expends or counts against the original Arsenal Relic's resource normally.

entries.name: Bound Requirements
entries: You must still satisfy an Arsenal Relic's Attunement requirement and any requirement based on the wielder, such as class, creature type, alignment, ability score, or another quality of the wielder.
Once you satisfy those requirements, every weapon in your Arsenal is treated as satisfying that item's weapon-specific requirements for the copied property.

entries.name: Transcendent Attunement
entries: As your bond with the Arsenal deepens, the Arsenal learns to sustain relics in your place.
At 7th level, one of your Arsenal Relics can function through this Invocation even if you are not Attuned to it.
At 11th level, up to two of your Arsenal Relics can ignore their Attunement requirements this way.
At 15th level, up to three of your Arsenal Relics can ignore their Attunement requirements this way.
At 17th level, all of your Arsenal Relics can function through this Invocation without requiring Attunement.

Ignoring Attunement this way applies only while the item is one of your Arsenal Relics and only to properties used through Relic Assimilation. It doesn't make you Attuned to the item, grant its normal benefits outside the Arsenal, or increase your number of Attunement slots.

entries.name: Relic Remains Whole
entries: An Arsenal Relic isn't consumed, destroyed, stripped of its magic, or permanently altered by this Invocation.
It remains a normal Magic Item and can still be summoned and used directly.

optionalfeature.name: Arsenal Instinct
entries: The Arsenal watches every clash.
It learns what fails, what pierces, and what kind of weapon the next moment demands.
Before long, you no longer choose the right weapon—the Arsenal does.

entries.name: Predatory Selection
entries: Whenever you miss a creature with a weapon from your Arsenal, or the creature reduces the damage of that attack through Resistance or Immunity, you can immediately return that weapon to the Arsenal and summon another stored weapon into the same hand. The replacement requires no action.
Until the end of your turn, your first attack against that creature with the replacement weapon has Advantage.

entries.name: Learned Weakness
entries: Once you damage a creature with a weapon from your Arsenal, the Arsenal remembers that creature until the end of your next Long Rest.
For a remembered creature, the Arsenal learns how that creature responds to damage dealt by your Arsenal, including any Resistance, Immunity, or Vulnerability revealed by those attacks.

entries.name: Adaptive Armament
entries: Whenever you make a weapon attack against a remembered creature using a weapon from your Arsenal, the Arsenal can alter that attack's damage type to the most effective damage type against that creature.
If the creature has one or more Vulnerabilities, the attack becomes a damage type to which it is Vulnerable.
If it has no Vulnerabilities, the Arsenal instead chooses a damage type that the creature neither Resists nor is Immune to, if one is available.
You don't need to know what damage type was chosen beforehand. The Arsenal determines the most effective option automatically when the attack hits.
The available damage types are Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, Necrotic, Piercing, Poison, Psychic, Radiant, Slashing, and Thunder.

entries.name: Perfect Answer
entries: Starting at 11th level, attacks altered by Adaptive Armament also ignore Resistance to the chosen damage type.
Starting at 17th level, if the creature has no Vulnerability, the chosen damage type treats the creature as though it had Vulnerability to that damage for that attack.

optionalfeature.name: Adaptive Arsenal
entries: No weapon leaves the Arsenal unchanged.
Each one is refined for the exact moment it is called.
What you draw is not merely a stored weapon, but the version of it the battle demands.

entries.name: Mutable Armament
entries: Whenever you summon a weapon from your Arsenal, choose one of the following properties: Finesse, Light, Thrown (20/60), Reach, or Versatile (1d10). The weapon gains the chosen property until it returns to the Arsenal.
If the weapon already has the chosen property, choose another.

entries.name: Greater Adaptation
entries: Starting at 7th level, choose two properties whenever you summon the weapon.
Starting at 13th level, choose three properties whenever you summon the weapon.

entries.name: Perfect Form
entries: Starting at 17th level, when you summon a weapon, you can also change its normal weapon damage die to 1d12 if it would normally be lower.
If the weapon normally rolls multiple weapon damage dice, you can instead change each of those dice to 1d8.

entries.name: Arsenal Mastery
entries: Whenever you summon a weapon from your Arsenal, you can choose which Weapon Mastery property you use with that weapon from among any Weapon Mastery properties you know.
You can choose again each time the weapon is summoned.

optionalfeature.name: Echoed Form
entries: The Mirror studies not what you are, but how you act.
A spell, a strike, a dash, a gesture—each leaves behind a perfect pattern.
For a moment, that pattern can be called upon again.

entries.name: Reflected Action
entries: Once on each of your turns after you take an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, the Mirror records the form of that action until the start of your next turn.
Before the reflection fades, you can use it once to repeat the same type of action without using its normal action cost.
The repeated action must be one you could currently perform and must obey all of its normal requirements.

entries.name: Shared Expenditure
entries: Repeating an action this way doesn't duplicate resources.
If the repeated action would expend a spell slot, class resource, item charge, limited-use feature, ammunition, Hit Die, or another expendable resource, you must expend that resource again normally.

entries.name: Mirrored Execution
entries: The repeated action doesn't need to target the same creature, point, or object.
If it includes an attack, spell, movement, Grapple, Shove, item interaction, or another effect, you can choose new legal targets and resolve it normally.

entries.name: Perfect Echo
entries: Starting at 11th level, you can maintain two different recorded actions at once.

Starting at 17th level, once on each of your turns, the first reflected action you repeat doesn't expend a limited-use class or subclass resource, though it still requires spell slots, item charges, ammunition, or other external resources normally.

monster.name: Tiny Crown-Bound Object

ac.special: 15 or the object's original AC, whichever is higher or more appropriate

hp.special: 5 + three times your level, or the object's original Hit Points if higher or more appropriate

languages: understands your commands but can't speak unless its physical form permits it

trait.name: Original Object
entries: Animation doesn't reshape the object or replace what it already is. It retains its original physical form, material, Armor Class, Hit Points, ability scores, saving throws, skills, movement speeds, resistances, immunities, vulnerabilities, senses, weapon properties, magical properties, traits, attacks, damage dice, special actions, and other existing abilities.

If the original object has an Armor Class higher than 15, use the original Armor Class. If it has Hit Points or another statistic that is higher or more appropriate than this stat block, use the original value instead. This stat block fills in statistics the object lacks and never weakens superior native statistics.

trait.name: Bound to the Crown
entries: The object obeys your commands absolutely and understands the meaning and intent of those commands despite lacking ordinary intelligence. This doesn't make it sapient or give it an independent personality.
Once given a command, it continues carrying out that command without requiring further actions from you.

trait.name: Object Nature
entries: The object doesn't need to breathe, eat, drink, or sleep.

While animated, it counts as a Construct for effects that require a creature type, and it also remains an object for effects specifically concerning objects, structures, materials, weapons, armor, or similar things.

trait.name: Floating Servant
entries: The object has a flying speed of 40 feet and can hover, regardless of its original shape. If it already possesses a faster appropriate speed, it can retain that speed. This movement doesn't transform the object.

trait.name: Initiative
entries: The object takes its turn immediately after yours. If multiple Crown-Bound Objects act at the same time, you determine their order.
The object doesn't require your Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction to take its turn or continue following an existing command.

trait.name: Native Attacks
entries: If the object already possesses an attack, it can use that attack instead of Crown Strike. The attack retains its normal damage dice, modifiers, range, reach, additional damage, magical properties, riders, and special effects.

trait.name: Object Forms
entries: A Form describes what the object's existing shape is naturally capable of doing. Choosing or applying a Form doesn't transform or reshape the object.

An object can qualify for more than one Form at the same time if its actual construction supports them, such as a halberd qualifying as Edged and Piercing or a spiked chain qualifying as Piercing and Grasping.

trait.name: Edged Form
entries: Examples include swords, axes, saws, blades, sharpened metal, and broken glass. Crown Strike deals slashing damage when this Form is used.

Once per turn when the object hits with an attack, it deals additional slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. When it scores a Critical Hit, roll one additional normal damage die of the attack.

trait.name: Piercing Form
entries: Examples include spears, spikes, needles, arrows, lances, and pointed debris. Crown Strike deals piercing damage when this Form is used.
The object's melee reach increases by 5 feet while using a piercing portion of its form.
Once per turn when it hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, that creature can't willingly move farther away from the object until the start of the object's next turn.

trait.name: Crushing Form
entries: Examples include hammers, mauls, rocks, statues, furniture, blocks of stone, and machinery. Crown Strike deals bludgeoning damage when this Form is used.

Once per turn when the object hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, choose one: push the creature 5 feet, knock it prone, or move it up to 5 feet to an unoccupied space within the object's reach.

trait.name: Guardian Form
entries: Examples include shields, armor, doors, wall sections, barricades, and metal plates. Crown Strike normally deals bludgeoning damage when this Form is used unless the object's actual form suggests otherwise.

trait.name: Grasping Form
entries: Examples include chains, ropes, vines, cloth, cables, and articulated mechanical arms.

When the object hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, it can immediately attempt to grapple the target as part of the same attack. The escape DC equals 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + the object's Strength modifier. If Dexterity better represents how the object binds the target, use its Dexterity modifier instead.
The object can continue attacking while maintaining the grapple if its physical form permits it.

trait.name: Projectile Form
entries: Examples include bows, crossbows, firearms, ballistae, launchers, and throwing weapons. The object retains its actual range, ammunition requirements, weapon properties, damage, and magical properties.

When making a native ranged attack, the object can use its Dexterity modifier + your Proficiency Bonus as the attack bonus instead of its normal attack bonus. Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on its ranged attacks.

action.name: Crown Strike
entries: {@atk mw} The attack bonus equals the object's Strength or Dexterity modifier, whichever is appropriate for the attack, + your Proficiency Bonus; reach is determined by the object's actual form, one target. {@h}{@damage 1d4} + the same Strength or Dexterity modifier + your Proficiency Bonus damage.

The damage type is determined by the object's actual physical form, typically bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing. If another damage type is more appropriate because of the object's original magical or physical properties, use that type instead.

reaction.name: Interpose (Guardian Form Only)
entries: When another creature within the object's reach is hit by an attack, the object can move up to half its flying speed toward that creature without provoking opportunity attacks from the attacker and interpose itself.
Reduce the triggering attack's damage by your Proficiency Bonus + the object's Constitution modifier. If this reduces the damage to 0, the protected creature takes no damage from the attack.

This stat block fills in statistics the object lacks and never weakens superior native statistics.

trait.name: Bound to the Crown
entries: The object obeys your commands absolutely and understands the meaning and intent of those commands despite lacking ordinary intelligence. This doesn't make it sapient or give it an independent personality.
Once given a command, it continues carrying out that command without requiring further actions from you.

trait.name: Object Nature
entries: The object doesn't need to breathe, eat, drink, or sleep.

While animated, it counts as a Construct for effects that require a creature type, and it also remains an object for effects specifically concerning objects, structures, materials, weapons, armor, or similar things.

trait.name: Floating Servant
entries: The object has a flying speed of 20 feet and can hover, regardless of its original shape. If it already possesses a faster appropriate speed, it can retain that speed. This movement doesn't transform the object.

trait.name: Initiative
entries: The object takes its turn immediately after yours. If multiple Crown-Bound Objects act at the same time, you determine their order.
The object doesn't require your Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction to take its turn or continue following an existing command.

trait.name: Native Attacks
entries: If the object already possesses an attack, it can use that attack instead of Crown Strike. The attack retains its normal damage dice, modifiers, range, reach, additional damage, magical properties, riders, and special effects.

trait.name: Object Forms
entries: A Form describes what the object's existing shape is naturally capable of doing. Choosing or applying a Form doesn't transform or reshape the object.

An object can qualify for more than one Form at the same time if its actual construction supports them, such as a halberd qualifying as Edged and Piercing or a spiked chain qualifying as Piercing and Grasping.

trait.name: Edged Form
entries: Examples include swords, axes, saws, blades, sharpened metal, and broken glass. Crown Strike deals slashing damage when this Form is used.

Once per turn when the object hits with an attack, it deals additional slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. When it scores a Critical Hit, roll one additional normal damage die of the attack.

trait.name: Piercing Form
entries: Examples include spears, spikes, needles, arrows, lances, and pointed debris. Crown Strike deals piercing damage when this Form is used.
The object's melee reach increases by 20 feet while using a piercing portion of its form.
Once per turn when it hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, that creature can't willingly move farther away from the object until the start of the object's next turn.

trait.name: Crushing Form
entries: Examples include hammers, mauls, rocks, statues, furniture, blocks of stone, and machinery. Crown Strike deals bludgeoning damage when this Form is used.

Once per turn when the object hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, choose one: push the creature 20 feet, knock it prone, or move it up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space within the object's reach.

trait.name: Guardian Form
entries: Examples include shields, armor, doors, wall sections, barricades, and metal plates. Crown Strike normally deals bludgeoning damage when this Form is used unless the object's actual form suggests otherwise.

trait.name: Grasping Form
entries: Examples include chains, ropes, vines, cloth, cables, and articulated mechanical arms.

When the object hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, it can immediately attempt to grapple the target as part of the same attack. The escape DC equals 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + the object's Strength modifier. If Dexterity better represents how the object binds the target, use its Dexterity modifier instead.
The object can continue attacking while maintaining the grapple if its physical form permits it.

trait.name: Projectile Form
entries: Examples include bows, crossbows, firearms, ballistae, launchers, and throwing weapons. The object retains its actual range, ammunition requirements, weapon properties, damage, and magical properties.

When making a native ranged attack, the object can use its Dexterity modifier + your Proficiency Bonus as the attack bonus instead of its normal attack bonus. Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on its ranged attacks.

trait.name: Monumental Mass
entries: The object counts as two sizes larger when determining its carrying capacity and the weight it can push, drag, or lift whenever that distinction can apply.
It has advantage on Strength and Constitution ability checks and saving throws.

trait.name: Living Fortress
entries: When its physical shape permits, creatures can stand on it, climb it, use it as a platform, take cover behind it, or move across it as terrain. Its movement can transport creatures and objects physically standing on or attached to it.

trait.name: Siege Sovereign
entries: The object deals quadruple damage to objects and structures.

action.name: Crown Strike
entries: {@atk mw} The attack bonus equals the object's Strength or Dexterity modifier, whichever is appropriate for the attack, + your Proficiency Bonus; reach is determined by the object's actual form, one target. {@h}{@damage 1d4} + the same Strength or Dexterity modifier + your Proficiency Bonus damage.

The damage type is determined by the object's actual physical form, typically bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing. If another damage type is more appropriate because of the object's original magical or physical properties, use that type instead.

reaction.name: Interpose (Guardian Form Only)
entries: When another creature within the object's reach is hit by an attack, the object can move up to half its flying speed toward that creature without provoking opportunity attacks from the attacker and interpose itself.
Reduce the triggering attack's damage by your Proficiency Bonus + the object's Constitution modifier. If this reduces the damage to 0, the protected creature takes no damage from the attack.

monster.name: Huge Crownforged Titan
languages: understands your commands; can't speak unless incorporated components allow it

trait.name: Absolute Servitor
entries: The Titan obeys your commands absolutely. It acts immediately after your turn and requires no Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction from you to continue carrying out an existing command.
It understands the meaning and intent of your commands and can independently determine how to fulfill them. It doesn't become Sapient or develop an independent will.

trait.name: Titan Save DC
entries: Whenever a Crownforged Titan ability requires a Saving Throw, the save DC equals 20 + your Proficiency Bonus unless that ability explicitly states otherwise.

trait.name: Titan Attack Formula
entries: This formula applies only to Crownforged Titans.
Whenever the Titan makes an attack, its Attack Bonus equals the Titan's relevant Ability modifier + its Proficiency Bonus (+6) + your Proficiency Bonus.
Its attack damage equals the attack's damage dice + the Titan's relevant Ability modifier + its Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus.

trait.name: The Whole Remembers Its Parts
entries: The Titan retains usable properties of incorporated components whenever those functions can still reasonably operate. This can include Magic Item properties, magical weapons, built-in spells, command-word abilities, siege weapons, firearms, launchers, engines, machinery, vehicles, armor, shields, chains, restraints, magical devices, technological systems, special materials, traps, and other functional components.
The Titan can operate these components itself. Charges, ammunition, fuel, consumable components, and similar resources are still consumed normally.

trait.name: Sovereign Magic Immunity
entries: The Titan is immune to spells and magical effects unless you choose for that specific effect to affect it.
This immunity doesn't interfere with your Crown features, the Titan's own abilities, magic belonging to incorporated components, or effects you voluntarily permit.
If an effect would normally have a reduced effect on a successful Saving Throw, it instead has no effect on the Titan unless you allow it.

trait.name: Sovereign Adamantine Body
entries: The Titan is immune to all damage caused by nonmagical attacks, regardless of the damage type dealt by that attack.
An attack must be magical or otherwise supernatural to bypass this immunity. After bypassing it, the Titan's other Damage Resistances and Damage Immunities still apply.

trait.name: Immutable Sovereign Form
entries: Unless you allow it, the Titan can't be transformed, polymorphed, petrified, forcibly changed in Size, merged into another creature or object, magically disassembled, forced to rearrange its components, partially teleported apart, or reshaped by another effect.
Only your Crown authority can voluntarily reconfigure or separate it.

trait.name: Absolute Mass
entries: Unless you allow it, the Titan can't be Grappled, knocked Prone, Shoved, forcibly moved, forcibly teleported, carried, dragged, lifted, or physically Restrained.
An effect that moves the entire surrounding region, plane, or structure can still move the Titan as part of that larger movement.

trait.name: Indestructible Convergence
entries: At the start of each of the Titan's turns, it regains 120 Hit Points.
This regeneration functions even while the Titan has 0 Hit Points. If it starts its turn at 0 Hit Points and eligible material remains available to constitute it, it regains Hit Points and reforms.
Reducing the Titan to 0 Hit Points doesn't automatically destroy it.

trait.name: Matter Feeds the Titan
entries: Whenever the Titan regenerates, it can draw eligible unattended nonliving matter within 120 feet into itself.

Eligible matter includes earth, soil, stone, sand, clay, rubble, minerals, raw metal, crystal, ice, snow, bone, dead wood, destroyed objects, damaged machinery, broken weapons, and other suitable nonliving matter.
The material moves toward the Titan and becomes part of its body. The Titan doesn't require its original components in order to continue rebuilding itself.

trait.name: Crownforged Weapons
entries: All of the Titan's attacks count as magical.
Whenever the Titan deals damage, it ignores Resistance to that damage. Immunity to that damage is treated as Resistance, and the Titan ignores that Resistance as well.

trait.name: Siege Incarnate
entries: The Titan deals four times normal damage to objects and structures.

trait.name: Unstoppable Advance
entries: The Titan can move through walls, fortifications, buildings, barricades, ordinary structures, unattended objects, and other noncreature physical barriers without spending additional movement.
It can smash the material apart, push it aside, incorporate it into itself, or leave a passage behind.

trait.name: Colossal Reach
entries: The Titan has a base melee Reach of 15 feet unless an incorporated component reasonably grants greater Reach.

trait.name: Living Mass
entries: The Titan can carry creatures, vehicles, structures, and objects on or inside its body when its shape permits.
Creatures can use sufficiently large portions of it as terrain, platforms, climbing surfaces, Half Cover, or Three-Quarters Cover.

trait.name: Titan Configuration
entries: Action Economy to change Configuration: Bonus Action.
This configuration lasts until it is changed again or the Titan ends.

When the Titan forms, choose one Configuration: War Titan, Fortress Titan, Siege Titan, Grasping Titan, or Devouring Titan. Changing Configuration rearranges the positions of existing components without changing their substance.

trait.name: War Titan
entries: Multiattack: the Titan makes 3 Titan Strikes.

Once per turn when Titan Strike hits, the target must succeed on a Strength Saving Throw against the Titan Save DC or you choose one of the following: push it 30 feet, knock it Prone, throw it to an unoccupied space within 30 feet, or force it to drop all objects it is holding.

trait.name: Fortress Titan
entries: The Titan gains +3 AC while in this Configuration.
Allies positioned on, within, or behind suitable portions of the Titan can gain Three-Quarters Cover.
Hostile creatures treat the area within the Titan's Reach as Difficult Terrain.

trait.name: Siege Titan
entries: The Titan can independently operate all incorporated siege weapons, firearms, launchers, magical ranged weapons, and similar ranged mechanisms that remain functional.

trait.name: Grasping Titan
entries: The Titan can simultaneously Grapple a number of creatures equal to your Proficiency Bonus + the Titan's Proficiency Bonus.
The escape DC for these Grapples equals the Titan Save DC.

trait.name: Devouring Titan
entries: Consume Matter can be used as a Bonus Action.

The Titan can draw eligible unattended matter within 20 feet into itself. It regains Hit Points equal to 5 × your level × the Size value of the absorbed material (Tiny 1, Small 2, Medium 3, Large 4, Huge 5, Gargantuan 6), up to its Hit Point maximum.

Endless Reconstruction — At the start of the Titan's turn, if eligible matter exists within 30 feet, it can absorb some of it and regain 60 Hit Points. This healing is in addition to Indestructible Convergence.

trait.name: Break Apart
entries: You can command the Titan to separate. Its surviving components detach and return to their original objects or materials. Any component maintained by another Crown effect can immediately resume functioning under that effect.

trait.name: Reconstruction at 0 Hit Points
entries: Reaching 0 Hit Points doesn't automatically end Titan Convergence. Because of Indestructible Convergence, the Titan can reconstruct itself at the start of its next turn if sufficient eligible material remains.
If Titan Convergence ends or the Titan can no longer reconstruct itself, its remaining components collapse into the spaces it occupied.

action.name: Titan Strike
entries: While in War Titan Configuration, the Titan can replace one attack of its Multiattack with this action.
Make a melee attack using the Titan Attack Formula. On a hit, the attack deals 4d12 + the Titan's relevant Ability modifier + its Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus damage.
The damage can be Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing according to the incorporated component used, or another justified damage type supplied by an incorporated magical component.

action.name: World-Crushing Trample
entries: The Titan can use this as part of its movement.
Limit: Once per turn per creature.
The Titan can move through the spaces of creatures smaller than itself.

The first time it enters a creature's space on a turn, that creature must succeed on a Dexterity Saving Throw against the Titan Save DC or take 8d12 + the Titan's Strength modifier + its Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus Bludgeoning damage, be knocked Prone, and either be pushed to an unoccupied space adjacent to the Titan's path or carried beneath or within the Titan's moving mass until the movement ends.
On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and is moved to the nearest available space outside the Titan's path.

action.name: Sovereign Breach
entries: The Titan can replace one attack of its Multiattack with this action.

The Titan can directly attack a magical barrier, ward, boundary, or supernatural obstruction within its Reach, including magical walls, walls of force, magical cages, magical domes, sealed magical doors, supernatural shields, wards preventing passage, barriers preventing teleportation, dimensional boundaries, magical prison walls, and similar effects.

For Sovereign Breach, such a barrier counts as something the Titan can physically attack even if its rules state that it can't be damaged, has no Hit Points, is immune to damage, can't be physically interacted with, can only be removed by a particular spell, or normally can't be destroyed by attacks.
Make an attack using the Titan Attack Formula. If the effect has an AC, use it. Otherwise its AC is 10 + the spell or effect's level, or 20 if it has no meaningful level.

On a hit, the magical barrier is shattered. If it is a single continuous barrier, the entire barrier ends. If it is an exceptionally large magical structure, the Titan destroys a section up to a 30-foot Cube with each successful Breach Attack.

Sovereign Breach ignores Damage Resistance, Damage Immunity, damage reduction, immunity to physical interaction, and requirements that only a particular spell can remove the barrier. The attack counts as both magical and physical for this purpose.

If a boundary prevents entering, leaving, teleporting, crossing dimensions, or passing through a region without physically manifesting, the Titan can attack the boundary itself. A successful Sovereign Breach destroys the restriction in the breached area.

action.name: Siege Barrage (Siege Titan Only)
entries: Choose a point within 300 feet. Each creature in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered there must make a Dexterity Saving Throw against the Titan Save DC.

On a failed save, a creature takes 8d12 + the Titan's Strength modifier + its Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus damage. Choose a damage type appropriate to the incorporated components, such as Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, Fire, or another justified damage type. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage.

action.name: Seize (Grasping Titan Only)
entries: This effect lasts until the Grapple ends.
Choose any number of creatures within the Titan's Reach up to its remaining Grapple capacity. Each target must make a Strength or Dexterity Saving Throw of its choice against the Titan Save DC.
On a failed save, the target is Grappled and Restrained.

bonus.name: Crush the Captive (Grasping Titan Only)
entries: Each creature currently Grappled by the Titan takes 3d12 + the Titan's Strength modifier + its Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus Bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Reconfigure
entries: This configuration lasts until it is changed again or the Titan ends.
Choose War Titan, Fortress Titan, Siege Titan, Grasping Titan, or Devouring Titan. The Titan rearranges its components accordingly and retains its current Hit Points.

reaction.name: Interpose the Fortress (Fortress Titan Only)
entries: When a creature within 30 feet takes damage, the Titan can move up to half its Speed toward that creature and interpose itself.
Reduce the damage by 3d12 + the Titan's Constitution modifier + its Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus. The Titan takes damage equal to the amount prevented.

trait.name: Young Mind, Ancient Blood
entries: The wyrmling is fully sapient but is still a child. It can speak, reason, learn, negotiate, deceive, understand consequences, and make deliberate plans, but it normally lacks the experience, restraint, knowledge, and long-term judgment of older dragons.
A wyrmling isn't automatically a scholar, mastermind, or expert spellcaster.

trait.name: Draconic Magical Instinct
entries: The dragon is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, and supernatural creatures.
This instinct doesn't automatically reveal complete information.

trait.name: Keen Senses
entries: The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: No Change Shape
entries: The wyrmling doesn't possess Change Shape. True dragons of this variant first gain Change Shape at the Young age category.

trait.name: Fire Affinity
entries: When the dragon casts a spell that deals Fire damage, it ignores Resistance to Fire damage.
A creature with Immunity to Fire damage remains immune.

trait.name: Innate Elemental Casting
entries: When the dragon casts a spell whose primary damage type is Fire, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed its Proficiency Bonus.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: Each spell listed as Draconic High Magic can be cast once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the dragon from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.
Draconic High Magic: {@spell burning hands|XPHB}.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.
Their element, temperament, instincts, and accumulated experience shape which spells come naturally to them.
As a dragon grows older, more of that inherited magic becomes effortless.
The dragon knows every spell in the Red Dragon Spell List of a level no higher than 1. Those spells are presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Age turns practiced magic into instinct.
The dragon can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack, if that dragon has Multiattack.
Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell burning hands|XPHB}.

trait.name: Sovereignty of the Burning Hoard
entries: To a red dragon, possession is not a legal concept but a fact of nature.
What it claims becomes part of its identity, and resistance to its authority is treated as a personal insult.
With age, the distinction between its treasure, its territory, and the world it believes it deserves begins to disappear.
{@b Wyrmling — Claimed Treasure.}
The dragon must touch the object for 1 minute to use this feature.
The claim lasts until the dragon willingly releases it.
The dragon can mystically mark up to PB × 10 objects as Claimed Treasure.

trait.name: Growing Draconic Mind
entries: A Young Dragon is fully sapient and has developed considerably beyond the impulsive reasoning of a wyrmling.
It can plan ahead, understand politics and social structures, deliberately manipulate others, study magic, manage servants or territory, and pursue long-term goals.
It is still substantially less experienced than an Adult or Ancient Dragon.

trait.name: Draconic Magical Instinct
entries: The dragon is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena.
Its greater experience allows it to recognize and analyze magic much more reliably than a wyrmling, but this feature doesn't grant automatic knowledge.

trait.name: Keen Senses
entries: The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The dragon can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the dragon ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The dragon magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is equal to or lower than the dragon's own Challenge Rating, or returns to its true form.
The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

While transformed, the dragon retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Draconic Magical Instinct; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The dragon can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the dragon chooses when it transforms.

trait.name: Acid Affinity
entries: When the dragon casts a spell that deals Acid damage, it ignores Resistance to Acid damage.
A creature with Immunity to Acid damage remains immune.

trait.name: Chromatic Orb Restriction
entries: When the dragon casts {@spell chromatic orb|XPHB} through Innate Draconic Spellcasting, it can choose only Acid as the spell's damage type.

trait.name: Innate Elemental Casting
entries: When the dragon casts a spell whose primary damage type is Acid, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed its Proficiency Bonus.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: Each spell listed as Draconic High Magic can be cast once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the dragon from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.
Draconic High Magic: {@spell greater invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell vitriolic sphere|XGE}.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.
Their element, temperament, instincts, and accumulated experience shape which spells come naturally to them.
As a dragon grows older, more of that inherited magic becomes effortless.
The dragon knows every spell in the Black Dragon Spell List of a level no higher than 4. Those spells are presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Age turns practiced magic into instinct.
The dragon can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack, if that dragon has Multiattack.
Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell fog cloud|XPHB}, {@spell chromatic orb|XPHB}, {@spell darkness|XPHB}, {@spell invisibility|XPHB}.

trait.name: Dominion of Ruin
entries: Black dragons don't merely destroy; they prefer to watch things decay.
Civilizations, fortifications, bodies, and promises are simply structures waiting to fail.
The older the dragon becomes, the more destruction itself seems to nourish it.
{@b Wyrmling — Mireborn Predator.}
The dragon ignores Difficult Terrain created by mud, shallow water, swamp, or rotting vegetation.
It can Hide while only Lightly Obscured by swamp vegetation, murky water, fog, or ruins.
{@b Young — Cruel Ambush.}
The healing prevention lasts until the start of the dragon's next turn.
The dragon can take the Hide action as a Bonus Action while it has suitable concealment.
The first time it hits a creature while Hidden or Unseen, the hit deals an extra ({@damage 3d8}) Acid damage, and the target can't regain Hit Points until the start of the dragon's next turn.

entries: Blue dragons regard the sky as a throne and the horizon as the boundary of their court.
Mirage, thunder, sand, and lightning blur together around their territories.

trait.name: Web of the Verdant Lie
entries: Green dragons understand that controlling what someone believes is often more useful than controlling their body.
They collect promises, weaknesses, fears, alliances, and secrets with the same appetite other dragons reserve for gold.
At great age, simply dealing with one becomes dangerous long before initiative is rolled.
{@b Wyrmling — Borrowed Voice.}
Reproducing a learned voice or sound requires an Action.
The dragon remembers the learned voice or sound indefinitely.
After hearing a voice or sound for at least 1 minute, the dragon can reproduce it.
A creature suspicious of the imitation can make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check against the dragon's Spell Save DC.
This doesn't provide perfect supernatural identity copying.
{@b Young — Venomous Bargain.}
This effect lasts for 24 hours.
When a creature willingly makes an explicit promise to the dragon, the dragon can mystically mark that promise.

If the dragon later actually learns that the creature knowingly broke the promise during the duration, it can trigger the mark. The creature takes ({@damage 4d8}) Poison plus ({@damage 4d8}) Psychic damage, and the dragon knows its direction for 1 hour while both remain on the same plane.
This isn't perfect lie detection; the dragon must genuinely learn that the promise was broken.

entries: White dragons may be less scholarly than their kin, but the hunt is a language they understand with terrifying clarity.

Once an elder white dragon decides something is prey, distance becomes a temporary inconvenience.

The dragon moves up to half its Speed toward its Chosen Prey.
This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from the Chosen Prey, and snow and ice don't cost the dragon extra movement during it.

{@b Young — Venomous Bargain.}

When a creature willingly makes an explicit promise to the dragon, the dragon can mystically mark that promise.

If the dragon later actually learns that the creature knowingly broke the promise during the duration, it can trigger the mark. The creature takes ({@damage 4d8}) Poison plus ({@damage 4d8}) Psychic damage, and the dragon knows its direction for 1 hour while both remain on the same plane.

On a success, the dragon learns one broad current reasonably exposed by the creature's behavior: a fear, desire, important loyalty, or immediate goal.

entries: Age has given the dragon more than size.

Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage.
At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature.

entries: Age has given the dragon more than size.

At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature.

Each creature of the dragon's choice within 180 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the wyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The wyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 25 or lower, or returns to its true form.

While transformed, it retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; Saving Throw and Skill proficiencies; languages; personality and memories; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.
It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The wyrm can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The wyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell cone of cold|XPHB}, {@spell wall of ice|XPHB}, {@spell forcecage|XPHB}, {@spell control weather|XPHB}, {@spell time stop|XPHB}, {@spell shapechange|XPHB}, and {@spell wish|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the wyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Innate Elemental Casting
entries: When the wyrm casts a spell whose primary damage type is Cold, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

trait.name: Wyrm Cold Supremacy
entries: The wyrm's Cold damage ignores Cold Resistance.

As a result, the wyrm's Cold damage affects creatures with Cold Resistance or Cold Immunity without reducing the damage.

trait.name: Apex High Magic Recovery
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the wyrm regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic for a spell of 8th level or lower.
A 9th-level Draconic High Magic use still requires a Long Rest to recover.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the wyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 24.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: World-Heart Reignition (1/Long Rest)
entries: When the wyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Breath Weapon; regains 3 expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic, including a 9th-level spell; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.

entries: White dragons may be less scholarly than their kin, but the hunt is a language they understand with terrifying clarity.

The wyrm must spend 1 minute observing a creature, its scent, or its tracks to use this feature.
The effect lasts until replaced.
The dragon marks one creature as its Chosen Prey.
It has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks made to locate or track that creature.

{@b Young — Relentless Pursuit.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
The dragon moves up to half its Speed toward its Chosen Prey.

The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
This effect lasts until the end of the dragon's next turn.

Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the wyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Innate Elemental Casting
entries: When the wyrm casts a spell whose primary damage type is Poison, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

trait.name: Wyrm Poison Supremacy
entries: The wyrm's Poison damage ignores Poison Resistance.
When the wyrm deals Poison damage to a creature with Poison Immunity, that Immunity is treated as Poison Resistance, and the wyrm then ignores that Resistance.
As a result, the wyrm's Poison damage affects creatures with Poison Resistance or Poison Immunity without reducing the damage.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the wyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 24.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: World-Heart Reignition (1/Long Rest)
entries: When the wyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Breath Weapon; regains 3 expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic, including a 9th-level spell; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.
Their element, temperament, instincts, and accumulated experience shape which spells come naturally to them.
As a dragon grows older, more of that inherited magic becomes effortless.
The dragon knows every spell in the Green Dragon Spell List of a level no higher than 9. Those spells are presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Age turns practiced magic into instinct.
The dragon can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack, if that dragon has Multiattack.

Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell disguise self|XPHB}, {@spell ray of sickness|XPHB}, {@spell detect thoughts|XPHB}, {@spell suggestion|XPHB}, {@spell hypnotic pattern|XPHB}, {@spell major image|XPHB}, {@spell charm monster|XGE}, {@spell greater invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell mass suggestion|XPHB}, {@spell project image|XPHB}.

trait.name: Web of the Verdant Lie
entries: Green dragons understand that controlling what someone believes is often more useful than controlling their body.
They collect promises, weaknesses, fears, alliances, and secrets with the same appetite other dragons reserve for gold.
At great age, simply dealing with one becomes dangerous long before initiative is rolled.
{@b Wyrmling — Borrowed Voice.}
Reproducing a learned voice or sound requires an Action.
The dragon remembers the learned voice or sound indefinitely.
After hearing a voice or sound for at least 1 minute, the dragon can reproduce it.
A creature suspicious of the imitation can make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check against the dragon's Spell Save DC.
This doesn't provide perfect supernatural identity copying.
{@b Young — Venomous Bargain.}
This effect lasts for 24 hours.
When a creature willingly makes an explicit promise to the dragon, the dragon can mystically mark that promise.

If the dragon later actually learns that the creature knowingly broke the promise during the duration, it can trigger the mark. The creature takes ({@damage 4d8}) Poison plus ({@damage 4d8}) Psychic damage, and the dragon knows its direction for 1 hour while both remain on the same plane.
This isn't perfect lie detection; the dragon must genuinely learn that the promise was broken.
{@b Adult — Web of Influence.}
After speaking with a creature for at least 1 minute, the dragon can make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check opposed by the creature's Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check.
On a success, the dragon learns one broad current reasonably exposed by the creature's behavior: a fear, desire, important loyalty, or immediate goal.
This doesn't reveal memories or perfectly hidden truths.
{@b Ancient — Forest of False Paths.}
In natural vegetation, forest, swamp, or jungle, the dragon leaves no trail unless it chooses, can't be tracked nonmagically, and can move through nonmagical plants without slowing.
A creature tracking the dragon can be deliberately led onto a false route unless it succeeds on a Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check against the dragon's Spell Save DC.
{@b Wyrm — Every Promise Has Teeth.}

Once per turn, when a creature affected by one of the wyrm's Enchantment spells, Illusion spells, Charmed effects, or Venomous Bargains damages the wyrm or knowingly acts directly against an instruction it accepted, that creature takes ({@damage 8d10}) Poison or Psychic damage (the wyrm's choice).
The creature also can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size.
Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of an apex creature that has survived centuries.
Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage.
At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the dragon's choice within 300 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.

This additional effect occurs only on the initial failed save.

headerEntries: The wyrm's spellcasting ability is Charisma.

It requires no Spellcasting Focus. It can perform Somatic components using its draconic body.
It doesn't require Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wyrm makes five attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail.
The wyrm can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Action.
The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} +18 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d10 + 10}) Piercing damage plus ({@damage 8d8}) Poison damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d6 + 10}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} +18 to hit, reach 35 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d8 + 10}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} +18 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d6 + 10}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Poison Breath {@recharge 4}
entries: The wyrm exhales its breath weapon in a 120-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 26 Constitution Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 32d6}) Poison damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
Wyrm Poison Supremacy applies to this Poison damage.

action.name: Sovereign Toxin
entries: {@atk rs} +17 to hit, range 400 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 16d12}) Poison damage.

The target must succeed on a DC 25 Constitution Saving Throw or, until the end of its next turn, have Disadvantage on Attack Rolls, Ability Checks, and Saving Throws, can't take Reactions, and have its Speed halved.
This attack is magical and counts as a spell attack, but isn't itself a spell.

entries: Blue dragons regard the sky as a throne and the horizon as the boundary of their court.

{@b Wyrmling — Mirage of the Wastes.}
The wyrm can use this feature as an Action.

The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.

If this movement changes whether the attack can legally reach it, the attack is resolved using the dragon's new position.
The dragon can use this Reaction a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.
{@b Adult — Storm Dominion.}

It requires no Spellcasting Focus. It can perform Somatic components using its draconic body.
It doesn't require Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wyrm makes five attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail.
The wyrm can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Action.
The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} +19 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d10 + 10}) Piercing damage plus ({@damage 8d8}) Fire damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} +19 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d6 + 10}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} +19 to hit, reach 35 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d8 + 10}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} +19 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d6 + 10}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Fire Breath {@recharge 4}
entries: The wyrm exhales its breath weapon in a 120-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 27 Dexterity Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 32d6}) Fire damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
Wyrm Fire Supremacy applies to this Fire damage.

action.name: Worldfire
entries: {@atk rs} +19 to hit, range 500 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 16d12}) Fire damage.
This attack is magical and counts as a spell attack, but isn't itself a spell.

legendaryHeader: The wyrm can take 7 Legendary Actions, choosing from the options below. Only one Legendary Action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The wyrm regains spent Legendary Actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Detect
entries: The wyrm makes a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check.

legendary.name: Claw Attack
entries: The wyrm makes one Claw attack.

legendary.name: Tail Attack
entries: The wyrm makes one Tail attack.

legendary.name: Cast Cantrip
entries: The wyrm casts one cantrip.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 25 feet of the wyrm must make a DC 27 Dexterity Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 8d6 + 10}) Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't fall Prone.
The wyrm can then fly up to half its Fly Speed.

legendary.name: Cataclysmic Movement (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The wyrm moves up to its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Each creature the wyrm passes within 20 feet of during this movement must succeed on a DC 27 Dexterity Saving Throw or fall Prone.

legendary.name: Cast Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The wyrm casts one spell of 7th level or lower that normally has a casting time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: Breath Surge (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The wyrm rolls one additional d6 to recharge Fire Breath. If Fire Breath is already available, the wyrm can instead immediately use Fire Breath.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The wyrm casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

monster.name: White Greatwyrm

conditionImmune.note: from effects other than being reduced to 0 Hit Points

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (9/Day)
entries: If the greatwyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Magic Resistance
entries: The greatwyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.
Spell attack rolls against the greatwyrm are made with Disadvantage.

trait.name: Perfect Concentration
entries: The greatwyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the greatwyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The greatwyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 33 or lower, or returns to its true form.

While transformed, it retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; Saving Throw and Skill proficiencies; languages; personality and memories; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.
It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The greatwyrm can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The greatwyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell cone of cold|XPHB}, {@spell wall of ice|XPHB}, {@spell forcecage|XPHB}, {@spell control weather|XPHB}, {@spell foresight|XPHB}, {@spell time stop|XPHB}, {@spell shapechange|XPHB}, and {@spell wish|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the greatwyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Innate Elemental Casting
entries: When the greatwyrm casts a spell whose primary damage type is Cold, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Cold Supremacy
entries: The greatwyrm's Cold damage ignores Resistance and Immunity to Cold damage.
An effect that would absorb, redirect, convert, or turn the greatwyrm's Cold damage into healing can't do so. The damage is dealt normally instead.
Effects that reduce damage without depending on its damage type function normally.

trait.name: Perfect High Magic Recovery
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic.
This can restore an expended use of a 9th-level spell.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 30.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: The Last Winter (1/Long Rest)
entries: When the greatwyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains all of its Hit Points; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Cold Breath; regains all expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains all expended uses of Draconic High Magic; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.
For 1 hour, the greatwyrm enters The Last Winter. A supernatural freezing storm extends 300 feet from the greatwyrm and moves with it.
The area is Difficult Terrain for creatures of the greatwyrm's choice.
At the start of each creature's turn within the area, the greatwyrm can choose for that creature to take ({@damage 6d10}) Cold damage. Greatwyrm Cold Supremacy applies to this damage.
Nonmagical flames within the area are extinguished.
At the start of each of the greatwyrm's turns, its Cold Breath automatically recharges.
While The Last Winter is active, the greatwyrm can use its Mythic Actions.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.
Their element, temperament, instincts, and accumulated experience shape which spells come naturally to them.
At Greatwyrm age, hunting instinct and spellcraft have become inseparable.
The greatwyrm knows every spell in the White Dragon Spell List through 9th-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic has become so deeply rooted in the greatwyrm that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
The greatwyrm can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The greatwyrm can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the greatwyrm's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack.

Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell fog cloud|XPHB}, {@spell longstrider|XPHB}, {@spell Rime's binding ice|FTD}, {@spell pass without trace|XPHB}, {@spell sleet storm|XPHB}, {@spell slow|XPHB}, {@spell ice storm|XPHB}, {@spell freedom of movement|XPHB}, {@spell cone of cold|XPHB}, {@spell wall of ice|XPHB}, {@spell forcecage|XPHB}, {@spell teleport|XPHB}, {@spell control weather|XPHB}.

trait.name: Memory of the Endless Hunt
entries: White dragons may be less scholarly than their kin, but the hunt is a language they understand with terrifying clarity.
Tracks, scents, wounds, habits, and escape routes become parts of a living map in the dragon's mind.
Once an elder white dragon decides something is prey, distance becomes a temporary inconvenience.
{@b Wyrmling — Chosen Prey.}
The greatwyrm must spend 1 minute observing a creature, its scent, or its tracks to use this feature.
The effect lasts until replaced.
The dragon marks one creature as its Chosen Prey.
It has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks made to locate or track that creature.
While within 1 mile, if there is a physical trail or scent the dragon could reasonably detect, it knows the trail's general direction.
{@b Young — Relentless Pursuit.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
The dragon moves up to half its Speed toward its Chosen Prey.
This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from the Chosen Prey, and snow and ice don't cost the dragon extra movement during it.
{@b Adult — Learn the Prey's Pattern.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
This effect lasts until the end of the dragon's next turn.

After its Chosen Prey hits the dragon with an attack or causes the dragon to fail a Saving Throw, the dragon gains a bonus equal to its PB to AC or Saving Throws, as appropriate, against subsequent uses of that same attack or effect by that prey until the end of the dragon's next turn.
{@b Ancient — Frozen Quarry.}
This effect lasts while the creature remains the dragon's Chosen Prey.
A Chosen Prey within 120 feet gains no benefit from being Invisible against the dragon and can't Hide from the dragon using snow, fog, or ice alone.
Whenever the dragon deals Cold damage to that creature, its Speed becomes 0 until the start of the dragon's next turn.
{@b Wyrm — There Is No Escape.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
When the Chosen Prey within 1 mile teleports or magically moves away, the greatwyrm immediately knows its direction, distance, and whether it changed planes.
If the prey remains on the same plane, the greatwyrm can immediately move up to its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
{@b Greatwyrm — Nowhere Is Far Enough.}

While its Chosen Prey is on the same plane of existence, the greatwyrm always knows its direction and distance. This knowledge doesn't require sight, sound, scent, a physical trail, or line of effect.
The Chosen Prey can't become Hidden from the greatwyrm, and being Invisible grants it no benefit against the greatwyrm.
Whenever the Chosen Prey teleports, is magically transported, or leaves its current plane of existence, the greatwyrm immediately knows what occurred and the plane to which the prey traveled.

When the Chosen Prey teleports or is magically transported, the greatwyrm can use its Reaction to follow. The greatwyrm appears in an unoccupied space of its choice within 60 feet of the prey's destination, even if the destination is on another plane of existence.
Running farther merely tells the greatwyrm where to hunt next.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the greatwyrm more than size.
Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of a creature that has outlived lesser empires.
At the start of its turn, the greatwyrm can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the greatwyrm's choice within 500 feet that can see or hear it must make a DC 26 Wisdom Saving Throw.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the greatwyrm for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that greatwyrm's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.
A creature that fails its initial Saving Throw also can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

entries: {@atk rs} +18 to hit, range 600 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 20d12}) Cold damage.

mythicHeader: While The Last Winter is active, the greatwyrm can use the following Mythic Actions as additional Legendary Action options. They expend Legendary Actions from the greatwyrm's normal pool.

mythic.name: Whiteout (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm chooses a point it can see within 180 feet. A supernatural blizzard fills a 60-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point until the start of the greatwyrm's next turn.
The area is Heavily Obscured to creatures other than the greatwyrm.
A creature of the greatwyrm's choice that enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes ({@damage 6d8}) Cold damage. Greatwyrm Cold Supremacy applies to this damage.

mythic.name: Endless Pursuit (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm moves up to its Fly Speed toward its Chosen Prey without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
At the end of this movement, it can make one Bite attack against the Chosen Prey if the prey is within reach.

mythic.name: The Hunt Ends (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm uses Absolute Zero against its Chosen Prey.
If the attack hits, the prey must also succeed on a DC 29 Constitution Saving Throw or become encased in supernatural ice and be Restrained until the end of its next turn.
While Restrained this way, the prey's Speed is 0 and it can't teleport or be magically transported.

Civilizations, fortifications, bodies, and promises are simply structures waiting to fail.

{@b Wyrmling — Mireborn Predator.}
The dragon ignores Difficult Terrain created by mud, shallow water, swamp, or rotting vegetation.
It can Hide while only Lightly Obscured by swamp vegetation, murky water, fog, or ruins.
{@b Young — Cruel Ambush.}
The healing prevention lasts until the start of the dragon's next turn.
The dragon can take the Hide action as a Bonus Action while it has suitable concealment.
The first time it hits a creature while Hidden or Unseen, the hit deals an extra ({@damage 3d8}) Acid damage, and the target can't regain Hit Points until the start of the dragon's next turn.
{@b Adult — Ruin Feeds the Strong.}

It can immediately move up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

This effect lasts until the start of the dragon's next turn.
A creature damaged by the dragon's Acid can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, and can't benefit from regeneration until the start of the dragon's next turn.
Objects and structures take maximum damage from the dragon's Acid instead of rolled damage.
{@b Wyrm — Nothing Endures.}
The effect is permanent, but the creature penalties last until the start of the greatgreatwyrm's next turn.
The greatgreatwyrm's Acid ignores damage thresholds and Acid Resistance or Immunity of objects, structures, and magical barriers.

This AC reduction stacks with another AC-reducing effect only when that effect explicitly allows it.

Objects, structures, magical barriers, and magical constructs damaged by the greatwyrm's Acid take maximum damage from it.
