On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 10d6 + 11}) Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't fall Prone.
The greatwyrm can then fly up to half its Fly Speed.

legendary.name: Cataclysmic Movement (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm moves up to its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Each creature the greatwyrm passes within 25 feet of during this movement must succeed on a DC 29 Dexterity Saving Throw or fall Prone.

legendary.name: Cast Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm casts one spell of 8th level or lower that normally has a Casting Time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: Absolute Dissolution (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm uses Absolute Dissolution.

legendary.name: Breath Surge (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm rolls one additional d6 to recharge Acid Breath. If Acid Breath is already available, the greatwyrm can instead immediately use Acid Breath.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

mythicHeader: While The Final Ruin is active, the greatwyrm can use the following Mythic Actions as additional Legendary Action options. They expend Legendary Actions from the greatwyrm's normal pool.

mythic.name: Collapse Protection (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: One creature within 180 feet must make a DC 29 Dexterity Saving Throw.

On a failed save, it takes ({@damage 8d10}) Acid damage, and one magical effect currently increasing its AC or granting it Resistance is suppressed until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and no effect is suppressed.
Greatwyrm Acid Supremacy applies to this damage.

mythic.name: Ruin Walks (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm moves up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
During this movement, it can move through nonmagical objects and structures as if they were Difficult Terrain, destroying the portions through which it passes.

mythic.name: Nothing Remains (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm uses Absolute Dissolution.
On a hit, any spell or magical effect of 8th level or lower currently creating a barrier, armor, shield, or protective field on the target also ends.

monster.name: Green Greatwyrm

conditionImmune.note: from effects other than being reduced to 0 Hit Points

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (9/Day)
entries: If the greatwyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Magic Resistance
entries: The greatwyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.
Spell attack rolls against the greatwyrm are made with Disadvantage.

trait.name: Perfect Concentration
entries: The greatwyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the greatwyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The greatwyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 35 or lower, or returns to its true form.

While transformed, it retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; Saving Throw and Skill proficiencies; languages; personality and memories; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.
It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The greatwyrm can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The greatwyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell modify memory|XPHB}, {@spell mass suggestion|XPHB}, {@spell dominate monster|XPHB}, {@spell feeblemind|XPHB}, {@spell psychic scream|XGE}, {@spell shapechange|XPHB}, and {@spell wish|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the greatwyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Innate Elemental Casting
entries: When the greatwyrm casts a spell whose primary damage type is Poison, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Poison Supremacy
entries: The greatwyrm's Poison damage ignores Resistance and Immunity to Poison damage.
An effect that would absorb, redirect, convert, or turn the greatwyrm's Poison damage into healing can't do so. The damage is dealt normally instead.
Effects that reduce damage without depending on its damage type function normally.

trait.name: Perfect High Magic Recovery
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic.
This can restore an expended use of a 9th-level spell.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 30.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: The Emerald Masquerade (1/Long Rest)
entries: When the greatwyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains all of its Hit Points; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Poison Breath; regains all expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains all expended uses of Draconic High Magic; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.
For 1 hour, poisonous hallucinatory mist fills a 300-foot aura around the greatwyrm and moves with it.

At the start of each hostile creature's turn in the aura, the greatwyrm chooses Poison or Psychic. That creature takes ({@damage 6d10}) damage of the chosen type. Greatwyrm Poison Supremacy applies if the chosen damage is Poison.
The first Saving Throw each turn that a hostile creature in the aura makes against one of the greatwyrm's Enchantment or Illusion effects is made with Disadvantage.
At the start of each of the greatwyrm's turns, its Poison Breath automatically recharges.
While The Emerald Masquerade is active, the greatwyrm can use its Mythic Actions.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.
Their element, temperament, instincts, and accumulated experience shape which spells come naturally to them.
At Greatwyrm age, deception, influence, poison, and spellcraft have become inseparable instruments of control.
The greatwyrm knows every spell in the Green Dragon Spell List through 9th-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Age turns practiced magic into instinct.
The dragon can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack, if that dragon has Multiattack.

Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell disguise self|XPHB}, {@spell ray of sickness|XPHB}, {@spell detect thoughts|XPHB}, {@spell suggestion|XPHB}, {@spell hypnotic pattern|XPHB}, {@spell major image|XPHB}, {@spell charm monster|XGE}, {@spell greater invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell mass suggestion|XPHB}, {@spell project image|XPHB}.

trait.name: Web of the Verdant Lie
entries: Green dragons understand that controlling what someone believes is often more useful than controlling their body.
They collect promises, weaknesses, fears, alliances, and secrets with the same appetite other dragons reserve for gold.
At great age, simply dealing with one becomes dangerous long before initiative is rolled.
{@b Wyrmling — Borrowed Voice.}
Reproducing a learned voice or sound requires an Action.
The dragon remembers the learned voice or sound indefinitely.
After hearing a voice or sound for at least 1 minute, the dragon can reproduce it.
A creature suspicious of the imitation can make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check against the dragon's Spell Save DC.
This doesn't provide perfect supernatural identity copying.
{@b Young — Venomous Bargain.}
This effect lasts for 24 hours.
When a creature willingly makes an explicit promise to the dragon, the dragon can mystically mark that promise.

If the dragon later actually learns that the creature knowingly broke the promise during the duration, it can trigger the mark. The creature takes ({@damage 4d8}) Poison plus ({@damage 4d8}) Psychic damage, and the dragon knows its direction for 1 hour while both remain on the same plane.
This isn't perfect lie detection; the dragon must genuinely learn that the promise was broken.
{@b Adult — Web of Influence.}
After speaking with a creature for at least 1 minute, the dragon can make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check opposed by the creature's Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check.
On a success, the dragon learns one broad current reasonably exposed by the creature's behavior: a fear, desire, important loyalty, or immediate goal.
This doesn't reveal memories or perfectly hidden truths.
{@b Ancient — Forest of False Paths.}
In natural vegetation, forest, swamp, or jungle, the dragon leaves no trail unless it chooses, can't be tracked nonmagically, and can move through nonmagical plants without slowing.
A creature tracking the dragon can be deliberately led onto a false route unless it succeeds on a Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check against the dragon's Spell Save DC.
{@b Wyrm — Every Promise Has Teeth.}

Once per turn, when a creature affected by one of the greatgreatwyrm's Enchantment spells, Illusion spells, Charmed effects, or Venomous Bargains damages the greatwyrm or knowingly acts directly against an instruction it accepted, that creature takes ({@damage 8d10}) Poison or Psychic damage (the greatgreatwyrm's choice).
The creature also can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
{@b Greatwyrm — The Lie You Live By.}
Whenever a creature fails a Saving Throw against one of the greatwyrm's Enchantment spells, Illusion spells, Charmed effects, or Venomous Bargains, it becomes Webbound for 24 hours.
While both are on the same plane, the greatwyrm knows the direction and distance to a Webbound creature.
A Webbound creature has Disadvantage on Saving Throws against the greatwyrm's Enchantment and Illusion spells.

Once per turn, when a Webbound creature knowingly acts directly against an instruction, bargain, promise, or course of action it previously accepted from the greatwyrm, it takes ({@damage 10d10}) Poison or Psychic damage, chosen by the greatwyrm.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the greatwyrm more than size.
Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of a creature that has outlived lesser empires.
At the start of its turn, the greatwyrm can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the greatwyrm's choice within 500 feet that can see or hear it must make a DC 28 Wisdom Saving Throw.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the greatwyrm for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that greatwyrm's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.
A creature that fails its initial Saving Throw also can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

A creature that fails the save is also Poisoned until the end of its next turn.
Greatwyrm Poison Supremacy applies to this Poison damage.

Mirage, thunder, sand, and lightning blur together around their territories.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

mythicHeader: While The Living Tempest is active, the greatwyrm can use the following Mythic Actions as additional Legendary Action options. They expend Legendary Actions from the greatwyrm's normal pool.

mythic.name: Ride the Thunder (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm moves up to its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Each creature it passes within 20 feet of takes ({@damage 4d10}) Thunder damage.

mythic.name: Chain of the Crown (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm uses Heaven's Judgment.
Whether the attack hits or misses, it can then use the lightning-arc effect of There Is No Sky but Mine from that target as though it had dealt Lightning damage to the target.

mythic.name: Cast Down the Sky (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: Each hostile flying creature of the greatwyrm's choice within 300 feet must make a DC 29 Strength Saving Throw.
On a failed save, the creature is driven directly toward the ground by up to 300 feet, taking falling damage normally if it strikes a surface. Its Fly Speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn.

monster.name: Red Greatwyrm

conditionImmune.note: from effects other than being reduced to 0 Hit Points

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (9/Day)
entries: If the greatwyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Magic Resistance
entries: The greatwyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.
Spell attack rolls against the greatwyrm are made with Disadvantage.

trait.name: Perfect Concentration
entries: The greatwyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the greatwyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The greatwyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 37 or lower, or returns to its true form.

While transformed, it retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; Saving Throw and Skill proficiencies; languages; personality and memories; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.
It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The greatwyrm can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The greatwyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell disintegrate|XPHB}, {@spell delayed blast fireball|XPHB}, {@spell incendiary cloud|XPHB}, {@spell meteor swarm|XPHB}, {@spell power word kill|XPHB}, {@spell time stop|XPHB}, and {@spell wish|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the greatwyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Innate Elemental Casting
entries: When the greatwyrm casts a spell whose primary damage type is Fire, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Fire Supremacy
entries: The greatwyrm's Fire damage ignores Resistance and Immunity to Fire damage.
An effect that would absorb, redirect, convert, or turn the greatwyrm's Fire damage into healing can't do so. The damage is dealt normally instead.
Effects that reduce damage without depending on its damage type function normally.

trait.name: Perfect High Magic Recovery
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic.
This can restore an expended use of a 9th-level spell.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 30.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: The Burning Crown (1/Long Rest)
entries: When the greatwyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains all of its Hit Points; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Fire Breath; regains all expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains all expended uses of Draconic High Magic; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.
For 1 hour, an aura of sovereign flame extends 300 feet from the greatwyrm and moves with it.
At the start of each hostile creature's turn in the aura, that creature takes ({@damage 6d10}) Fire damage. Greatwyrm Fire Supremacy applies to this damage.
Whenever the greatwyrm rolls Fire damage, it treats any 1, 2, or 3 on a damage die as a 4.
At the start of each of the greatwyrm's turns, its Fire Breath automatically recharges.
While The Burning Crown is active, the greatwyrm can use its Mythic Actions.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.
Their element, temperament, instincts, and accumulated experience shape which spells come naturally to them.
At Greatwyrm age, flame, authority, conquest, and spellcraft have become a single expression of dominion.
The greatwyrm knows every spell in the Red Dragon Spell List through 9th-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Age turns practiced magic into instinct.
The dragon can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack, if that dragon has Multiattack.

Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell burning hands|XPHB}, {@spell scorching ray|XPHB}, {@spell see invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell fireball|XPHB}, {@spell dispel magic|XPHB}, {@spell wall of fire|XPHB}, {@spell immolation|XGE}, {@spell disintegrate|XPHB}, {@spell delayed blast fireball|XPHB}.

trait.name: Sovereignty of the Burning Hoard
entries: To a red dragon, possession is not a legal concept but a fact of nature.
What it claims becomes part of its identity, and resistance to its authority is treated as a personal insult.
With age, the distinction between its treasure, its territory, and the world it believes it deserves begins to disappear.
{@b Wyrmling — Claimed Treasure.}
The greatwyrm must touch the object for 1 minute to use this feature.
The claim lasts until the dragon willingly releases it.
The dragon can mystically mark up to PB × 10 objects as Claimed Treasure.
While a Claimed object is on the same plane and within 1 mile, the dragon knows its direction, approximate distance, and whether it is moving.
This doesn't reveal who carries the object or grant supernatural vision through it.
{@b Young — Tyrant's Challenge.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
The dragon chooses one creature within 60 feet. The target must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.

On a failed save, the target has Disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than the dragon, and the first time on each of its turns that it damages another creature, it takes ({@damage 2d8}) Fire damage.
The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
{@b Adult — Burning Dominion.}
The dragon emits a 60-foot aura. A hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura while Frightened of the dragon takes Fire damage equal to the dragon's PB + Charisma modifier.
Until the start of that creature's next turn, it can't become Invisible and treats movement that carries it farther from the dragon as Difficult Terrain.
{@b Ancient — Hoardfire Reprisal.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
When a creature within 120 feet damages the dragon or takes or removes something the dragon has Claimed, the dragon erupts flame around that creature.

The creature makes a Dexterity Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC, taking ({@damage 6d10}) Fire damage and being pushed 30 feet on a failure, or taking half as much damage with no push on a success.
{@b Wyrm — All Beneath the Crown.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The greatwyrm creates a 300-foot aura. At the start of each hostile creature's turn in the aura, that creature must make a Charisma Saving Throw against the greatgreatwyrm's Spell Save DC.

On a failed save, until the start of its next turn the creature can't teleport, can't become Invisible, can't willingly move farther from the greatwyrm, and can't carry a Claimed Treasure farther away from it.
{@b Greatwyrm — The World Is Mine.}
Whenever All Beneath the Crown is active, its radius becomes 500 feet.
Every unattended object and structure in the aura is considered Claimed Treasure for the purpose of the greatwyrm's features.
A hostile creature that fails the Saving Throw against All Beneath the Crown can't teleport, become Invisible, willingly move farther from the greatwyrm, or remove a Claimed object farther from it.

In addition, the first time each turn such a creature damages the greatwyrm or attempts to take, destroy, move, or magically alter something the greatwyrm has Claimed, it takes ({@damage 10d10}) Fire damage.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the greatwyrm more than size.
Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of a creature that has outlived lesser empires.
At the start of its turn, the greatwyrm can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the greatwyrm's choice within 500 feet that can see or hear it must make a DC 30 Wisdom Saving Throw.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the greatwyrm for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that greatwyrm's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.
A creature that fails its initial Saving Throw also can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

spellcasting.name: Innate Draconic Spellcasting
headerEntries: The greatwyrm's spellcasting ability is Charisma.
Its spell save DC is 30, and it has +22 to hit with spell attacks.
It requires no Spellcasting Focus. It can perform Somatic components using its draconic body.
It doesn't require Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The greatwyrm makes six attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail.
The greatwyrm can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a Casting Time of 1 Action.
The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} +22 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d10 + 11}) Piercing damage plus ({@damage 10d8}) Fire damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} +22 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d6 + 11}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} +22 to hit, reach 40 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d8 + 11}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} +22 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d6 + 11}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Fire Breath {@recharge 3}
entries: The greatwyrm exhales its breath weapon in a 180-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 30 Dexterity Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 40d6}) Fire damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
A creature that fails the save also burns until the end of its next turn, taking ({@damage 6d10}) Fire damage at the start of its turn.
Greatwyrm Fire Supremacy applies to this Fire damage.

action.name: Worldfire
entries: {@atk rs} +22 to hit, range 800 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 20d12}) Fire damage.

On a hit, each creature other than the target within 20 feet of it must make a DC 30 Dexterity Saving Throw, taking ({@damage 8d10}) Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
This attack is magical and counts as a spell attack, but isn't itself a spell.
Greatwyrm Fire Supremacy applies to this damage.

legendary.name: Detect
entries: The greatwyrm makes a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check.

legendary.name: Claw Attack
entries: The greatwyrm makes one Claw attack.

legendary.name: Tail Attack
entries: The greatwyrm makes one Tail attack.

legendary.name: Cast Cantrip
entries: The greatwyrm casts one cantrip.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 30 feet of the greatwyrm must make a DC 30 Dexterity Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 10d6 + 11}) Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't fall Prone.
The greatwyrm can then fly up to half its Fly Speed.

legendary.name: Cataclysmic Movement (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm moves up to its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Each creature the greatwyrm passes within 25 feet of during this movement must succeed on a DC 30 Dexterity Saving Throw or fall Prone.

legendary.name: Cast Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm casts one spell of 8th level or lower that normally has a Casting Time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: Worldfire (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm uses Worldfire.

entries: The greatwyrm rolls one additional d6 to recharge Fire Breath. If Fire Breath is already available, the greatwyrm can instead immediately use Fire Breath.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)

mythic.name: Imperial Reprisal (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm chooses one creature within 300 feet that damaged it since the end of its previous turn.
That creature takes ({@damage 8d10}) Fire damage. Greatwyrm Fire Supremacy applies to this damage.

mythic.name: Kneel (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: Each hostile creature of the greatwyrm's choice within 120 feet must make a DC 30 Charisma Saving Throw.
On a failed save, the creature falls Prone, its Speed becomes 0, and it can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn.

mythic.name: Burn the Rebellious (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm immediately uses Fire Breath.
Creatures currently affected by All Beneath the Crown make the Saving Throw against this use with Disadvantage.

trait.name: Young Mind, Ancient Blood
entries: The dragon is fully sapient but still a child. It can speak, reason, learn, negotiate, deceive, understand consequences, and make simple plans.
It lacks the experience, restraint, long-term judgment, and accumulated expertise of older dragons and isn't automatically a scholar, mastermind, or expert caster.

entries: The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Voice of the Open Horizon
entries: Brass dragons have always treated conversation as something more powerful than claws.
Their voices carry intent, emotion, warning, humor, and authority far beyond ordinary speech.
As they age, even violence can be interrupted by the simple fact that a Brass Dragon has chosen to speak.
{@b Wyrmling — Tongue Without Borders.}
Any creature within 60 feet that knows at least one language can understand the Brass Dragon's spoken words, regardless of what language the dragon actually uses.
The dragon similarly understands the general meaning of spoken language it hears, though this doesn't decipher codes, secret meanings, or magically concealed information.

trait.name: The World Plays Along
entries: Copper dragons rarely accept the world exactly as they find it.
Stone becomes a stage, distance becomes a joke, and certainty becomes something to be mocked.
With age, reality itself seems increasingly willing to participate in the dragon's tricks.

This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon chooses a 10-foot square of ground within 60 feet and magically alters its texture and shape.
It can make the area Difficult Terrain, harmlessly slippery, uneven enough to grant Half Cover to a Small creature, or visually appear slightly different.
The alteration isn't permanent.

entries: The dragon exhales its breath weapon in a 90-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line. Each creature in that area must make a DC 18 Dexterity Saving Throw.

action.name: Repulsion Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: The dragon exhales repulsive energy in a 30-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 18 Strength Saving Throw.
On a failed save, the creature is pushed 60 feet away from the dragon and knocked Prone.
If the creature strikes a solid obstacle before completing that movement, it takes ({@damage 3d6}) Bludgeoning damage.

trait.name: Growing Draconic Mind
entries: The dragon is no longer merely a gifted child.
Experience has begun turning instinct into judgment, curiosity into expertise, and power into deliberate technique.
It can now pursue plans that last months or years rather than moments.

A Young Metallic Dragon can plan ahead, study magic, make agreements, manage territory, and understand social structures far better than a wyrmling, though it still lacks the accumulated experience of an Adult Dragon.

trait.name: Draconic Magical Instinct
entries: The dragon is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena.
Its growing experience makes it more reliable than a wyrmling, but this trait doesn't grant automatic or complete knowledge.

trait.name: Keen Senses
entries: The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The dragon can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the dragon ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The dragon magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 12 or lower, or returns to its true form.
The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

While transformed, the dragon retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Draconic Magical Instinct; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The dragon can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the dragon chooses when it transforms.

trait.name: Innate Elemental Casting
entries: When the dragon casts a spell whose primary damage type is Cold, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 4.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The dragon can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell revivify|XPHB}, {@spell greater restoration|XPHB}, {@spell wall of ice|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the dragon from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.
Their element, temperament, instincts, and accumulated experience shape which spells come naturally to them.
As a dragon grows older, more of that inherited magic becomes effortless.
The dragon knows every spell in the Silver Dragon Spell List through 6-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Age turns practiced magic into instinct.
The dragon can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack.
Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell fog cloud|XPHB}, {@spell lesser restoration|XPHB}, {@spell misty step|XPHB}.

trait.name: Sanctuary of the Gentle Sky
entries: Silver dragons carry the safety of high mountains and quiet snowfall with them.
Their presence turns survival into recovery and fear into calm.
The oldest among them can make death itself wait outside the boundaries of their protection.
{@b Wyrmling — Warmth Beneath the Snow.}
Creatures chosen by the dragon within 30 feet are protected from natural extreme cold, have Advantage on Death Saving Throws, and automatically stabilize after succeeding on one Death Saving Throw.
{@b Young — Shelter in the Storm.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
The Temporary Hit Points last until depleted or replaced; condition removal is instantaneous.
The dragon chooses a creature within 60 feet. That creature gains Temporary Hit Points equal to twice the dragon's PB + its Charisma modifier.
The creature can immediately end either the Frightened or Charmed condition on itself.

trait.name: Argent Aegis
entries: Silver dragons are born with an instinctive resistance to hostile magic that goes beyond ordinary draconic durability.
Their scales carry a quiet force that catches, diffuses, and turns aside supernatural pressure before it reaches the body beneath.
As a silver dragon matures, that instinct develops into one of the strongest natural magical defenses among true dragons.
{@b Wyrmling — Argent Ward.}
The dragon has Advantage on Saving Throws against cantrips and spells of 1st level.
{@b Young — Spellward Scales.}
The dragon has Advantage on Saving Throws against all spells and other magical effects.
Spellward Scales supersedes Argent Ward while the dragon is at the Young age category or older.

trait.name: Crown of the First Dawn
entries: Gold dragons carry something older than rulership and brighter than ordinary flame.
Their presence makes courage easier, deception harder, and cruelty far more dangerous.
As a Gold Dragon matures, its authority ceases to feel political and begins to feel cosmic.
{@b Wyrmling — Dawnfire.}

trait.name: Voice of the Open Horizon
entries: Brass dragons have always treated conversation as something more powerful than claws.
Their voices carry intent, emotion, warning, humor, and authority far beyond ordinary speech.
As they age, even violence can be interrupted by the simple fact that a Brass Dragon has chosen to speak.
{@b Wyrmling — Tongue Without Borders.}
Any creature within 60 feet that knows at least one language can understand the Brass Dragon's spoken words, regardless of what language the dragon actually uses.
The dragon similarly understands the general meaning of spoken language it hears, though this doesn't decipher codes, secret meanings, or magically concealed information.
{@b Young — Words Before Violence.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction.
This effect lasts until the start of the triggering creature's next turn.
When a creature within 60 feet that can hear the dragon makes an Attack Roll, the dragon can speak a warning, argument, insult, plea, or distraction.

The creature makes a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC. On a failure, it has Disadvantage on that attack, can't make Opportunity Attacks, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.
{@b Adult — Command the Conversation.}
The dragon can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Creatures of the dragon's choice within 120 feet that can hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.
On a failure, a creature can't willingly attack the dragon or a creature designated by the dragon until the end of its next turn. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size.

Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage.
At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the dragon's choice within 120 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.

trait.name: The World Plays Along
entries: Copper dragons rarely accept the world exactly as they find it.
Stone becomes a stage, distance becomes a joke, and certainty becomes something to be mocked.
With age, reality itself seems increasingly willing to participate in the dragon's tricks.
{@b Wyrmling — Mischievous Ground.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon chooses a 10-foot square of ground within 60 feet and magically alters its texture and shape.
It can make the area Difficult Terrain, harmlessly slippery, uneven enough to grant Half Cover to a Small creature, or visually appear slightly different.
The alteration isn't permanent.
{@b Young — Wrong Step.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction.
When a creature within 60 feet moves at least 10 feet, the dragon can distort the ground beneath it.

The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon chooses a 60-foot-radius area within 120 feet and can continuously reshape nonmagical earth and stone there into slopes, shallow pits, waist-high walls, ramps, steps, pillars, or trenches.
No single alteration can directly crush a creature or instantly destroy a building.
The dragon can rearrange the affected terrain again as a Bonus Action.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size.
Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of an apex creature that has survived centuries.
Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage.
At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the dragon's choice within 120 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.

entries: The dragon makes three attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail.

entries: {@atk mw} +11 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 4d10 + 6}) Piercing damage plus ({@damage 4d8}) Acid damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 4d6 + 6}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} +11 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 4d8 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} +11 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 4d6 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The dragon can use this feature as an Action.

The dragon magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 18 or lower, or returns to its true form.
The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

While transformed, the dragon retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Draconic Magical Instinct; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The dragon can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the dragon chooses when it transforms.

entries: When the dragon casts a spell whose primary damage type is Lightning, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 6.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The dragon can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell chain lightning|XPHB}, {@spell control weather|XPHB}, {@spell storm of vengeance|XPHB}.

entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.

As a dragon grows older, more of that inherited magic becomes effortless.
The dragon knows every spell in the Bronze Dragon Spell List through 9-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic

entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.

trait.name: Voice of the Open Horizon
entries: Brass dragons have always treated conversation as something more powerful than claws.
Their voices carry intent, emotion, warning, humor, and authority far beyond ordinary speech.

{@b Young — Words Before Violence.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction.
This effect lasts until the start of the triggering creature's next turn.

{@b Adult — Command the Conversation.}
The dragon can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The dragon can use this feature as an Action.

The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

trait.name: Innate Elemental Casting
entries: When the dragon casts a spell whose primary damage type is Cold, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

entries: The dragon's Cold damage ignores Cold Resistance.

entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 14.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The dragon can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell globe of invulnerability|XPHB}, {@spell Fizban's platinum shield|FTD}, {@spell forcecage|XPHB}, {@spell mass heal|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the dragon from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.
Their element, temperament, instincts, and accumulated experience shape which spells come naturally to them.
As a dragon grows older, more of that inherited magic becomes effortless.
The dragon knows the Silver Dragon spells presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait through 9th-level magic.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.

Age turns practiced magic into instinct.

Creatures chosen by the dragon within 30 feet are protected from natural extreme cold, have Advantage on Death Saving Throws, and automatically stabilize after succeeding on one Death Saving Throw.
{@b Young — Shelter in the Storm.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
The Temporary Hit Points last until depleted or replaced; condition removal is instantaneous.
The dragon chooses a creature within 60 feet. That creature gains Temporary Hit Points equal to twice the dragon's PB + its Charisma modifier.
The creature can immediately end either the Frightened or Charmed condition on itself.

The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction.

The dragon can then move that creature up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space the dragon can see.

entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the wyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 24.

trait.name: Voice of the Open Horizon
entries: Brass dragons have always treated conversation as something more powerful than claws.

As they age, even violence can be interrupted by the simple fact that a Brass Dragon has chosen to speak.
{@b Wyrmling — Tongue Without Borders.}
Any creature within 60 feet that knows at least one language can understand the Brass Dragon's spoken words, regardless of what language the dragon actually uses.

{@b Young — Words Before Violence.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
This effect lasts until the start of the triggering creature's next turn.
When a creature within 60 feet that can hear the dragon makes an Attack Roll, the dragon can speak a warning, argument, insult, plea, or distraction.

The creature makes a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC. On a failure, it has Disadvantage on that attack, can't make Opportunity Attacks, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.
{@b Adult — Command the Conversation.}
The wyrm can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Creatures of the dragon's choice within 120 feet that can hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.
On a failure, a creature can't willingly attack the dragon or a creature designated by the dragon until the end of its next turn. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns.

The dragon can deliberately project its voice to any location within 10 miles that it knows.

This effect lasts for 1 minute.

entries: Age has given the dragon more than size.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (7/Day)
entries: If the wyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Wyrm Magic Resistance
entries: The wyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Perfect Concentration
entries: The wyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.

trait.name: Draconic Magical Instinct
entries: The wyrm is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena.

trait.name: Keen Senses
entries: The wyrm has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the wyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The wyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 30 or lower, or returns to its true form.

While transformed, it retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; Saving Throw and Skill proficiencies; languages; personality and memories; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.
It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The wyrm can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The wyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell globe of invulnerability|XPHB}, {@spell Fizban's platinum shield|FTD}, {@spell forcecage|XPHB}, {@spell antimagic field|XPHB}, {@spell mass heal|XPHB}, {@spell true resurrection|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the wyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Innate Elemental Casting
entries: When the wyrm casts a spell whose primary damage type is Cold, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

trait.name: Wyrm Cold Supremacy
entries: The wyrm's Cold damage ignores Cold Resistance.
When the wyrm deals Cold damage to a creature with Cold Immunity, that Immunity is treated as Cold Resistance, and the wyrm then ignores that Resistance.
As a result, the wyrm's Cold damage affects creatures with Cold Resistance or Cold Immunity without reducing the damage.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the wyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 27.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: World-Heart Reignition (1/Long Rest)
entries: When the wyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges both of its Breath Weapons; regains 3 expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic, including a 9th-level spell; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.
Their element, temperament, instincts, and accumulated experience shape which spells come naturally to them.
As a dragon grows older, more of that inherited magic becomes effortless.
The wyrm knows every spell presented in its Silver Dragon spell list through 9th-level magic, as shown in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Age turns practiced magic into instinct.
The wyrm can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The wyrm can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the wyrm's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack.

Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell fog cloud|XPHB}, {@spell lesser restoration|XPHB}, {@spell misty step|XPHB}, {@spell revivify|XPHB}, {@spell freedom of movement|XPHB}, {@spell wall of force|XPHB}, {@spell globe of invulnerability|XPHB}, {@spell forcecage|XPHB}, {@spell holy aura|XPHB}.

trait.name: Argent Aegis
entries: Silver dragons are born with an instinctive resistance to hostile magic that goes beyond ordinary draconic durability.
Their scales carry a quiet force that catches, diffuses, and turns aside supernatural pressure before it reaches the body beneath.
As a silver dragon matures, that instinct develops into one of the strongest natural magical defenses among true dragons.
{@b Wyrmling — Argent Ward.}
The dragon has Advantage on Saving Throws against cantrips and spells of 1st level.
{@b Young — Spellward Scales.}
The dragon has Advantage on Saving Throws against all spells and other magical effects.
Spellward Scales supersedes Argent Ward while the dragon is at the Young age category or older.
{@b Ancient — Unbroken Silver Aegis.}
Magic bends around the elder silver dragon rather than finding easy purchase.
Force that should imprison it fractures against its scales.
Attempts to banish, bind, or displace it meet a will reinforced by living arcane armor.
The dragon retains Magic Resistance and is Immune to Force damage.
It has Advantage on checks and Saving Throws made to resist forced teleportation, banishment, magical restraint, magical imprisonment, and forced planar movement.
When a magical effect would teleport or banish the dragon against its will, the dragon can use its Reaction to cause that effect to fail against it.
{@b Wyrm — Absolute Argent Aegis.}
Magic no longer merely struggles against the silver wyrm—it breaks upon it.
The invisible architecture of Force bends around its scales like wind around a mountain.
Those sheltered beneath its wings share in a defense that even archmages find difficult to penetrate.
The wyrm is Immune to Force damage, retains Magic Resistance, and has Resistance to all damage dealt by spells.
The wyrm can't be teleported, banished, or moved to another plane against its will.

Chosen creatures within 120 feet have Magic Resistance, Resistance to Force damage, and Advantage on checks and Saving Throws made to resist banishment, forced teleportation, magical restraint, magical imprisonment, and forced planar movement.
{@b Argent Refraction.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.

When a spell or magical effect the wyrm can see within 120 feet targets the wyrm or a creature protected by Absolute Argent Aegis, the wyrm can grant that target a +5 bonus to AC against the triggering effect or a +5 bonus to the triggering Saving Throw.

If that bonus causes the attack to miss or the Saving Throw to succeed, the wyrm can move the protected creature up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. This Force movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

trait.name: Sanctuary of the Gentle Sky
entries: Silver dragons carry the safety of high mountains and quiet snowfall with them.
Their presence turns survival into recovery and fear into calm.
The oldest among them can make death itself wait outside the boundaries of their protection.
{@b Wyrmling — Warmth Beneath the Snow.}
Creatures chosen by the dragon within 30 feet are protected from natural extreme cold, have Advantage on Death Saving Throws, and automatically stabilize after succeeding on one Death Saving Throw.
{@b Young — Shelter in the Storm.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
The Temporary Hit Points last until depleted or replaced; condition removal is instantaneous.
The dragon chooses a creature within 60 feet. That creature gains Temporary Hit Points equal to twice the dragon's PB + its Charisma modifier.
The creature can immediately end either the Frightened or Charmed condition on itself.
{@b Adult — Merciful Intercession.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
When a creature within 120 feet would drop to 0 Hit Points, the dragon can cause it to drop to 1 Hit Point instead.
The dragon can then move that creature up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space the dragon can see.
The dragon can use this Reaction a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.
{@b Ancient — Sanctuary Cannot Be Broken.}
The wyrm can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.

The dragon creates a 120-foot aura. Chosen creatures in the aura have Advantage on Death Saving Throws, can't have their Hit Point maximum reduced, can't be prevented from regaining Hit Points, and can't be instantly killed while above 0 Hit Points.
{@b Wyrm — Death Waits Outside.}
While Sanctuary Cannot Be Broken is active, the first time each chosen creature would die during that duration, it doesn't die.
Instead, it returns to half its Hit Point maximum; ends Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, and Stunned on itself; and can immediately stand without spending movement.
Each creature can benefit from this effect only once per use of Sanctuary Cannot Be Broken.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size.
Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of an apex creature that has survived centuries.
Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage.
At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the dragon's choice within 300 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.

Each creature the wyrm passes within 20 feet of during this movement must succeed on a DC 28 Dexterity Saving Throw or fall Prone.

legendary.name: Cast Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The wyrm casts one spell of 7th level or lower that normally has a casting time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: Breath Surge (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The wyrm chooses one of its Breath Weapons and rolls one additional d6 to recharge that Breath Weapon. If the chosen Breath Weapon is already available, the wyrm can instead immediately use that Breath Weapon.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The wyrm casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

monster.name: Brass Greatwyrm

conditionImmune.note: from effects other than being reduced to 0 Hit Points

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (9/Day)
entries: If the greatwyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Magic Resistance
entries: The greatwyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.
Spell attack rolls against the greatwyrm are made with Disadvantage.

trait.name: Perfect Concentration
entries: The greatwyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.

trait.name: Draconic Magical Instinct
entries: The greatwyrm is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena.
This trait doesn't grant automatic or complete knowledge.

trait.name: Keen Senses
entries: The greatwyrm has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the greatwyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The greatwyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 34 or lower, or returns to its true form.

While transformed, it retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; Saving Throw and Skill proficiencies; languages; personality and memories; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.
It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The greatwyrm can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The greatwyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell dream|XPHB}, {@spell mass suggestion|XPHB}, {@spell teleport|XPHB}, {@spell mirage arcane|XPHB}, {@spell project image|XPHB}, {@spell power word stun|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}, {@spell foresight|XPHB}, and {@spell power word heal|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the greatwyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Innate Elemental Casting
entries: When the greatwyrm casts a spell whose primary damage type is Fire, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Fire Supremacy
entries: The greatwyrm's Fire damage ignores Resistance and Immunity to Fire damage.
An effect that would absorb, redirect, convert, or turn the greatwyrm's Fire damage into healing can't do so. The damage is dealt normally instead.
Effects that reduce damage without depending on its damage type function normally.

trait.name: Perfect High Magic Recovery
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic.
This can restore an expended use of a 9th-level spell.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 30.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: The Final Parley (1/Long Rest)
entries: When the greatwyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains all of its Hit Points; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges both of its Breath Weapons; regains all expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains all expended uses of Draconic High Magic; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.
For 1 hour, the greatwyrm radiates an aura of absolute discourse extending 1,000 feet from it and moving with it.
Hostile creatures in the aura can't take Reactions.
The World Must Hear is active throughout this duration without requiring an Action.
At the start of each of the greatwyrm's turns, both of its Breath Weapons automatically recharge.
While The Final Parley is active, the greatwyrm can use its Mythic Actions.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.
Their element, temperament, instincts, and accumulated experience shape which spells come naturally to them.
As a dragon grows older, more of that inherited magic becomes effortless.
The greatwyrm knows every spell presented in its Brass Dragon spell list through 9th-level magic, as shown in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Age turns practiced magic into instinct.
The greatwyrm can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The greatwyrm can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the greatwyrm's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack.

Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell speak with animals|XPHB}, {@spell calm emotions|XPHB}, {@spell suggestion|XPHB}, {@spell sending|XPHB}, {@spell tongues|XPHB}, {@spell charm monster|XGE}, {@spell mass suggestion|XPHB}, {@spell project image|XPHB}, {@spell teleport|XPHB}.

trait.name: Voice of the Open Horizon
entries: Brass dragons have always treated conversation as something more powerful than claws.
Their voices carry intent, emotion, warning, humor, and authority far beyond ordinary speech.
As they age, even violence can be interrupted by the simple fact that a Brass Dragon has chosen to speak.
{@b Wyrmling — Tongue Without Borders.}
Any creature within 60 feet that knows at least one language can understand the Brass Dragon's spoken words, regardless of what language the dragon actually uses.
The dragon similarly understands the general meaning of spoken language it hears, though this doesn't decipher codes, secret meanings, or magically concealed information.
{@b Young — Words Before Violence.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
This effect lasts until the start of the triggering creature's next turn.
When a creature within 60 feet that can hear the dragon makes an Attack Roll, the dragon can speak a warning, argument, insult, plea, or distraction.

The creature makes a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC. On a failure, it has Disadvantage on that attack, can't make Opportunity Attacks, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.
{@b Adult — Command the Conversation.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Creatures of the dragon's choice within 120 feet that can hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.
On a failure, a creature can't willingly attack the dragon or a creature designated by the dragon until the end of its next turn. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns.
Taking damage from a protected creature immediately allows another save. This effect isn't Charmed and functions against creatures immune to Charmed.
{@b Ancient — Voice Across Kingdoms.}
The dragon can deliberately project its voice to any location within 10 miles that it knows.

Its speech arrives clearly at the chosen location regardless of intervening terrain. The dragon can choose to speak simultaneously through any number of points within that radius and can choose which creatures at those points hear it.
This isn't telepathy and doesn't allow a recipient to answer the dragon automatically.
{@b Wyrm — The World Must Hear.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The greatwyrm creates a 500-foot aura of enforced parley.

Before a hostile creature in the aura that can hear the greatwyrm can make an attack, cast a damaging spell, or use an effect that forces another creature to make a Saving Throw in order to deal damage, it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the greatwyrm's Spell Save DC.
On a failed save, the attempted hostile act expends neither the creature's Action, spell slot, nor limited use, but the creature can't attempt that hostile act again until the start of its next turn.
This effect isn't Charmed and functions against creatures immune to Charmed.
{@b Greatwyrm — The Last Word.}
When the greatwyrm uses The World Must Hear, the aura's radius becomes 1,000 feet.
Every creature in the aura that knows at least one language can understand the greatwyrm while it speaks, regardless of the language used.
A hostile creature must make the Saving Throw required by The World Must Hear before each hostile act covered by that feature.

When a hostile creature succeeds on that Saving Throw, the greatwyrm can force it to reroll the Saving Throw and use the lower result. The greatwyrm can do so once on each creature's turn without using a Reaction.
A creature that fails can't attempt another hostile act covered by The World Must Hear until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the greatwyrm more than size.
Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of a creature that has outlived lesser empires.
At the start of its turn, the greatwyrm can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the greatwyrm's choice within 500 feet that can see or hear it must make a DC 28 Wisdom Saving Throw.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the greatwyrm for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that greatwyrm's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.
A creature that fails its initial Saving Throw also can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

It doesn't require Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The greatwyrm makes six attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail.
The greatwyrm can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a Casting Time of 1 Action.
The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

entries: {@atk mw} +21 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d10 + 11}) Piercing damage plus ({@damage 10d8}) Fire damage.

entries: {@atk mw} +21 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d6 + 11}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} +21 to hit, reach 40 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d8 + 11}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} +21 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d6 + 11}) Bludgeoning damage.

entries: The greatwyrm exhales its breath weapon in a 180-foot-long, 30-foot-wide Line. Each creature in that area must make a DC 29 Dexterity Saving Throw.

Greatwyrm Fire Supremacy applies to this damage.

entries: This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.

On a failed save, a creature is Unconscious for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
The effect also ends on a creature if it takes damage or if another creature uses an Action to wake it.

This effect isn't Charmed.

trait.name: The World Plays Along
entries: Copper dragons rarely accept the world exactly as they find it.
Stone becomes a stage, distance becomes a joke, and certainty becomes something to be mocked.
With age, reality itself seems increasingly willing to participate in the dragon's tricks.
{@b Wyrmling — Mischievous Ground.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon chooses a 10-foot square of ground within 60 feet and magically alters its texture and shape.
It can make the area Difficult Terrain, harmlessly slippery, uneven enough to grant Half Cover to a Small creature, or visually appear slightly different.
The alteration isn't permanent.
{@b Young — Wrong Step.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
When a creature within 60 feet moves at least 10 feet, the dragon can distort the ground beneath it.
The creature must make a Dexterity Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC. On a failure, the dragon moves it up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space on the same surface, and it falls Prone.
{@b Adult — Laughing Terrain.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon chooses a 60-foot-radius area within 120 feet and can continuously reshape nonmagical earth and stone there into slopes, shallow pits, waist-high walls, ramps, steps, pillars, or trenches.
No single alteration can directly crush a creature or instantly destroy a building.
The dragon can rearrange the affected terrain again as a Bonus Action.
{@b Ancient — Impossible Shortcut.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
The dragon enters a solid earth or stone surface and emerges from another connected earth or stone surface within 300 feet.
Creatures and objects it is carrying travel with it. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks and doesn't require line of sight, provided the two surfaces are connected by earth or stone.
{@b Wyrm — Reality Gets the Joke.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
When a creature the greatwyrm can see within 300 feet teleports, is pushed or pulled, moves through magical movement, or creates an Area of Effect, the greatwyrm can alter the final positioning.
It can shift a creature's destination by up to 60 feet or shift the origin point of the Area of Effect by up to 60 feet.
The new position must still be legally possible for the original effect. This feature doesn't cancel the original effect.
{@b Greatwyrm — The Rules Are Suggestions.}
Reality Gets the Joke can affect a creature or effect the greatwyrm can see within 500 feet.
The greatwyrm can shift a creature's destination by up to 120 feet, or shift the origin point of an Area of Effect by up to 120 feet.
If the effect creates a Line or Cone, the greatwyrm can also change its direction from the new origin.
If an effect targets a creature rather than creating an Area of Effect, the greatwyrm can instead replace one target with another legal target within 60 feet of the original target.
The replacement must be a creature or object that the original effect could legally affect.
The original effect isn't canceled; reality simply resolves it from the greatwyrm's revised positioning.
