Until the start of the greatwyrm's next turn, the first Attack Roll or single-target spell that would target that creature can instead target another legal creature within 60 feet of it, chosen by the greatwyrm.

mythic.name: The Punchline (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm chooses a point within 300 feet. Space, gravity, and stone violently disagree in a 60-foot-radius Sphere around that point.

Creatures of the greatwyrm's choice in the area must make a DC 29 Dexterity Saving Throw, taking ({@damage 10d10}) Bludgeoning damage plus ({@damage 10d10}) Acid damage and falling Prone on a failed save, or taking half as much damage without falling Prone on a successful one.
The greatwyrm can then move every creature that failed the save up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space in the area.
Greatwyrm Acid Supremacy applies to the Acid damage.

monster.name: Bronze Greatwyrm

conditionImmune.note: from effects other than being reduced to 0 Hit Points

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (9/Day)
entries: If the greatwyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Magic Resistance
entries: The greatwyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.
Spell attack rolls against the greatwyrm are made with Disadvantage.

trait.name: Perfect Concentration
entries: The greatwyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.

trait.name: Draconic Magical Instinct
entries: The greatwyrm is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena.
This trait doesn't grant automatic or complete knowledge.

trait.name: Keen Senses
entries: The greatwyrm has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the greatwyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The greatwyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 37 or lower, or returns to its true form.

While transformed, it retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; Saving Throw and Skill proficiencies; languages; personality and memories; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.
It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The greatwyrm can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The greatwyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell chain lightning|XPHB}, {@spell control weather|XPHB}, {@spell reverse gravity|XPHB}, {@spell Fizban's platinum shield|FTD}, {@spell storm of vengeance|XPHB}, {@spell time stop|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}, {@spell holy aura|XPHB}, and {@spell mass heal|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the greatwyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Innate Elemental Casting
entries: When the greatwyrm casts a spell whose primary damage type is Lightning, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Lightning Supremacy
entries: The greatwyrm's Lightning damage ignores Resistance and Immunity to Lightning damage.
An effect that would absorb, redirect, convert, or turn the greatwyrm's Lightning damage into healing can't do so. The damage is dealt normally instead.
Effects that reduce damage without depending on its damage type function normally.

trait.name: Perfect High Magic Recovery
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic.
This can restore an expended use of a 9th-level spell.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 30.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: The Unbroken Storm (1/Long Rest)
entries: When the greatwyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains all of its Hit Points; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges both of its Breath Weapons; regains all expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains all expended uses of Draconic High Magic; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.
For 1 hour, a protective storm extends 300 feet from the greatwyrm and moves with it.
At the start of each chosen creature's turn in the storm, that creature gains 30 Temporary Hit Points.
Chosen creatures in the storm have Advantage on Death Saving Throws and on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.

Once per turn when a hostile creature damages one of those chosen creatures, lightning strikes the attacker for ({@damage 4d10}) Lightning damage. Greatwyrm Lightning Supremacy applies to this damage.
At the start of each of the greatwyrm's turns, both of its Breath Weapons automatically recharge.
While The Unbroken Storm is active, the greatwyrm can use its Mythic Actions.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.
Their element, temperament, instincts, and accumulated experience shape which spells come naturally to them.
As a dragon grows older, more of that inherited magic becomes effortless.
The greatwyrm knows every spell presented in its Bronze Dragon spell list through 9th-level magic, as shown in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Age turns practiced magic into instinct.
The greatwyrm can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The greatwyrm can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the greatwyrm's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack.

Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell protection from evil and good|XPHB}, {@spell see invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell shatter|XPHB}, {@spell lightning bolt|XPHB}, {@spell protection from energy|XPHB}, {@spell control winds|XGE}, {@spell chain lightning|XPHB}, {@spell reverse gravity|XPHB}, {@spell control weather|XPHB}.

trait.name: Stormwarden's Instinct
entries: Bronze dragons possess an almost compulsive awareness of danger around them.
Thunder answers not merely anger, but the decision to stand between harm and another creature.
An elder Bronze Dragon doesn't simply endure a battlefield—it controls who is allowed to be hurt within it.
{@b Wyrmling — Protective Instinct.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
When a creature within 30 feet is hit by an attack, the dragon can impose a penalty equal to its PB on the triggering attack roll, potentially causing it to miss.
{@b Young — Storm Interception.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
When a creature within 60 feet is targeted by an attack, the dragon can move up to half its Speed toward that creature without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
If physically possible, the dragon places itself between the attacker and target and becomes the target of the attack instead.
If the attack hits the dragon, the attacker takes Lightning damage equal to PB × 1d8.
{@b Adult — Guardian of the Storm.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
When a creature within 120 feet fails a Saving Throw against a spell or magical effect, the dragon can allow it to reroll the Saving Throw.
If the reroll succeeds, lightning strikes the source of the effect, dealing ({@damage 4d10}) Lightning damage to it.
{@b Ancient — Storm Answers Harm.}
This effect lasts until the end of the dragon's next turn.
Whenever a creature within 120 feet damages one of the dragon's chosen allies, that attacker becomes Storm-Marked until the end of the dragon's next turn.

The first time the dragon damages that creature while it is Storm-Marked, it takes an additional ({@damage 6d10}) Lightning damage, can't take Reactions, and has its Speed halved until the end of the dragon's next turn.
{@b Wyrm — No One Falls While I Stand.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
When a creature the greatwyrm can see within 300 feet would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, the greatwyrm can move up to its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
If it ends this movement within 30 feet of that creature, the creature drops to 1 Hit Point instead and gains 58 Temporary Hit Points.
The source that dealt the triggering damage is then struck by lightning and takes ({@damage 10d10}) Lightning damage.
This feature doesn't require the greatwyrm to cast a spell.
{@b Greatwyrm — I Decide Who Falls.}
Once per round, when a chosen creature the greatwyrm can see within 500 feet would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, that creature drops to 1 Hit Point instead and gains 80 Temporary Hit Points.
This effect requires no Action or Reaction.
The source that dealt the triggering damage is immediately struck by lightning and takes ({@damage 12d10}) Lightning damage. Greatwyrm Lightning Supremacy applies to this damage.
The greatwyrm can still use No One Falls While I Stand normally against a different triggering event.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the greatwyrm more than size.
Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of a creature that has outlived lesser empires.
At the start of its turn, the greatwyrm can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the greatwyrm's choice within 500 feet that can see or hear it must make a DC 30 Wisdom Saving Throw.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the greatwyrm for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that greatwyrm's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.
A creature that fails its initial Saving Throw also can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

spellcasting.name: Innate Draconic Spellcasting
headerEntries: The greatwyrm's spellcasting ability is Charisma.
Its spell save DC is 30, and it has +22 to hit with spell attacks.
It requires no Spellcasting Focus. It can perform Somatic components using its draconic body.
It doesn't require Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The greatwyrm makes six attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail.
The greatwyrm can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a Casting Time of 1 Action.
The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} +23 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d10 + 12}) Piercing damage plus ({@damage 10d8}) Lightning damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} +23 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d6 + 12}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} +23 to hit, reach 40 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d8 + 12}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} +23 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d6 + 12}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Lightning Breath {@recharge 3}
entries: The greatwyrm exhales its breath weapon in a 300-foot-long, 30-foot-wide Line. Each creature in that area must make a DC 31 Dexterity Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 40d10}) Lightning damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
Greatwyrm Lightning Supremacy applies to this damage.

action.name: Repulsion Breath {@recharge 3}
entries: The greatwyrm exhales repulsive energy in a 180-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 31 Strength Saving Throw.
On a failed save, the creature is pushed up to 300 feet directly away from the greatwyrm and knocked Prone.
If the creature strikes a solid obstacle before completing that movement, it takes ({@damage 10d6}) Bludgeoning damage.

legendaryHeader: The greatwyrm can take 9 Legendary Actions, choosing from the options below. Only one Legendary Action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The greatwyrm regains spent Legendary Actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Detect
entries: The greatwyrm makes a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check.

legendary.name: Claw Attack
entries: The greatwyrm makes one Claw attack.

legendary.name: Tail Attack
entries: The greatwyrm makes one Tail attack.

legendary.name: Cast Cantrip
entries: The greatwyrm casts one cantrip.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 30 feet of the greatwyrm must make a DC 31 Dexterity Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 10d6 + 12}) Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't fall Prone.
The greatwyrm can then fly up to half its Fly Speed.

legendary.name: Cataclysmic Movement (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm moves up to its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Each creature the greatwyrm passes within 25 feet of during this movement must succeed on a DC 31 Dexterity Saving Throw or fall Prone.

legendary.name: Cast Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm casts one spell of 8th level or lower that normally has a Casting Time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: Breath Surge (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm chooses one of its Breath Weapons and rolls one additional d6 to recharge that Breath Weapon. If the chosen Breath Weapon is already available, the greatwyrm can instead immediately use that Breath Weapon.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

mythicHeader: While The Unbroken Storm is active, the greatwyrm can use the following Mythic Actions as additional Legendary Action options. They expend Legendary Actions from the greatwyrm's normal pool.

mythic.name: Intercept the Blow (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm moves up to its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
It can end this movement adjacent to a chosen creature. That creature gains Half Cover until the start of the greatwyrm's next turn.

mythic.name: Stormwarden's Verdict (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: One creature within 500 feet that damaged a chosen ally since the end of the greatwyrm's previous turn is struck by lightning.
It takes ({@damage 12d10}) Lightning damage and can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn. Greatwyrm Lightning Supremacy applies to this damage.

mythic.name: None Shall Fall (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm chooses up to five creatures within 300 feet that currently have 0 Hit Points.
Each immediately regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum, can stand without spending movement, and gains 50 Temporary Hit Points.

trait.name: Argent Aegis
entries: Silver dragons are born with an instinctive resistance to hostile magic that goes beyond ordinary draconic durability.
Their scales carry a quiet force that catches, diffuses, and turns aside supernatural pressure before it reaches the body beneath.
As a silver dragon matures, that instinct develops into one of the strongest natural magical defenses among true dragons.
{@b Wyrmling — Argent Ward.}
The dragon has Advantage on Saving Throws against cantrips and spells of 1st level.
{@b Young — Spellward Scales.}
The dragon has Advantage on Saving Throws against all spells and other magical effects.
Spellward Scales supersedes Argent Ward while the dragon is at the Young age category or older.
{@b Ancient — Unbroken Silver Aegis.}
Magic bends around the elder silver dragon rather than finding easy purchase.
Force that should imprison it fractures against its scales.
Attempts to banish, bind, or displace it meet a will reinforced by living arcane armor.
The dragon retains Magic Resistance and is Immune to Force damage.
It has Advantage on checks and Saving Throws made to resist forced teleportation, banishment, magical restraint, magical imprisonment, and forced planar movement.
When a magical effect would teleport or banish the dragon against its will, the dragon can use its Reaction to cause that effect to fail against it.
{@b Wyrm — Absolute Argent Aegis.}
Magic no longer merely struggles against the silver wyrm—it breaks upon it.
The invisible architecture of Force bends around its scales like wind around a mountain.
Those sheltered beneath its wings share in a defense that even archmages find difficult to penetrate.
The greatwyrm is Immune to Force damage, retains Magic Resistance, and has Resistance to all damage dealt by spells.
The greatwyrm can't be teleported, banished, or moved to another plane against its will.

Chosen creatures within 120 feet have Magic Resistance, Resistance to Force damage, and Advantage on checks and Saving Throws made to resist banishment, forced teleportation, magical restraint, magical imprisonment, and forced planar movement.
{@b Argent Refraction.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.

When a spell or magical effect the greatwyrm can see within 120 feet targets the greatwyrm or a creature protected by Absolute Argent Aegis, the greatwyrm can grant that target a +5 bonus to AC against the triggering effect or a +5 bonus to the triggering Saving Throw.

If that bonus causes the attack to miss or the Saving Throw to succeed, the greatwyrm can move the protected creature up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. This Force movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.
{@b Greatwyrm — Magic Breaks Before the Sky.}
The greatwyrm is Immune to Force damage and has Resistance to all damage dealt by spells.
It can't be teleported, banished, magically restrained, magically imprisoned, or moved to another plane against its will.
Chosen creatures within 300 feet have Magic Resistance, Resistance to Force damage, and Resistance to all damage dealt by spells.
Argent Refraction grants a +7 bonus instead of +5.
If that bonus causes a spell attack to miss or a Saving Throw against a spell to succeed, a spell of 8th level or lower has no further effect on the protected creature.

trait.name: Sanctuary of the Gentle Sky
entries: Silver dragons carry the safety of high mountains and quiet snowfall with them.
Their presence turns survival into recovery and fear into calm.
The oldest among them can make death itself wait outside the boundaries of their protection.
{@b Wyrmling — Warmth Beneath the Snow.}
Creatures chosen by the dragon within 30 feet are protected from natural extreme cold, have Advantage on Death Saving Throws, and automatically stabilize after succeeding on one Death Saving Throw.
{@b Young — Shelter in the Storm.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
The Temporary Hit Points last until depleted or replaced; condition removal is instantaneous.
The dragon chooses a creature within 60 feet. That creature gains Temporary Hit Points equal to twice the dragon's PB + its Charisma modifier.
The creature can immediately end either the Frightened or Charmed condition on itself.
{@b Adult — Merciful Intercession.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
When a creature within 120 feet would drop to 0 Hit Points, the dragon can cause it to drop to 1 Hit Point instead.
The dragon can then move that creature up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space the dragon can see.
The dragon can use this Reaction a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.
{@b Ancient — Sanctuary Cannot Be Broken.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.

The dragon creates a 120-foot aura. Chosen creatures in the aura have Advantage on Death Saving Throws, can't have their Hit Point maximum reduced, can't be prevented from regaining Hit Points, and can't be instantly killed while above 0 Hit Points.
{@b Wyrm — Death Waits Outside.}
While Sanctuary Cannot Be Broken is active, the first time each chosen creature would die during that duration, it doesn't die.
Instead, it returns to half its Hit Point maximum; ends Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, and Stunned on itself; and can immediately stand without spending movement.
Each creature can benefit from this effect only once per use of Sanctuary Cannot Be Broken.
{@b Greatwyrm — Death Has No Permission Here.}
While Sanctuary Cannot Be Broken is active, its radius becomes 300 feet.
A chosen creature in the aura can't be reduced below 1 Hit Point by damage while the greatwyrm is conscious and within the aura.
The creature can still be Incapacitated, transformed, banished, or affected by other effects normally unless another Greatwyrm feature prevents it.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 30 feet of the greatwyrm must make a DC 31 Dexterity Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 10d6 + 12}) Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't fall Prone.
The greatwyrm can then fly up to half its Fly Speed.

legendary.name: Cataclysmic Movement (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm moves up to its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Each creature the greatwyrm passes within 25 feet of during this movement must succeed on a DC 31 Dexterity Saving Throw or fall Prone.

legendary.name: Cast Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm casts one spell of 8th level or lower that normally has a Casting Time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: Breath Surge (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm chooses one of its Breath Weapons and rolls one additional d6 to recharge that Breath Weapon. If the chosen Breath Weapon is already available, the greatwyrm can instead immediately use that Breath Weapon.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

mythicHeader: While The Gentle Sky Eternal is active, the greatwyrm can use the following Mythic Actions as additional Legendary Action options. They expend Legendary Actions from the greatwyrm's normal pool.

mythic.name: Shelter the Living (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: One chosen creature within 300 feet gains 60 Temporary Hit Points and can immediately move up to 60 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

mythic.name: Break the Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm chooses one spell of 8th level or lower producing an ongoing effect within 180 feet. That spell ends.

mythic.name: Death Waits (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm chooses up to three creatures within 300 feet that have 0 Hit Points.

Each immediately regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum, ends Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, and Stunned on itself, and can immediately stand without spending movement.

monster.name: Gold Greatwyrm

conditionImmune.note: from effects other than being reduced to 0 Hit Points

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (9/Day)
entries: If the greatwyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Magic Resistance
entries: The greatwyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.
Spell attack rolls against the greatwyrm are made with Disadvantage.

trait.name: Perfect Concentration
entries: The greatwyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.

trait.name: Draconic Magical Instinct
entries: The greatwyrm is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena.
This trait doesn't grant automatic or complete knowledge.

trait.name: Keen Senses
entries: The greatwyrm has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the greatwyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The greatwyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 39 or lower, or returns to its true form.

While transformed, it retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; Saving Throw and Skill proficiencies; languages; personality and memories; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.
It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The greatwyrm can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The greatwyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell heal|XPHB}, {@spell resurrection|XPHB}, {@spell true resurrection|XPHB}, {@spell holy aura|XPHB}, {@spell mass heal|XPHB}, {@spell meteor swarm|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}, {@spell foresight|XPHB}, and {@spell shapechange|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the greatwyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Innate Elemental Casting
entries: When the greatwyrm casts a spell whose primary damage type is Fire, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Dawn Supremacy
entries: The greatwyrm's Fire and Radiant damage ignore Resistance and Immunity to Fire and Radiant damage.
An effect that would absorb, redirect, convert, or turn that Fire or Radiant damage into healing can't do so. The damage is dealt normally instead.
Whenever the greatwyrm deals Fire damage, it can convert any portion of that damage to Radiant damage, and vice versa.
Effects that reduce damage without depending on its damage type function normally.

trait.name: Perfect High Magic Recovery
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic.
This can restore an expended use of a 9th-level spell.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 30.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: The First Dawn Eternal (1/Long Rest)
entries: When the greatwyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains all of its Hit Points; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges both of its Breath Weapons; regains all expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains all expended uses of Draconic High Magic; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.
For 1 hour, the greatwyrm radiates true sunlight in a 500-foot radius that moves with it.
Chosen allies in the sunlight have Resistance to all damage, can't be Charmed or Frightened, and can't have their Hit Point maximum reduced.
At the start of each chosen ally's turn, it regains 40 Hit Points.

At the start of each hostile creature's turn in the sunlight, the greatwyrm chooses Fire or Radiant. That creature takes ({@damage 8d10}) damage of the chosen type. Greatwyrm Dawn Supremacy applies to this damage.
At the start of each of the greatwyrm's turns, both of its Breath Weapons automatically recharge.
While The First Dawn Eternal is active, the greatwyrm can use its Mythic Actions.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Dragons don't learn magic as mortals do.
Their element, temperament, instincts, and accumulated experience shape which spells come naturally to them.
As a dragon grows older, more of that inherited magic becomes effortless.
The greatwyrm knows every spell presented in its Gold Dragon spell list through 9th-level magic, as shown in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Age turns practiced magic into instinct.
The greatwyrm can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The greatwyrm can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the greatwyrm's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack.

Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell command|XPHB}, {@spell scorching ray|XPHB}, {@spell zone of truth|XPHB}, {@spell fireball|XPHB}, {@spell revivify|XPHB}, {@spell greater restoration|XPHB}, {@spell heal|XPHB}, {@spell holy aura|XPHB}, {@spell sunburst|XPHB}.

trait.name: Crown of the First Dawn
entries: Gold dragons carry something older than rulership and brighter than ordinary flame.
Their presence makes courage easier, deception harder, and cruelty far more dangerous.
As a Gold Dragon matures, its authority ceases to feel political and begins to feel cosmic.
{@b Wyrmling — Dawnfire.}
Whenever the dragon deals Fire damage, it can choose for any portion of that damage to become Radiant damage instead.
Whenever it deals both Fire and Radiant damage to the same target during its turn, that target sheds Bright Light for 10 feet until the start of the dragon's next turn.
This doesn't automatically reveal an Invisible creature, but it visibly marks the space occupied by a target that was actually hit.
{@b Young — Radiant Authority.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon chooses one creature within 60 feet. That creature becomes Judged.

Once per turn, when the Judged creature damages another creature, willingly breaks a promise it made to the dragon during this duration, or attempts to harm a creature the dragon explicitly placed under its protection, the dragon can deal ({@damage 2d8}) + its Charisma modifier Radiant damage to the Judged creature without using an Action.
This isn't perfect lie detection; the dragon must actually know or observe the triggering conduct.
{@b Adult — Sovereign Presence.}
Chosen allies within 60 feet gain a bonus equal to the dragon's PB to Saving Throws against Charmed and Frightened, have Resistance to Radiant damage, and have Advantage on Death Saving Throws.
A hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura while Judged takes Radiant damage equal to the dragon's Charisma modifier + PB.
{@b Ancient — Judgment of the Sun.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
The dragon chooses one creature within 180 feet. The target must make a DC 25 Charisma Saving Throw.

On a failed save, the target is Condemned for 1 minute. While Condemned, it can't benefit from Fire or Radiant Resistance against the dragon; Fire or Radiant Immunity is treated as Resistance against the dragon; it can't become Invisible to the dragon; and whenever it damages another creature, it takes ({@damage 4d10}) Radiant damage.
The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
{@b Wyrm — Crown of the First Dawn.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The greatwyrm emits sunlight in a 300-foot radius.
Chosen allies in the sunlight have Resistance to all damage from spells, regain 20 Hit Points at the start of each of their turns, and can't be Charmed or Frightened.

Hostile creatures in the sunlight can't benefit from Fire or Radiant Resistance against the greatwyrm. Fire and Radiant Immunity are treated as Resistance against the greatwyrm, and hostile creatures have Disadvantage on Saving Throws against the greatwyrm's Fire or Radiant effects.
When the greatwyrm uses its Fire Breath, it can convert any portion of that damage to Radiant damage.
{@b Greatwyrm — Dawn Without End.}
When the greatwyrm activates Crown of the First Dawn, its radius becomes 500 feet.
Chosen allies in the sunlight have Resistance to all damage, regain 30 Hit Points at the start of each of their turns, and can't be Charmed or Frightened.
They also can't have their Hit Point maximum reduced.
Hostile creatures in the sunlight can't benefit from Fire or Radiant Resistance or Immunity against the greatwyrm.
They have Disadvantage on Saving Throws against the greatwyrm's Fire and Radiant effects.
Once per turn, when a Judged or Condemned creature damages one of the greatwyrm's chosen allies, that creature takes ({@damage 8d10}) Radiant damage.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the greatwyrm more than size.
Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of a creature that has outlived lesser empires.
At the start of its turn, the greatwyrm can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the greatwyrm's choice within 500 feet that can see or hear it must make a DC 32 Wisdom Saving Throw.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the greatwyrm for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that greatwyrm's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.
A creature that fails its initial Saving Throw also can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

spellcasting.name: Innate Draconic Spellcasting
headerEntries: The greatwyrm's spellcasting ability is Charisma.
Its spell save DC is 32, and it has +24 to hit with spell attacks.
It requires no Spellcasting Focus. It can perform Somatic components using its draconic body.
It doesn't require Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The greatwyrm makes six attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail.
The greatwyrm can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a Casting Time of 1 Action.
The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

entries: {@atk mw} +24 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d10 + 12}) Piercing damage plus ({@damage 10d8}) Fire damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} +24 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d6 + 12}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} +24 to hit, reach 40 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d8 + 12}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} +24 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d6 + 12}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Fire Breath {@recharge 3}
entries: The greatwyrm exhales dawnfire in a 240-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 32 Dexterity Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 44d6}) Fire or Radiant damage, chosen separately for each creature by the greatwyrm. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
Greatwyrm Dawn Supremacy applies to this damage.

action.name: Weakening Breath {@recharge 3}
entries: This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
The greatwyrm exhales weakening gas in a 180-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 32 Strength Saving Throw.

On a failed save, the creature has Disadvantage on Strength checks and Strength Saving Throws, its Strength-based weapon attacks deal half damage, its carrying, lifting, and pushing capacities are halved, and its Speed is halved.
The creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

trait.name: Young Mind, Ancient Blood
entries: The dragon is fully sapient but still a child. It can speak, reason, learn, negotiate, deceive, understand consequences, and make simple plans.
It lacks the experience, restraint, long-term judgment, and accumulated expertise of older dragons and isn't automatically a scholar, mastermind, or expert caster.

entries: Gem dragons are born with minds that reach beyond the limits of spoken language.
Thought travels from them as naturally as breath, carrying intent directly from one consciousness to another.
As the dragon matures, this inborn psionic presence becomes an increasingly important part of how it understands and influences the world.
The dragon can communicate telepathically with a creature it can see within 120 feet.
A contacted creature can understand the dragon if it knows at least one language, and it can reply telepathically while it remains within 120 feet of the dragon.

entries: The dragon can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Gem dragon magic grows from instinct, thought, temperament, and the strange resonance of their crystalline bodies.
Their spellcraft is psionic in expression even when it reproduces effects recognizable as conventional spells.
Age deepens that inheritance, turning increasingly complex magic into something the dragon can perform as naturally as movement or speech.
The dragon knows the listed Amethyst Dragon spells through 2nd-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait.

At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell Tenser's floating disk|PHB}.

trait.name: Authority of Mass
entries: Amethyst dragons don't see gravity as an immutable law.
Weight, momentum, and position are simply relationships that can be altered by sufficient will.
Even a young amethyst dragon instinctively experiments with making the world heavier or lighter than it should be.
{@b Wyrmling — Local Gravity.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon chooses one creature or unattended object within 60 feet. An unwilling creature must make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.

The dragon chooses Heavy or Light. While Heavy, the target's Speed is reduced by 10 feet, its jump distance is halved, and it has Advantage on checks and Saving Throws against being pushed or knocked Prone.
While Light, the target's Speed increases by 10 feet, its jump distance is doubled, its falling damage is halved, and it has Disadvantage on Saving Throws against being pushed.
The dragon can have only one target affected by Local Gravity at a time.

entries: Crystal dragon magic doesn't merely illuminate—it reinforces life and possibility.

When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Gem dragon magic grows from instinct, thought, temperament, and the strange resonance of their crystalline bodies.
Their spellcraft is psionic in expression even when it reproduces effects recognizable as conventional spells.
Age deepens that inheritance, turning increasingly complex magic into something the dragon can perform as naturally as movement or speech.
The dragon knows the listed Emerald Dragon spells through 2nd-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Age turns practiced magic into instinct.
The dragon can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell disguise self|XPHB}, {@spell silent image|XPHB}.

trait.name: The Hidden Thought
entries: Emerald dragons prefer to know more than they reveal.
Illusion is not merely concealment to them; it is a way to control which version of reality another mind receives.
Their earliest psionic instincts are already devoted to watching without being watched in return.
{@b Wyrmling — Observer Behind the Image.}
The dragon can Hide as a Bonus Action while Lightly Obscured, behind an illusion, within Dim Light, or possessing Half Cover or better.

It can determine the approximate Size, direction, movement, and number of creatures moving on the same connected surface.

entries: Gem dragons don't always cross distance by moving through it.
Their crystalline bodies can briefly become an extension of thought rather than matter.
With maturity, a destination seen by the mind can become a destination reached by the body.
The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
The dragon teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.
This isn't a spell and requires no components. The dragon can use Psychic Step without a usage limit.
Only the dragon and objects it is wearing or carrying teleport. A creature being carried by the dragon doesn't teleport with it.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: A young gem dragon has learned to translate thought into more than motion.
Its mind can impose a different physical pattern upon its body without surrendering the psionic identity beneath.
The adopted shape is a body, not a replacement for the dragon's memories, magic, or will.
The dragon can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the dragon ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The dragon magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 12 or lower, or returns to its true form.
The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

While transformed, the dragon retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics); Psionic Mind; Psychic Step; Draconic Magical Instinct; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The dragon can continue using its own psionic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the dragon chooses when it transforms.

trait.name: Authority of Mass
entries: Amethyst dragons don't see gravity as an immutable law.
Weight, momentum, and position are simply relationships that can be altered by sufficient will.
Even a young amethyst dragon instinctively experiments with making the world heavier or lighter than it should be.
{@b Wyrmling — Local Gravity.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon chooses one creature or unattended object within 60 feet. An unwilling creature must make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.

The dragon chooses Heavy or Light. While Heavy, the target's Speed is reduced by 10 feet, its jump distance is halved, and it has Advantage on checks and Saving Throws against being pushed or knocked Prone.
While Light, the target's Speed increases by 10 feet, its jump distance is doubled, its falling damage is halved, and it has Disadvantage on Saving Throws against being pushed.
The dragon can have only one target affected by Local Gravity at a time.
{@b Young — Gravitational Domain.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon chooses a point within 90 feet and creates a 30-foot-radius sphere centered there. It chooses Crushing Gravity or Liberating Gravity when the Domain is created.

{@b Crushing Gravity.} The area is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures, their jump distance is quartered, and a hostile flying creature that starts its turn in the Domain must make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, it descends up to 30 feet.

{@b Liberating Gravity.} Chosen creatures in the Domain gain 10 feet of Speed, have their jump distance tripled, take no falling damage, and have Advantage on Saving Throws against being Grappled or Restrained by effects caused by physical force.
As a Bonus Action, the dragon can move the center of the Domain up to 30 feet. The dragon can have only one Gravitational Domain at a time.

trait.name: Keen Senses
entries: The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Psionic Mind
entries: Gem dragons are born with minds that reach beyond the limits of spoken language.
Thought travels from them as naturally as breath, carrying intent directly from one consciousness to another.
As the dragon matures, this inborn psionic presence becomes an increasingly important part of how it understands and influences the world.
The dragon can communicate telepathically with a creature it can see within 120 feet.
A contacted creature can understand the dragon if it knows at least one language, and it can reply telepathically while it remains within 120 feet of the dragon.

trait.name: Psychic Step
entries: Gem dragons don't always cross distance by moving through it.
Their crystalline bodies can briefly become an extension of thought rather than matter.

The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
The dragon teleports up to 90 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.

Objects worn or carried by the dragon teleport with it normally.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: An adult gem dragon can impose a different physical pattern upon its body without surrendering the psionic identity beneath.
Its transformed body is a chosen vessel rather than a replacement for the mind, memories, or magic that define the dragon.
Even while wearing another shape, its thought remains unmistakably draconic.
The dragon can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the dragon ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The dragon magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 18 or lower, or returns to its true form.
The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

While transformed, the dragon retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics); Psionic Mind; Psychic Step; Draconic Magical Instinct; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The dragon can continue using its own psionic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the dragon chooses when it transforms.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The dragon can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Tunneler
entries: The dragon can burrow through solid rock at half its Burrow Speed and leaves a 5-foot-wide tunnel in its wake.

trait.name: Superior Thunder Affinity
entries: The dragon's Thunder damage ignores Thunder Resistance.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 6.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The dragon can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell control winds|XGE}, {@spell control weather|XPHB}, {@spell foresight|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the dragon from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Gem dragon magic grows from instinct, thought, temperament, and the strange resonance of their crystalline bodies.
Their spellcraft is psionic in expression even when it reproduces effects recognizable as conventional spells.
Age deepens that inheritance, turning increasingly complex magic into something the dragon can perform as naturally as movement or speech.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic

trait.name: Resonance of Strategy
entries: Sapphire dragons hear a battlefield differently from other creatures.
Every footstep, impact, vibration, and hollow space adds another piece to an invisible tactical map.
Before they understand formal warfare, they already understand where things are moving and where stone is empty.

While touching stone, earth, metal, or another continuous solid surface, the dragon gains Tremorsense 30 feet.
It can determine the approximate Size, direction, movement, and number of creatures moving on the same connected surface.
It can detect movement through up to 10 feet of nonmagical stone but doesn't gain sight through that stone.
{@b Young — Expanded Echo Map.}
The Tremorsense granted by Echo Map increases from 30 feet to 60 feet.
{@b Young — Tactical Resonance.}
The dragon can activate this feature as a Bonus Action; the protective movement uses a Reaction.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.

The dragon creates a 60-foot aura. It knows the location of every creature in the aura that touches a connected floor, wall, or ceiling, or that creates sound or vibration, provided the creature isn't completely isolated from vibration.
Chosen allies in the aura can't be Surprised, gain a bonus to Initiative equal to the dragon's PB, and Opportunity Attacks against them have Disadvantage.

When an ally in the aura is targeted by an attack, the dragon can use its Reaction to move that ally up to 10 feet by psionic vibration before the attack is resolved. If the movement carries the ally beyond the attack's legal reach or range, the attack misses.
{@b Adult — Expanded Echo Map.}
The Tremorsense granted by Echo Map increases to 90 feet.
{@b Adult — Battlefield Harmonics.}
The radius of Tactical Resonance increases from 60 feet to 90 feet.

A chosen ally that starts its turn in the aura can move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks, has Advantage on Saving Throws against being pushed, pulled, or knocked Prone, and can receive telepathic tactical instructions from the dragon without an Action.

The first time in each round that a hostile creature in the aura moves at least 10 feet, the dragon can use its Reaction to force that creature to make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the creature's movement immediately ends and its Speed becomes 0 until the end of the current turn.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size.
Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of an apex creature that has survived centuries.
Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage.
At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the dragon's choice within 120 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.

Once per turn when the dragon deals Radiant damage to at least one creature or restores Hit Points to another creature, it chooses itself or one creature within 30 feet.
That creature gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the dragon's PB + Intelligence modifier + Charisma modifier (18 Temporary Hit Points for this ancient dragon).
{@b Young — Shared Brilliance.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction.
The Temporary Hit Points persist until depleted or replaced.
When a creature the dragon can see within 60 feet takes damage or fails a Saving Throw, the dragon releases a radiant pulse and chooses Shielding Light or Guiding Light.
{@b Shielding Light.} Reduce the triggering damage by ({@damage 3d8}) + the dragon's Charisma modifier.
{@b Guiding Light.} The target rerolls the failed Saving Throw and must use the new result.
If Shielding Light reduces the triggering damage to 0, or if the reroll from Guiding Light succeeds, the target gains 12 Temporary Hit Points.
The dragon can use Shared Brilliance a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.
{@b Adult — Beacon of Renewal.}
The dragon can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon creates a 60-foot aura. A chosen creature that starts its turn in the aura while it has at least 1 Hit Point regains Hit Points equal to the dragon's PB + Charisma modifier.
Whenever a chosen creature in the aura regains Hit Points from another source, the amount restored increases by the dragon's PB.
The first time on each of its turns that a chosen creature gains Temporary Hit Points, it can end Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned on itself.
If a chosen creature is at its Hit Point maximum when it would regain Hit Points from Beacon of Renewal, it gains that amount as Temporary Hit Points instead.

When a chosen creature in Beacon of Renewal regains Hit Points and that healing would raise it above its Hit Point maximum, the excess healing becomes Temporary Hit Points instead, to a maximum of 5 × the dragon's PB (35 for this ancient dragon).

once per turn when a creature in the aura regains Hit Points from any source, the dragon can choose a second creature in the aura. The second creature regains Hit Points equal to half the healing the first creature actually received.
Healing created by Overflowing Life can't trigger Overflowing Life again.

When the dragon causes a creature to regain Hit Points with one of its spells or features, it can end Blinded, Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned on that creature.
A creature can benefit from Prismatic Purification only once per turn.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size.
Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of an apex creature that has survived centuries.
Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage.
At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the dragon's choice within 180 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.

spellcasting.name: Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics)
headerEntries: The dragon's spellcasting ability is Intelligence.
Its spell save DC is 22, and it has +14 to hit with spell attacks.
The dragon casts these spells psionically. It requires no Verbal or Somatic components and no Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed.
Material components that have a listed cost or are consumed are still required normally.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes four attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail.
The dragon can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Action.
The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} +15 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 6d10 + 8}) Piercing damage plus ({@damage 6d8}) Radiant damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} +15 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 6d6 + 8}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} +15 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 6d8 + 8}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} +15 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 6d6 + 8}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Scintillating Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: The Temporary Hit Points persist until depleted or replaced.
The dragon exhales scintillating radiance in a 120-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 23 Constitution Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 24d8}) Radiant damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
After resolving the Breath, the dragon chooses up to PB creatures within 120 feet. Each chosen creature gains 25 Temporary Hit Points.

legendaryHeader: The dragon can take 5 Legendary Actions, choosing from the options below. Only one Legendary Action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The dragon regains spent Legendary Actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Detect
entries: The dragon makes a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check.

legendary.name: Tail Attack
entries: The dragon makes one Tail attack.

legendary.name: Cast Cantrip
entries: The dragon casts one cantrip.

legendary.name: Psychic Step
entries: The dragon uses Psychic Step, but teleports no more than 60 feet and can't bring another creature with it.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 20 feet of the dragon must make a DC 23 Dexterity Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 6d6 + 8}) Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't fall Prone.
The dragon can then fly up to half its Fly Speed.

legendary.name: Psionic Displacement (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The dragon chooses one creature it can see within 60 feet. The target must make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the dragon moves the target up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.
This movement isn't teleportation.

legendary.name: Breath Surge (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The dragon rolls one additional d6 to recharge its Breath Weapon. If the Breath Weapon is already available, the dragon can instead immediately use it.

legendary.name: Cast Psionic Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The dragon casts one psionic spell of 5th level or lower that normally has a casting time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The dragon casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

monster.name: Ancient Topaz Dragon

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (5/Day)
entries: If the dragon fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Draconic Magical Instinct
entries: The dragon is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena.
This trait doesn't grant automatic or complete knowledge.

trait.name: Keen Senses
entries: The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Psionic Mind
entries: Gem dragons are born with minds that reach beyond the limits of spoken language.
Thought travels from them as naturally as breath, carrying intent directly from one consciousness to another.
As the dragon matures, this inborn psionic presence becomes an increasingly important part of how it understands and influences the world.
The dragon can communicate telepathically with a creature it can see within 120 feet.
A contacted creature can understand the dragon if it knows at least one language, and it can reply telepathically while it remains within 120 feet of the dragon.

trait.name: Psychic Step
entries: Distance has become increasingly optional to an elder gem dragon.
Its body follows thought with almost no delay, slipping between positions before ordinary movement can properly begin.
Those it chooses to carry can briefly become part of that same act of will.
The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
The dragon teleports up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.
When it teleports, the dragon can choose up to two willing creatures within 10 feet of it. Each chosen creature teleports with the dragon and appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of it.
This isn't a spell and requires no components. The dragon can use Psychic Step without a usage limit.
Objects worn or carried by the dragon teleport with it normally.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: An ancient gem dragon can impose a different physical pattern upon its body without surrendering the psionic identity beneath.
Its transformed body is a chosen vessel rather than a replacement for the mind, memories, or magic that define the dragon.
Even while wearing another shape, its thought remains unmistakably draconic.
The dragon can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the dragon ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The dragon magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 21 or lower, or returns to its true form.
The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

While transformed, the dragon retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics); Psionic Mind; Psychic Step; Draconic Magical Instinct; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The dragon can continue using its own psionic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the dragon chooses when it transforms.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The dragon can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Ancient Necrotic Supremacy
entries: The dragon's Necrotic damage ignores Necrotic Resistance.
When the dragon deals Necrotic damage to a creature with Necrotic Immunity, that Immunity is treated as Necrotic Resistance, and the dragon then ignores that Resistance.
As a result, the dragon's Necrotic damage affects creatures with Necrotic Resistance or Necrotic Immunity without reducing the damage.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 14.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The dragon can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell harm|XPHB}, {@spell finger of death|XPHB}, {@spell Abi-Dalzim's horrid wilting|XGE}, {@spell power word kill|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the dragon from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Gem dragon magic grows from instinct, thought, temperament, and the strange resonance of their crystalline bodies.
Their spellcraft is psionic in expression even when it reproduces effects recognizable as conventional spells.
Age deepens that inheritance, turning increasingly complex magic into something the dragon can perform as naturally as movement or speech.
The dragon knows the listed Topaz Dragon spells through 9th-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Age turns practiced magic into instinct.
The dragon can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack.

Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell create or destroy water|XPHB}, {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell ray of enfeeblement|XPHB}, {@spell wither and bloom|SCC}, {@spell bestow curse|XPHB}, {@spell blight|XPHB}, {@spell enervation|XGE}, {@spell harm|XPHB}.

trait.name: Law of Ending

Water evaporates, flesh weakens, stone erodes, and every living thing eventually reaches its conclusion.
Even a wyrmling can accelerate tiny fragments of that process through instinctive psionic entropy.
{@b Wyrmling — Drying Touch.}
Using Drying Touch on an environmental liquid requires an Action.
The environmental change is permanent, and the healing prevention lasts until the start of the dragon's next turn.
The dragon can touch nonmagical water or another ordinary liquid and instantly destroy up to 1 cubic foot of it through supernatural desiccation.
This can't directly desiccate liquid inside a living creature.
once per turn when the dragon deals Necrotic damage to a creature, that creature can't regain Hit Points until the start of the dragon's next turn.
{@b Young — Entropic Field.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon creates a 30-foot aura. A chosen hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura must make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, until the start of its next turn the creature can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet.
The dragon can also cause nonmagical unattended plants, food, wood, cloth, and other ordinary organic matter in the aura to dry, wilt, or become brittle at an accelerated rate.

The Maximum Hit Point reduction lasts 1 hour.

The radius of Entropic Field increases from 30 feet to 60 feet.

A chosen hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura and fails the Constitution Saving Throw can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, has its Speed reduced by 20 feet, and can't benefit from regeneration until the start of its next turn.
Healing that would restore Hit Points to that creature before the start of its next turn restores 0 Hit Points instead.
The first time on each of its turns that such a creature takes Necrotic damage from the dragon, it loses all Temporary Hit Points before that damage is applied.
{@b Collapse Toward the End.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction.

When a creature the dragon can see within Entropic Field uses healing, regains Hit Points, or attempts to remove a reduction to its Hit Point maximum, the dragon can force it to make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the triggering effect is still expended or used normally but has no effect on that creature.
The dragon can use Collapse Toward the End a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.

entries: Emerald dragons prefer to know more than they reveal.
Illusion is not merely concealment to them; it is a way to control which version of reality another mind receives.
Their earliest psionic instincts are already devoted to watching without being watched in return.
{@b Wyrmling — Observer Behind the Image.}
The dragon can Hide as a Bonus Action while Lightly Obscured, behind an illusion, within Dim Light, or possessing Half Cover or better.

{@b Young — False Presence.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon creates an illusory duplicate of itself in an unoccupied space it can see within 60 feet.
The duplicate has no Hit Points, can't pass through objects, and looks, sounds, and smells like the dragon. When the dragon uses a Bonus Action, it can move the duplicate up to 40 feet.
The dragon can use the duplicate as the apparent origin point of its telepathy, its Illusion spells, and spells that target a mind or perception but don't create a physical projectile.

The first time on each turn that a creature attacks the duplicate, the attack automatically misses and the attacker must make an Intelligence Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, that creature can't see the real dragon until the start of its next turn.
{@b Adult — Distributed Presence.}
The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
When the dragon uses False Presence, it can maintain a number of duplicates at once equal to its PB (6 for this adult dragon).
Each duplicate occupies its own position and can serve as an origin for the dragon's telepathy, Illusion spells, and mind- or perception-targeting spells as described by False Presence.
When the dragon uses a Bonus Action to move its duplicates, each duplicate can move up to 40 feet.

The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction.
When the dragon is targeted by an attack or fails a Saving Throw, it can swap positions with one of its duplicates within 120 feet. The chosen duplicate then disappears.

This is psionic displacement, not the casting of a teleportation spell.

On a failed save, the dragon chooses one of its duplicates to become the target instead. The duplicate disappears after the effect is resolved.
If the effect can't legally target the chosen duplicate, the effect fails against the dragon, but any Action, spell slot, charge, or other limited use spent on that effect is still expended.

entries: Gem dragon magic grows from instinct, thought, temperament, and the strange resonance of their crystalline bodies.

trait.name: Resonance of Strategy

Every footstep, impact, vibration, and hollow space adds another piece to an invisible tactical map.

While touching stone, earth, metal, or another continuous solid surface, the dragon gains Tremorsense 30 feet.

The Tremorsense granted by Echo Map increases from 30 feet to 60 feet.

The dragon can activate this feature as a Bonus Action; the protective movement uses a Reaction.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.

The dragon creates a 60-foot aura. It knows the location of every creature in the aura that touches a connected floor, wall, or ceiling, or that creates sound or vibration, provided the creature isn't completely isolated from vibration.

The Tremorsense granted by Echo Map increases to 90 feet.

The radius of Tactical Resonance increases from 60 feet to 90 feet.

A chosen ally that starts its turn in the aura can move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks, has Advantage on Saving Throws against being pushed, pulled, or knocked Prone, and can receive telepathic tactical instructions from the dragon without an Action.

The Tremorsense granted by Echo Map increases to 150 feet.

The dragon can freely reassign the rolled Initiative results among those chosen creatures. This doesn't change the numerical Initiative results; it changes which chosen creature uses each result.

The dragon can use this feature as a Reaction.

When a chosen ally in Tactical Resonance ends its turn, the dragon can choose a different chosen ally in the aura. That creature can immediately move up to half its Speed, make one weapon attack, or take the Dodge action.
The dragon can use Resonant Command a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.

The radius of Tactical Resonance increases from 90 feet to 150 feet.

The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action.

The dragon chooses a point within 90 feet and creates a 30-foot-radius sphere centered there. It chooses Crushing Gravity or Liberating Gravity when the Domain is created.

When a creature or object the dragon can see within 120 feet moves at least 10 feet, falls, flies, is pushed or pulled, or is thrown, the dragon can alter that movement's vector.
