entries: The dragon makes a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check.

legendary.name: Tail Attack
entries: The dragon makes one Tail attack.

legendary.name: Cast Cantrip
entries: The dragon casts one cantrip.

legendary.name: Psychic Step
entries: The dragon uses Psychic Step, but teleports no more than 60 feet and can't bring another creature with it.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 20 feet of the dragon must make a DC 25 Dexterity Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 6d6 + 9}) Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't fall Prone.
The dragon can then fly up to half its Fly Speed.

legendary.name: Psionic Displacement (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The dragon chooses one creature it can see within 60 feet. The target must make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the dragon moves the target up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.
This movement isn't teleportation.

legendary.name: Breath Surge (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The dragon rolls one additional d6 to recharge its Breath Weapon. If the Breath Weapon is already available, the dragon can instead immediately use it.

legendary.name: Cast Psionic Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The dragon casts one psionic spell of 5th level or lower that normally has a casting time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The dragon casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

monster.name: Crystal Wyrm

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (7/Day)
entries: If the wyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Wyrm Magic Resistance
entries: Ancient psionic power has hardened the wyrm's mind and body against hostile magic.
Spells must overcome not only draconic resilience but an intellect that instinctively pushes back against supernatural intrusion.
At this age, magical resistance is no longer a practiced defense; it is part of the creature's existence.
The wyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Perfect Concentration
entries: A gem wyrm can hold a psionic construct in mind with terrifying stability.
Pain, impact, and violent motion no longer break the continuity of a thought it has chosen to maintain.
Its concentration fails only when something more fundamental than injury forces it to end.
The wyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.

trait.name: Draconic Magical Instinct
entries: The dragon is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena.
This trait doesn't grant automatic or complete knowledge.

trait.name: Keen Senses
entries: The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Psionic Mind
entries: Gem dragons are born with minds that reach beyond the limits of spoken language.
Thought travels from them as naturally as breath, carrying intent directly from one consciousness to another.
As the dragon matures, this inborn psionic presence becomes an increasingly important part of how it understands and influences the world.
The dragon can communicate telepathically with a creature it can see within 120 feet.
A contacted creature can understand the dragon if it knows at least one language, and it can reply telepathically while it remains within 120 feet of the dragon.

trait.name: Psychic Step
entries: Distance is no longer a route to a gem wyrm.
Position is simply another state its mind can choose.
Those close enough to enter that thought can cross space with it.
The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
The wyrm teleports up to 180 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.
When it teleports, it can choose up to four willing creatures within 20 feet. Each chosen creature teleports with it and appears in an unoccupied space within 20 feet of the wyrm.
This isn't a spell and requires no components. The wyrm can use Psychic Step without a usage limit, including while Grappled or Restrained.
Objects worn or carried by the wyrm teleport with it normally.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: A gem wyrm can impose an entirely different physical pattern upon its body without diminishing the mind beneath.
Its chosen shape is merely another arrangement of matter directed by the same ancient consciousness.
No borrowed body can replace the psionic identity that defines the wyrm.
The wyrm can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the wyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The wyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 26 or lower, or returns to its true form.
The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

While transformed, the wyrm retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics); Psionic Mind; Psychic Step; Draconic Magical Instinct; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The wyrm can continue using its own psionic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the wyrm chooses when it transforms.

trait.name: Wyrm Radiant Supremacy
entries: The wyrm's mastery of radiant power has exceeded the ordinary defensive categories used by lesser creatures.
Resistance no longer represents meaningful protection, and even immunity can be forced into a state the dragon can overcome.
Its signature energy behaves as an extension of psionic authority rather than an ordinary source of damage.
The wyrm's Radiant damage ignores Radiant Resistance.
When the wyrm deals Radiant damage to a creature with Radiant Immunity, that Immunity is treated as Radiant Resistance, and the wyrm then ignores that Resistance.
As a result, the wyrm's Radiant damage affects creatures with Radiant Resistance or Radiant Immunity without reducing the damage.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the wyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 24.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The wyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell greater restoration|XPHB}, {@spell heal|XPHB}, {@spell resurrection|XPHB}, {@spell mass heal|XPHB}, {@spell true resurrection|XPHB}, {@spell holy aura|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the wyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: World-Heart Reignition (1/Long Rest)
entries: The death of a wyrm is not always a single event.
Its ancient body and psionic identity can violently reassert themselves when destruction should have become final.
For a brief second phase of existence, the creature returns with its greatest powers burning again.
When the wyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Breath Weapon; regains 3 expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic, including a 9th-level spell; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Gem dragon magic grows from instinct, thought, temperament, and the strange resonance of their crystalline bodies.
Their spellcraft is psionic in expression even when it reproduces effects recognizable as conventional spells.
At wyrm age, inherited magic and deliberate mastery have become nearly indistinguishable.
The wyrm knows the listed Crystal Dragon spells through 9th-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Wyrm age turns practiced psionics into instinct.
The wyrm can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The wyrm can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the wyrm's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack.

Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell sanctuary|XPHB}, {@spell guiding bolt|XPHB}, {@spell lesser restoration|XPHB}, {@spell revivify|XPHB}, {@spell death ward|XPHB}, {@spell greater restoration|XPHB}, {@spell heal|XPHB}, {@spell mass cure wounds|XPHB}, {@spell holy aura|XPHB}.

trait.name: Light That Wants to Live
entries: Crystal dragon magic doesn't merely illuminate—it reinforces life and possibility.
Radiance passing through their crystalline bodies seems reluctant to disappear without leaving something useful behind.
Even a wyrmling instinctively turns excess magical light into protection for itself or another.
{@b Wyrmling — Reflected Vitality.}
The Temporary Hit Points persist until depleted or replaced.
Once per turn when the dragon deals Radiant damage to at least one creature or restores Hit Points to another creature, it chooses itself or one creature within 30 feet.
That creature gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the dragon's PB + Intelligence modifier + Charisma modifier (18 Temporary Hit Points for this ancient dragon).
{@b Young — Shared Brilliance.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
The Temporary Hit Points persist until depleted or replaced.
When a creature the dragon can see within 60 feet takes damage or fails a Saving Throw, the dragon releases a radiant pulse and chooses Shielding Light or Guiding Light.
{@b Shielding Light.} Reduce the triggering damage by ({@damage 3d8}) + the dragon's Charisma modifier.
{@b Guiding Light.} The target rerolls the failed Saving Throw and must use the new result.
If Shielding Light reduces the triggering damage to 0, or if the reroll from Guiding Light succeeds, the target gains 12 Temporary Hit Points.
The dragon can use Shared Brilliance a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.
{@b Adult — Beacon of Renewal.}
The wyrm can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon creates a 60-foot aura. A chosen creature that starts its turn in the aura while it has at least 1 Hit Point regains Hit Points equal to the dragon's PB + Charisma modifier.
Whenever a chosen creature in the aura regains Hit Points from another source, the amount restored increases by the dragon's PB.
The first time on each of its turns that a chosen creature gains Temporary Hit Points, it can end Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned on itself.
If a chosen creature is at its Hit Point maximum when it would regain Hit Points from Beacon of Renewal, it gains that amount as Temporary Hit Points instead.
{@b Ancient — Overflowing Life.}

When a chosen creature in Beacon of Renewal regains Hit Points and that healing would raise it above its Hit Point maximum, the excess healing becomes Temporary Hit Points instead, to a maximum of 5 × the dragon's PB (35 for this ancient dragon).

once per turn when a creature in the aura regains Hit Points from any source, the dragon can choose a second creature in the aura. The second creature regains Hit Points equal to half the healing the first creature actually received.
Healing created by Overflowing Life can't trigger Overflowing Life again.
{@b Prismatic Purification.}
When the dragon causes a creature to regain Hit Points with one of its spells or features, it can end Blinded, Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned on that creature.
A creature can benefit from Prismatic Purification only once per turn.
{@b Wyrm — Life Beyond the Limit.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The wyrm creates a 300-foot Life Nexus.

Chosen creatures in the Nexus regain 20 Hit Points at the start of each of their turns, increase all healing they receive by the wyrm's PB, can't have their Hit Point maximum reduced, can't be prevented from regaining Hit Points, and can't have their regeneration suppressed.

{@b Overflowing Vitality.} When a chosen creature at its Hit Point maximum would regain Hit Points, all of that healing becomes Temporary Hit Points instead. Temporary Hit Points granted by Life Beyond the Limit can stack with themselves, to a maximum of 5 × the wyrm's CR (130 for this Crystal Wyrm).

{@b Life Echo.} Once per turn when a chosen creature receives healing, the wyrm can choose up to PB other chosen creatures in the Nexus. Each selected creature regains Hit Points equal to half the amount of healing the first creature actually received. Healing from Life Echo can't trigger Life Echo again.

{@b Refuse Deterioration.} Chosen creatures in the Nexus are immune to reductions to their Hit Point maximum, magical aging, magical decay of the body, and effects that prevent them from regaining Hit Points.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size.
Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of an apex creature that has survived centuries.
Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage.
At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the dragon's choice within 300 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.
a creature that fails its initial Saving Throw can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
This additional effect occurs only on the initial failed save.

spellcasting.name: Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics)
headerEntries: The wyrm's spellcasting ability is Intelligence.
Its spell save DC is 24, and it has +16 to hit with spell attacks.
The wyrm casts these spells psionically. It requires no Verbal or Somatic components and no Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed.
Material components that have a listed cost or are consumed are still required normally.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wyrm makes five attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail.
The wyrm can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Action.
The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} +18 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d10 + 10}) Piercing damage plus ({@damage 8d8}) Radiant damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d6 + 10}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} +18 to hit, reach 35 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d8 + 10}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} +18 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d6 + 10}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Scintillating Breath {@recharge 4}
entries: The Temporary Hit Points persist until depleted or replaced.
The wyrm exhales scintillating radiance in a 180-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 26 Constitution Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 32d8}) Radiant damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
After resolving the Breath, the wyrm chooses up to PB creatures within 180 feet. Each chosen creature gains 40 Temporary Hit Points.

trait.name: Law of Ending
entries: Topaz dragons perceive decay less as tragedy and more as a universal rule.
Water evaporates, flesh weakens, stone erodes, and every living thing eventually reaches its conclusion.
Even a wyrmling can accelerate tiny fragments of that process through instinctive psionic entropy.
{@b Wyrmling — Drying Touch.}
Using Drying Touch on an environmental liquid requires an Action.
The environmental change is permanent, and the healing prevention lasts until the start of the dragon's next turn.
The dragon can touch nonmagical water or another ordinary liquid and instantly destroy up to 1 cubic foot of it through supernatural desiccation.
This can't directly desiccate liquid inside a living creature.

{@b Young — Entropic Field.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon creates a 30-foot aura. A chosen hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura must make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, until the start of its next turn the creature can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet.
The dragon can also cause nonmagical unattended plants, food, wood, cloth, and other ordinary organic matter in the aura to dry, wilt, or become brittle at an accelerated rate.
Entropic Field doesn't automatically deal damage to creatures.
{@b Adult — Accelerated Ending.}
The Maximum Hit Point reduction lasts 1 hour.
Once per turn when the dragon deals Necrotic damage to a creature in its Entropic Field, the target must make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the target's Hit Point maximum is reduced by half the Necrotic damage it took from the triggering damage, to a maximum reduction of 5 × the dragon's PB (25 for this adult dragon).
Multiple reductions from Accelerated Ending don't stack; only the highest reduction applies.
This isn't a disease or curse. {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} or other magic that removes reductions to a creature's Hit Point maximum can end the reduction normally.
{@b Ancient — Entropy Becomes Law.}
The radius of Entropic Field increases from 30 feet to 60 feet.

A chosen hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura and fails the Constitution Saving Throw can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, has its Speed reduced by 20 feet, and can't benefit from regeneration until the start of its next turn.
Healing that would restore Hit Points to that creature before the start of its next turn restores 0 Hit Points instead.
The first time on each of its turns that such a creature takes Necrotic damage from the dragon, it loses all Temporary Hit Points before that damage is applied.
{@b Collapse Toward the End.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.

When a creature the dragon can see within Entropic Field uses healing, regains Hit Points, or attempts to remove a reduction to its Hit Point maximum, the dragon can force it to make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the triggering effect is still expended or used normally but has no effect on that creature.
The dragon can use Collapse Toward the End a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.
{@b Wyrm — Everything Reaches Its End.}
The wyrm can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The wyrm creates a 300-foot Entropic Dominion.

Hostile creatures in the Dominion can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, and can't benefit from regeneration. Healing effects that target them still expend their resources but restore 0 Hit Points.

The first time on each turn that a creature in the Dominion takes Necrotic damage from the wyrm, its Hit Point maximum is reduced by half the Necrotic damage it took, to a maximum reduction of 10 × the wyrm's PB on that turn (80 for this Topaz Wyrm).
This Hit Point maximum reduction lasts until the creature finishes a Long Rest or it is removed by appropriate magic.

{@b Nothing Returns Unchanged.} If a creature in the Dominion is returned from the dead by a spell or effect, it returns normally, but for 1 hour its Hit Point maximum is halved, its Speed is halved, and it has Disadvantage on all Saving Throws.
{@b Final Collapse.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.

When a creature in the Dominion with fewer than 25 percent of its Hit Point maximum would regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points, the wyrm can cause that effect to fail against the creature. The triggering resource is still expended.
The wyrm can use Final Collapse a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.

entries: Ancient psionic power has hardened the wyrm's mind and body against hostile magic.

entries: The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Psionic Mind
entries: Gem dragons are born with minds that reach beyond the limits of spoken language.

trait.name: Psychic Step

trait.name: Wyrm Psychic Supremacy
entries: The wyrm's mastery of psychic power has exceeded the ordinary defensive categories used by lesser creatures.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the wyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 24.

trait.name: The Hidden Thought
entries: Emerald dragons prefer to know more than they reveal.

Their earliest psionic instincts are already devoted to watching without being watched in return.
{@b Wyrmling — Observer Behind the Image.}
The dragon can Hide as a Bonus Action while Lightly Obscured, behind an illusion, within Dim Light, or possessing Half Cover or better.
when it communicates telepathically, the recipient can't determine the direction or physical location from which the telepathic voice originates unless the dragon allows it.
{@b Young — False Presence.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon creates an illusory duplicate of itself in an unoccupied space it can see within 60 feet.
The duplicate has no Hit Points, can't pass through objects, and looks, sounds, and smells like the dragon. When the dragon uses a Bonus Action, it can move the duplicate up to 40 feet.
The dragon can use the duplicate as the apparent origin point of its telepathy, its Illusion spells, and spells that target a mind or perception but don't create a physical projectile.

The first time on each turn that a creature attacks the duplicate, the attack automatically misses and the attacker must make an Intelligence Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, that creature can't see the real dragon until the start of its next turn.

The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.

When the dragon uses a Bonus Action to move its duplicates, each duplicate can move up to 40 feet.

The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.

This is psionic displacement, not the casting of a teleportation spell.

The dragon can maintain a number of False Presence duplicates at once equal to PB + 3 (10 for this ancient dragon).

On a failed save, the dragon chooses one of its duplicates to become the target instead. The duplicate disappears after the effect is resolved.
If the effect can't legally target the chosen duplicate, the effect fails against the dragon, but any Action, spell slot, charge, or other limited use spent on that effect is still expended.

A creature can't determine the dragon's precise location solely through telepathy, divination that detects thoughts, or magical detection of consciousness unless the dragon allows it.
Such effects can reveal that a mind or consciousness is present in the relevant area but don't reveal the dragon's exact location by themselves.

The wyrm can maintain up to 20 False Presence duplicates at once. Each duplicate can speak, carry the wyrm's telepathy, serve as a spell origin as allowed by the previous stages of this feature, and move independently when the wyrm directs its duplicates.

Once per turn, the wyrm can use Distributed Self.
The wyrm swaps positions with one duplicate within 300 feet. The duplicate isn't destroyed by this swap.

On a failed save, the wyrm chooses a duplicate to receive the effect instead. If the effect can't legally affect the duplicate, the effect fails and its resource is still expended.

The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.

The wyrm creates a 300-foot psychic field. Hostile creatures in the field can't determine the wyrm's precise location through telepathy or divination alone and have Disadvantage on checks made to distinguish its illusions.

The wyrm can communicate telepathically with every creature in the field simultaneously and can cast an Enchantment spell, Illusion spell, or spell that deals Psychic damage from the position of any duplicate in the field.

{@b Wyrmling — Echo Map.}
While touching stone, earth, metal, or another continuous solid surface, the dragon gains Tremorsense 30 feet.
It can determine the approximate Size, direction, movement, and number of creatures moving on the same connected surface.
It can detect movement through up to 10 feet of nonmagical stone but doesn't gain sight through that stone.
{@b Young — Expanded Echo Map.}
The Tremorsense granted by Echo Map increases from 30 feet to 60 feet.
{@b Young — Tactical Resonance.}
The wyrm can activate this feature as a Bonus Action; the protective movement uses a Reaction.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.

The dragon creates a 60-foot aura. It knows the location of every creature in the aura that touches a connected floor, wall, or ceiling, or that creates sound or vibration, provided the creature isn't completely isolated from vibration.
Chosen allies in the aura can't be Surprised, gain a bonus to Initiative equal to the dragon's PB, and Opportunity Attacks against them have Disadvantage.

When an ally in the aura is targeted by an attack, the dragon can use its Reaction to move that ally up to 10 feet by psionic vibration before the attack is resolved. If the movement carries the ally beyond the attack's legal reach or range, the attack misses.
{@b Adult — Expanded Echo Map.}
The Tremorsense granted by Echo Map increases to 90 feet.
{@b Adult — Battlefield Harmonics.}
The radius of Tactical Resonance increases from 60 feet to 90 feet.

A chosen ally that starts its turn in the aura can move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks, has Advantage on Saving Throws against being pushed, pulled, or knocked Prone, and can receive telepathic tactical instructions from the dragon without an Action.

The first time in each round that a hostile creature in the aura moves at least 10 feet, the dragon can use its Reaction to force that creature to make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the creature's movement immediately ends and its Speed becomes 0 until the end of the current turn.
{@b Ancient — Expanded Echo Map.}
The Tremorsense granted by Echo Map increases to 150 feet.
{@b Ancient — Command the Initiative.}
This effect lasts until combat ends.
After Initiative is rolled but before the first turn begins, the dragon chooses up to PB willing creatures within Tactical Resonance.
The dragon can freely reassign the rolled Initiative results among those chosen creatures. This doesn't change the numerical Initiative results; it changes which chosen creature uses each result.
{@b Resonant Command.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.

When a chosen ally in Tactical Resonance ends its turn, the dragon can choose a different chosen ally in the aura. That creature can immediately move up to half its Speed, make one weapon attack, or take the Dodge action.
The dragon can use Resonant Command a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.
{@b Ancient Battlefield Harmonics.}
The radius of Tactical Resonance increases from 90 feet to 150 feet.
{@b Wyrm — Battle Is Already Solved.}
This effect lasts until combat ends.

After Initiative is rolled but before the first turn begins, the wyrm can freely reassign the rolled Initiative results among all chosen allies within Tactical Resonance. There is no PB limit on the number of chosen allies for this feature.
{@b Perfect Command Network.}
This effect lasts while Tactical Resonance is active.
The radius of Tactical Resonance increases to 300 feet.

Chosen allies in the aura can't be Surprised, gain a bonus to Initiative equal to the wyrm's PB, impose Disadvantage on Opportunity Attacks made against them, have Advantage on Saving Throws against forced movement, and can communicate telepathically with the wyrm and with one another.
{@b Command Chain.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.

When a chosen ally ends its turn, the wyrm chooses another chosen ally. That creature can immediately move up to half its Speed, make one weapon attack, cast one cantrip, take the Dodge action, or take the Disengage action.
Command Chain has no usage limit, but each creature can benefit from it only once per round.
{@b Predictive Countermeasure.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.

When a hostile creature in Tactical Resonance moves, casts a spell, makes an attack, or teleports, the wyrm chooses one chosen ally. That ally can immediately move up to 20 feet before the triggering action is resolved.
If this movement leaves the triggering action without a legal target or places the ally outside its legal reach or range, that action can't continue against that ally.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size.
Its voice, gaze, posture, and supernatural presence carry the instinctive certainty of an apex creature that has survived centuries.
Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage.
At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the dragon's choice within 300 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.
a creature that fails its initial Saving Throw can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
This additional effect occurs only on the initial failed save.

spellcasting.name: Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics)
headerEntries: The wyrm's spellcasting ability is Intelligence.
Its spell save DC is 25, and it has +17 to hit with spell attacks.
The wyrm casts these spells psionically. It requires no Verbal or Somatic components and no Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed.
Material components that have a listed cost or are consumed are still required normally.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wyrm makes five attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail.
The wyrm can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Action.
The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} +18 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d10 + 10}) Piercing damage plus ({@damage 8d8}) Thunder damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d6 + 10}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} +18 to hit, reach 35 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d8 + 10}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} +18 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 8d6 + 10}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Debilitating Breath {@recharge 4}
entries: This effect lasts until the end of the target's next turn.
The wyrm exhales high-frequency resonant force in a 180-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 27 Constitution Saving Throw.

On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 32d10}) Thunder damage, is Incapacitated until the end of its next turn, has Speed 0, can't take Reactions or Bonus Actions, immediately loses Concentration, and can't teleport until the end of its next turn.
On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effect.

legendaryHeader: The wyrm can take 7 Legendary Actions, choosing from the options below. Only one Legendary Action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The wyrm regains spent Legendary Actions at the start of its turn.

entries: The wyrm makes a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check.

legendary.name: Tail Attack
entries: The wyrm makes one Tail attack.

legendary.name: Cast Cantrip
entries: The wyrm casts one cantrip.

legendary.name: Psychic Step
entries: The wyrm uses Psychic Step, but teleports no more than 90 feet and can't bring another creature with it.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 25 feet of the wyrm must make a DC 27 Dexterity Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 8d6 + 10}) Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't fall Prone.
The wyrm can then fly up to half its Fly Speed.

legendary.name: Psionic Displacement (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The wyrm chooses one creature it can see within 120 feet. The target must make a Strength Saving Throw against the wyrm's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the wyrm moves the target up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.
This movement isn't teleportation.

legendary.name: Thought Before Motion (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The wyrm moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, or it uses a special 60-foot version of Psychic Step that can't bring another creature with it.

legendary.name: Breath Surge (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The wyrm rolls one additional d6 to recharge its Breath Weapon. If the Breath Weapon is already available, the wyrm can instead immediately use it.

legendary.name: Cast Psionic Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The wyrm casts one psionic spell of 7th level or lower that normally has a casting time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The wyrm casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

monster.name: Amethyst Wyrm

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (7/Day)
entries: If the wyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Wyrm Magic Resistance
entries: Ancient psionic power has hardened the wyrm's mind and body against hostile magic.
Spells must overcome not only draconic resilience but an intellect that instinctively pushes back against supernatural intrusion.
At this age, magical resistance is no longer a practiced defense; it is part of the creature's existence.
The wyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Perfect Concentration
entries: A gem wyrm can hold a psionic construct in mind with terrifying stability.
Pain, impact, and violent motion no longer break the continuity of a thought it has chosen to maintain.
Its concentration fails only when something more fundamental than injury forces it to end.
The wyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.

trait.name: Draconic Magical Instinct
entries: The dragon is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena.
This trait doesn't grant automatic or complete knowledge.

trait.name: Keen Senses
entries: The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Psionic Mind
entries: Gem dragons are born with minds that reach beyond the limits of spoken language.
Thought travels from them as naturally as breath, carrying intent directly from one consciousness to another.
As the dragon matures, this inborn psionic presence becomes an increasingly important part of how it understands and influences the world.
The dragon can communicate telepathically with a creature it can see within 120 feet.
A contacted creature can understand the dragon if it knows at least one language, and it can reply telepathically while it remains within 120 feet of the dragon.

trait.name: Psychic Step
entries: Distance is no longer a route to a gem wyrm.
Position is simply another state its mind can choose.
Those close enough to enter that thought can cross space with it.
The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
The wyrm teleports up to 180 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.
When it teleports, it can choose up to four willing creatures within 20 feet. Each chosen creature teleports with it and appears in an unoccupied space within 20 feet of the wyrm.
This isn't a spell and requires no components. The wyrm can use Psychic Step without a usage limit, including while Grappled or Restrained.
Objects worn or carried by the wyrm teleport with it normally.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: A gem wyrm can impose an entirely different physical pattern upon its body without diminishing the mind beneath.
Its chosen shape is merely another arrangement of matter directed by the same ancient consciousness.
No borrowed body can replace the psionic identity that defines the wyrm.
The wyrm can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the wyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The wyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 29 or lower, or returns to its true form.
The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

While transformed, the wyrm retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics); Psionic Mind; Psychic Step; Draconic Magical Instinct; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The wyrm can continue using its own psionic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the wyrm chooses when it transforms.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The dragon can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Wyrm Force Supremacy
entries: The wyrm's mastery of force power has exceeded the ordinary defensive categories used by lesser creatures.
Resistance no longer represents meaningful protection, and even immunity can be forced into a state the dragon can overcome.
Its signature energy behaves as an extension of psionic authority rather than an ordinary source of damage.
The wyrm's Force damage ignores Force Resistance.
When the wyrm deals Force damage to a creature with Force Immunity, that Immunity is treated as Force Resistance, and the wyrm then ignores that Resistance.
As a result, the wyrm's Force damage affects creatures with Force Resistance or Force Immunity without reducing the damage.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the wyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 27.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The wyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell reverse gravity|XPHB}, {@spell forcecage|XPHB}, {@spell maze|XPHB}, {@spell antimagic field|XPHB}, {@spell time stop|XPHB}, {@spell shapechange|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the wyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: World-Heart Reignition (1/Long Rest)
entries: The death of a wyrm is not always a single event.
Its ancient body and psionic identity can violently reassert themselves when destruction should have become final.
For a brief second phase of existence, the creature returns with its greatest powers burning again.
When the wyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Breath Weapon; regains 3 expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic, including a 9th-level spell; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Gem dragon magic grows from instinct, thought, temperament, and the strange resonance of their crystalline bodies.
Their spellcraft is psionic in expression even when it reproduces effects recognizable as conventional spells.
At wyrm age, inherited magic and deliberate mastery have become nearly indistinguishable.
The wyrm knows the listed Amethyst Dragon spells through 9th-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Wyrm age turns practiced psionics into instinct.
The wyrm can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The wyrm can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the wyrm's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack.

Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell Tenser's floating disk|PHB}, {@spell levitate|XPHB}, {@spell vortex warp|SCC}, {@spell gravity sinkhole|EGW}, {@spell telekinesis|XPHB}, {@spell reverse gravity|XPHB}, {@spell forcecage|XPHB}, {@spell maze|XPHB}, {@spell time stop|XPHB}.

trait.name: Authority of Mass
entries: Amethyst dragons don't see gravity as an immutable law.
Weight, momentum, and position are simply relationships that can be altered by sufficient will.
Even a young amethyst dragon instinctively experiments with making the world heavier or lighter than it should be.
{@b Wyrmling — Local Gravity.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon chooses one creature or unattended object within 60 feet. An unwilling creature must make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.

The dragon chooses Heavy or Light. While Heavy, the target's Speed is reduced by 10 feet, its jump distance is halved, and it has Advantage on checks and Saving Throws against being pushed or knocked Prone.
While Light, the target's Speed increases by 10 feet, its jump distance is doubled, its falling damage is halved, and it has Disadvantage on Saving Throws against being pushed.
The dragon can have only one target affected by Local Gravity at a time.
{@b Young — Gravitational Domain.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon chooses a point within 90 feet and creates a 30-foot-radius sphere centered there. It chooses Crushing Gravity or Liberating Gravity when the Domain is created.

{@b Crushing Gravity.} The area is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures, their jump distance is quartered, and a hostile flying creature that starts its turn in the Domain must make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, it descends up to 30 feet.

{@b Liberating Gravity.} Chosen creatures in the Domain gain 10 feet of Speed, have their jump distance tripled, take no falling damage, and have Advantage on Saving Throws against being Grappled or Restrained by effects caused by physical force.
As a Bonus Action, the dragon can move the center of the Domain up to 30 feet. The dragon can have only one Gravitational Domain at a time.
{@b Adult — Absolute Vector.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
When a creature or object the dragon can see within 120 feet moves at least 10 feet, falls, flies, is pushed or pulled, or is thrown, the dragon can alter that movement's vector.
Choose one: Redirect the movement by up to 90 degrees; Magnify the movement by up to 30 feet; or Suppress the movement by up to 30 feet, to a minimum of 0 feet.
An unwilling creature can make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a success, its movement is unchanged.
Absolute Vector doesn't teleport a creature and can't force a creature or object through a solid object.
{@b Ancient — Event Horizon.}
The wyrm can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon chooses a point within 180 feet and creates a 60-foot-radius sphere centered there.
A hostile creature that starts its turn in the sphere must make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.

On a failed save, the creature is pulled up to 30 feet toward the center and its Speed is halved until the start of its next turn. If it is flying, its Fly Speed becomes 0 until the start of its next turn.
If the creature is within 15 feet of the center when it fails the save, its Speed instead becomes 0, it can't teleport, and it can't be pushed away from the center until the start of its next turn.

A creature that attempts to teleport into, out of, or through Event Horizon must make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC. On a failed save, the teleportation fails, but the resource used to attempt it isn't expended.

The dragon is unaffected by the negative effects of Event Horizon, can use Psychic Step into or out of it freely, and treats every point inside the sphere as visible for purposes of Psychic Step unless solid Total Cover blocks that point.
{@b Gravitational Collapse.}
While Event Horizon is active, the wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
Once per round, the dragon compresses Event Horizon. Creatures of its choice in the sphere make a Strength Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 6d10}) Force damage and is pulled up to 30 feet toward the center. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't pulled.
{@b Wyrm — Sovereign Singularity.}
The wyrm can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The wyrm chooses a point within 300 feet and creates a 120-foot-radius gravitational singularity centered there.

A hostile creature that starts its turn in the singularity must make a DC 27 Strength Saving Throw. On a failed save, it is pulled up to 60 feet toward the center, its Speed is halved, its Fly Speed becomes 0, and it can't teleport until the start of its next turn.

If the creature is within 30 feet of the center when it fails the save, its Speed instead becomes 0, it is Restrained, it can't teleport, and it can't be pushed or pulled away from the center. A creature Restrained this way repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the Restrained condition on itself on a success.

{@b Spatial Lock.} A creature attempting teleportation or planar travel into, out of, or through Sovereign Singularity must make a DC 27 Strength Saving Throw. On a failed save, the effect fails but the resource used to attempt it isn't expended.
{@b Curved Reality.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.

When a ranged attack or line-shaped spell passes through Sovereign Singularity, the wyrm can change the direction of that line or projectile by up to 90 degrees. Any new target, origin, or path must still be legal for the original effect.
{@b Collapse the Worldline.}
The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
Once per round, the wyrm compresses the singularity. Creatures of its choice in the area make a Strength Saving Throw against the wyrm's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 10d10}) Force damage and is pulled up to 60 feet toward the center. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't pulled.
If this pull carries a creature to the center of the singularity, that creature takes an additional ({@damage 4d10}) Force damage.

While transformed, the greatwyrm retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics); Psionic Mind; Psychic Step; Draconic Magical Instinct; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The greatwyrm can continue using its own psionic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the greatwyrm chooses when it transforms.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Radiant Supremacy
entries: The greatwyrm's Radiant damage ignores Resistance and Immunity to Radiant damage.
An effect that would absorb, redirect, convert, or turn the greatwyrm's Radiant damage into healing can't do so. The damage is dealt normally instead.
Effects that reduce damage without depending on its damage type function normally.

trait.name: Perfect High Magic Recovery
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic.
This can restore an expended use of a 9th-level spell.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 30.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The greatwyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell greater restoration|XPHB}, {@spell heal|XPHB}, {@spell resurrection|XPHB}, {@spell mass heal|XPHB}, {@spell true resurrection|XPHB}, {@spell holy aura|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}, {@spell power word heal|XPHB}, and {@spell shapechange|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the greatwyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: The Light That Refuses to Die (1/Long Rest)
entries: When the greatwyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains all of its Hit Points; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Breath Weapon; regains all expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains all expended uses of Draconic High Magic; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.
For 1 hour, a 500-foot Life Nexus surrounds the greatwyrm and moves with it.

Chosen creatures in the Nexus regain 40 Hit Points at the start of each of their turns, can't have their Hit Point maximum reduced, can't be prevented from regaining Hit Points, and can't have their regeneration suppressed.
The first time each chosen creature would be reduced to 0 Hit Points during this phase, it instead remains at 1 Hit Point and gains 80 Temporary Hit Points.
At the start of each of the greatwyrm's turns, its Scintillating Breath automatically recharges.
While The Light That Refuses to Die is active, the greatwyrm can use its Mythic Actions.

trait.name: Draconic Spell List
entries: Gem dragon magic grows from instinct, thought, temperament, and the strange resonance of their crystalline bodies.
Their spellcraft is psionic in expression even when it reproduces effects recognizable as conventional spells.
At Greatwyrm age, inherited psionics and deliberate mastery have become inseparable.
The greatwyrm knows the listed Crystal Dragon spells through 9th-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait.

trait.name: Draconic At-Will Magic
entries: Some magic becomes so deeply rooted in a dragon that expenditure is no longer meaningful.
Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Greatwyrm age deepens this instinct into effortless psionic expression.
The greatwyrm can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The greatwyrm can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the greatwyrm's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack.

Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell sanctuary|XPHB}, {@spell guiding bolt|XPHB}, {@spell lesser restoration|XPHB}, {@spell revivify|XPHB}, {@spell death ward|XPHB}, {@spell greater restoration|XPHB}, {@spell heal|XPHB}, {@spell mass cure wounds|XPHB}, {@spell holy aura|XPHB}.
At Greatwyrm age, the following spells also become At-Will Magic: {@spell resurrection|XPHB}, {@spell mass heal|XPHB}.

trait.name: Light That Wants to Live
entries: Crystal dragon magic doesn't merely illuminate—it reinforces life and possibility.
Radiance passing through their crystalline bodies seems reluctant to disappear without leaving something useful behind.
Even a greatwyrmling instinctively turns excess magical light into protection for itself or another.
{@b Wyrmling — Reflected Vitality.}
The Temporary Hit Points persist until depleted or replaced.
Once per turn when the dragon deals Radiant damage to at least one creature or restores Hit Points to another creature, it chooses itself or one creature within 30 feet.
That creature gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the dragon's PB + Intelligence modifier + Charisma modifier (18 Temporary Hit Points for this ancient dragon).
{@b Young — Shared Brilliance.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.
The Temporary Hit Points persist until depleted or replaced.
When a creature the dragon can see within 60 feet takes damage or fails a Saving Throw, the dragon releases a radiant pulse and chooses Shielding Light or Guiding Light.
{@b Shielding Light.} Reduce the triggering damage by ({@damage 3d8}) + the dragon's Charisma modifier.
{@b Guiding Light.} The target rerolls the failed Saving Throw and must use the new result.
If Shielding Light reduces the triggering damage to 0, or if the reroll from Guiding Light succeeds, the target gains 12 Temporary Hit Points.
The dragon can use Shared Brilliance a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.
{@b Adult — Beacon of Renewal.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon creates a 60-foot aura. A chosen creature that starts its turn in the aura while it has at least 1 Hit Point regains Hit Points equal to the dragon's PB + Charisma modifier.
Whenever a chosen creature in the aura regains Hit Points from another source, the amount restored increases by the dragon's PB.
The first time on each of its turns that a chosen creature gains Temporary Hit Points, it can end Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned on itself.
If a chosen creature is at its Hit Point maximum when it would regain Hit Points from Beacon of Renewal, it gains that amount as Temporary Hit Points instead.
{@b Ancient — Overflowing Life.}

When a chosen creature in Beacon of Renewal regains Hit Points and that healing would raise it above its Hit Point maximum, the excess healing becomes Temporary Hit Points instead, to a maximum of 5 × the dragon's PB (35 for this ancient dragon).

once per turn when a creature in the aura regains Hit Points from any source, the dragon can choose a second creature in the aura. The second creature regains Hit Points equal to half the healing the first creature actually received.
Healing created by Overflowing Life can't trigger Overflowing Life again.
{@b Prismatic Purification.}
When the dragon causes a creature to regain Hit Points with one of its spells or features, it can end Blinded, Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned on that creature.
A creature can benefit from Prismatic Purification only once per turn.
{@b Wyrm — Life Beyond the Limit.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The greatwyrm creates a 300-foot Life Nexus.

Chosen creatures in the Nexus regain 20 Hit Points at the start of each of their turns, increase all healing they receive by the greatwyrm's PB, can't have their Hit Point maximum reduced, can't be prevented from regaining Hit Points, and can't have their regeneration suppressed.

{@b Overflowing Vitality.} When a chosen creature at its Hit Point maximum would regain Hit Points, all of that healing becomes Temporary Hit Points instead. Temporary Hit Points granted by Life Beyond the Limit can stack with themselves, to a maximum of 5 × the greatwyrm's CR (130 for this Crystal Wyrm).

{@b Life Echo.} Once per turn when a chosen creature receives healing, the greatwyrm can choose up to PB other chosen creatures in the Nexus. Each selected creature regains Hit Points equal to half the amount of healing the first creature actually received. Healing from Life Echo can't trigger Life Echo again.

{@b Refuse Deterioration.} Chosen creatures in the Nexus are immune to reductions to their Hit Point maximum, magical aging, magical decay of the body, and effects that prevent them from regaining Hit Points.
{@b Greatwyrm — Life Has No Ceiling.}
The radius of Life Beyond the Limit becomes 500 feet.
Chosen creatures in the Life Nexus regain 30 Hit Points at the start of each of their turns.
Whenever healing would restore a chosen creature above its Hit Point maximum, the excess becomes Temporary Hit Points.
Temporary Hit Points created by this feature stack with themselves up to 10 × the greatwyrm's CR.

Once per turn when a chosen creature receives healing, the greatwyrm can cause up to its Proficiency Bonus other chosen creatures in the Nexus to regain Hit Points equal to the healing actually received by the first creature.
Healing produced by this effect can't trigger itself.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the greatwyrm more than size.
At the start of its turn, the greatwyrm can activate this feature.
This effect lasts for up to 1 minute.
Each creature of the greatwyrm's choice within 500 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the greatwyrm's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the greatwyrm for 1 minute.
The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that greatwyrm's Frightful Presence for 24 hours.
This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.
A creature that fails its initial Saving Throw can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

spellcasting.name: Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics)
headerEntries: The greatwyrm's spellcasting ability is Intelligence.
Its spell save DC is 28, and it has +20 to hit with spell attacks.
The greatwyrm casts these spells psionically. It requires no Verbal or Somatic components and no Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed.
Material components that have a listed cost or are consumed are still required normally.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The greatwyrm makes six attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail.
The greatwyrm can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a psionic spell that normally has a Casting Time of 1 Action.
The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} +21 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d10 + 11}) Piercing damage plus ({@damage 10d8}) Radiant damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} +21 to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d6 + 11}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} +21 to hit, reach 40 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d8 + 11}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} +21 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}({@damage 10d6 + 11}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Scintillating Breath {@recharge 3}
entries: The greatwyrm exhales scintillating radiance in a 240-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 29 Constitution Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 40d8}) Radiant damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
After resolving the Breath, the greatwyrm chooses up to a number of creatures equal to its Proficiency Bonus within 240 feet. Each chosen creature gains 60 Temporary Hit Points.
Greatwyrm Radiant Supremacy applies to this Radiant damage.

legendaryHeader: The greatwyrm can take 9 Legendary Actions, choosing from the options below. Only one Legendary Action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The greatwyrm regains spent Legendary Actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Detect
entries: The greatwyrm makes a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check.

legendary.name: Tail Attack
entries: The greatwyrm makes one Tail attack.

legendary.name: Cast Cantrip
entries: The greatwyrm casts one cantrip.

legendary.name: Psychic Step
entries: The greatwyrm uses Psychic Step, but teleports no more than 150 feet and can't bring another creature with it.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 30 feet of the greatwyrm must make a DC 29 Dexterity Saving Throw.
On a failed save, a creature takes ({@damage 10d6 + 11}) Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't fall Prone.
The greatwyrm can then fly up to half its Fly Speed.

legendary.name: Psionic Displacement (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm chooses one creature it can see within 120 feet. The target must make a Strength Saving Throw against the greatwyrm's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the greatwyrm moves the target up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.
This movement isn't teleportation.

legendary.name: Thought Before Motion (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, or it uses a special 100-foot version of Psychic Step that can't bring another creature with it.

legendary.name: Breath Surge (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm rolls one additional d6 to recharge its Breath Weapon. If the Breath Weapon is already available, the greatwyrm can instead immediately use it.

legendary.name: Cast Psionic Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm casts one psionic spell of 8th level or lower that normally has a Casting Time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

mythicHeader: While The Light That Refuses to Die is active, the greatwyrm can use the following Mythic Actions as additional Legendary Action options. They expend Legendary Actions from the greatwyrm's normal pool.

mythic.name: Overflow (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm chooses up to three creatures it can see within 300 feet. Each chosen creature regains 60 Hit Points. Any healing that would exceed a creature's Hit Point maximum becomes Temporary Hit Points instead.

mythic.name: Life Echo (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: One creature the greatwyrm can see within 300 feet regains 100 Hit Points. The greatwyrm then chooses up to a number of other creatures equal to its Proficiency Bonus within 300 feet. Each of those creatures regains 50 Hit Points.

mythic.name: Refuse the Ending (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The greatwyrm chooses up to three creatures within 300 feet that died since the end of the greatwyrm's previous turn.
Each chosen creature returns to life with Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum.

monster.name: Topaz Greatwyrm

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (9/Day)
entries: If the greatwyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Greatwyrm Magic Resistance
entries: The greatwyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.
Spell attack rolls against the greatwyrm are made with Disadvantage.

trait.name: Perfect Concentration
entries: A gem wyrm can hold a psionic construct in mind with terrifying stability.
Pain, impact, and violent motion no longer break the continuity of a thought it has chosen to maintain.
Its concentration fails only when something more fundamental than injury forces it to end.
The greatwyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.

trait.name: Draconic Magical Instinct
entries: The dragon is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena.
This trait doesn't grant automatic or complete knowledge.

trait.name: Keen Senses
entries: The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.

trait.name: Psionic Mind
entries: Gem dragons are born with minds that reach beyond the limits of spoken language.
Thought travels from them as naturally as breath, carrying intent directly from one consciousness to another.
As the dragon matures, this inborn psionic presence becomes an increasingly important part of how it understands and influences the world.
The dragon can communicate telepathically with a creature it can see within 120 feet.
A contacted creature can understand the dragon if it knows at least one language, and it can reply telepathically while it remains within 120 feet of the dragon.

trait.name: Psychic Step
entries: Distance has become little more than a decision to a Gem Greatwyrm.
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
It teleports up to 300 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.

When it teleports, it can choose up to a number of willing creatures equal to its Proficiency Bonus within 30 feet. Each chosen creature teleports with it and appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of the greatwyrm.
This isn't a spell and requires no components. The greatwyrm can use Psychic Step without a usage limit, including while Grappled or Restrained.
Objects worn or carried by the greatwyrm teleport with it normally.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: A Gem Greatwyrm can impose an entirely different physical pattern upon its body without diminishing the mind beneath.
The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action.
The transformation lasts until the greatwyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies.
The greatwyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 35 or lower, or returns to its true form.
The assumed form can be any Size the chosen creature normally possesses.

While transformed, the greatwyrm retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; personality and memories; alignment; Saving Throw proficiencies; Skill proficiencies; languages; Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics); Psionic Mind; Psychic Step; Draconic Magical Instinct; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body.

It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics, including Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, movement modes, natural weapons, physical senses, and other body-dependent traits and actions.
It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features.
The greatwyrm can continue using its own psionic spellcasting while transformed.
Equipment it is wearing or carrying can merge into the new form or remain usable, as the greatwyrm chooses when it transforms.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The dragon can breathe air and water.

entries: The greatwyrm's Necrotic damage ignores Resistance and Immunity to Necrotic damage.
An effect that would absorb, redirect, convert, or turn the greatwyrm's Necrotic damage into healing can't do so. The damage is dealt normally instead.
Effects that reduce damage without depending on its damage type function normally.

trait.name: Perfect High Magic Recovery
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic.
This can restore an expended use of a 9th-level spell.

trait.name: Arcane Reclamation
entries: At the end of a Short Rest, the greatwyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 30.
It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The greatwyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell harm|XPHB}, {@spell finger of death|XPHB}, {@spell Abi-Dalzim's horrid wilting|XGE}, {@spell power word kill|XPHB}, {@spell time stop|XPHB}, {@spell weird|XPHB}, {@spell wish|XPHB}, {@spell imprisonment|XPHB}, and {@spell shapechange|XPHB}.
Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the greatwyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot.
When cast through Draconic High Magic, the spell doesn't require Material components unless they have a listed cost or are consumed.

trait.name: The Final Silence (1/Long Rest)
entries: When the greatwyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious.

Instead, it regains all of its Hit Points; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Breath Weapon; regains all expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains all expended uses of Draconic High Magic; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.
For 1 hour, a 500-foot Entropic Dominion surrounds the greatwyrm and moves with it.
At the start of each hostile creature's turn in the Dominion, that creature takes ({@damage 8d10}) Necrotic damage. Greatwyrm Necrotic Supremacy applies to this damage.
A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points within the Dominion immediately has its Hit Point maximum reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn.
At the start of each of the greatwyrm's turns, its Desiccating Breath automatically recharges.
While The Final Silence is active, the greatwyrm can use its Mythic Actions.

The greatwyrm knows the listed Topaz Dragon spells through 9th-level magic, as presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait.

Such spells are closer to breathing, hunting, or moving a wing than deliberate acts of spellcasting.
Greatwyrm age deepens this instinct into effortless psionic expression.
The greatwyrm can cast each spell listed under At Will in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting (Psionics) trait without expending a spell slot and with no usage limit.
A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The greatwyrm can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable.
An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the greatwyrm's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack.

Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell create or destroy water|XPHB}, {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell ray of enfeeblement|XPHB}, {@spell wither and bloom|SCC}, {@spell bestow curse|XPHB}, {@spell blight|XPHB}, {@spell enervation|XGE}, {@spell harm|XPHB}, {@spell finger of death|XPHB}, {@spell Abi-Dalzim's horrid wilting|XGE}.
At Greatwyrm age, the following spells also become At-Will Magic: {@spell power word kill|XPHB}.

trait.name: Law of Ending
entries: Topaz dragons perceive decay less as tragedy and more as a universal rule.
Water evaporates, flesh weakens, stone erodes, and every living thing eventually reaches its conclusion.
Even a greatwyrmling can accelerate tiny fragments of that process through instinctive psionic entropy.
{@b Wyrmling — Drying Touch.}
Using Drying Touch on an environmental liquid requires an Action.
The environmental change is permanent, and the healing prevention lasts until the start of the dragon's next turn.
The dragon can touch nonmagical water or another ordinary liquid and instantly destroy up to 1 cubic foot of it through supernatural desiccation.
This can't directly desiccate liquid inside a living creature.
once per turn when the dragon deals Necrotic damage to a creature, that creature can't regain Hit Points until the start of the dragon's next turn.
{@b Young — Entropic Field.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The dragon creates a 30-foot aura. A chosen hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura must make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, until the start of its next turn the creature can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet.
The dragon can also cause nonmagical unattended plants, food, wood, cloth, and other ordinary organic matter in the aura to dry, wilt, or become brittle at an accelerated rate.
Entropic Field doesn't automatically deal damage to creatures.
{@b Adult — Accelerated Ending.}
The Maximum Hit Point reduction lasts 1 hour.
Once per turn when the dragon deals Necrotic damage to a creature in its Entropic Field, the target must make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the target's Hit Point maximum is reduced by half the Necrotic damage it took from the triggering damage, to a maximum reduction of 5 × the dragon's PB (25 for this adult dragon).
Multiple reductions from Accelerated Ending don't stack; only the highest reduction applies.
This isn't a disease or curse. {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} or other magic that removes reductions to a creature's Hit Point maximum can end the reduction normally.
{@b Ancient — Entropy Becomes Law.}
The radius of Entropic Field increases from 30 feet to 60 feet.

A chosen hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura and fails the Constitution Saving Throw can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, has its Speed reduced by 20 feet, and can't benefit from regeneration until the start of its next turn.
Healing that would restore Hit Points to that creature before the start of its next turn restores 0 Hit Points instead.
The first time on each of its turns that such a creature takes Necrotic damage from the dragon, it loses all Temporary Hit Points before that damage is applied.
{@b Collapse Toward the End.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.

When a creature the dragon can see within Entropic Field uses healing, regains Hit Points, or attempts to remove a reduction to its Hit Point maximum, the dragon can force it to make a Constitution Saving Throw against the dragon's Psionic Save DC.
On a failed save, the triggering effect is still expended or used normally but has no effect on that creature.
The dragon can use Collapse Toward the End a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.
{@b Wyrm — Everything Reaches Its End.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action.
This effect lasts for 1 minute.
The greatwyrm creates a 300-foot Entropic Dominion.

Hostile creatures in the Dominion can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, and can't benefit from regeneration. Healing effects that target them still expend their resources but restore 0 Hit Points.

The first time on each turn that a creature in the Dominion takes Necrotic damage from the greatwyrm, its Hit Point maximum is reduced by half the Necrotic damage it took, to a maximum reduction of 10 × the greatwyrm's PB on that turn (80 for this Topaz Wyrm).
This Hit Point maximum reduction lasts until the creature finishes a Long Rest or it is removed by appropriate magic.

{@b Nothing Returns Unchanged.} If a creature in the Dominion is returned from the dead by a spell or effect, it returns normally, but for 1 hour its Hit Point maximum is halved, its Speed is halved, and it has Disadvantage on all Saving Throws.
{@b Final Collapse.}
The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction.

When a creature in the Dominion with fewer than 25 percent of its Hit Point maximum would regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points, the greatwyrm can cause that effect to fail against the creature. The triggering resource is still expended.
The greatwyrm can use Final Collapse a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.
{@b Greatwyrm — The End Is Absolute.}
The radius of Entropic Dominion becomes 500 feet.
Hostile creatures in the Dominion can't regain Hit Points, gain Temporary Hit Points, or benefit from regeneration.
Whenever the greatwyrm deals Necrotic damage to one of those creatures, its Hit Point maximum is reduced by half the Necrotic damage taken.
A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points within the Dominion can't regain Hit Points until the start of the greatwyrm's next turn.
A dead creature within the Dominion can't be returned to life until it leaves the Dominion or the Dominion ends.
This doesn't destroy a soul or prevent resurrection permanently.

entries: Age has given the greatwyrm more than size.
